source.title: On locally analytic vectors of the completed cohomology of modular curves II
source.journal: Annals of Mathematics 203 (2026), no. 1, 121-281, doi:10.4007/annals.2026.203.1.3 (not obtained)
source.version: arXiv v1, 14 September 2022, 127 pages - the only arXiv version, and the text read; all locators are its numbering

summary: The sequel to the author's study of the locally analytic vectors of the completed cohomology of modular curves. Its theorem is a new proof, geometric and independent of the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, of a classicality result of Emerton: a two-dimensional absolutely irreducible p-adic representation of the Galois group of Q which appears in the completed cohomology of modular curves and is de Rham at p with Hodge-Tate weights 0 and k > 0 comes from a cuspidal eigenform of weight k+1. The method is to construct Fontaine's monodromy operator geometrically. On the perfectoid modular curve at infinite level, the push-forward of the structure sheaf along the Hodge-Tate period map has a subsheaf of locally analytic sections which, by Paper I, is annihilated by the horizontal nilpotent subalgebra and so decomposes by weight for the horizontal Cartan action. The paper builds two differential operators on those weight sheaves - one along the modular curve, extending the classical theta operator O_Fl-linearly, one along the flag variety, coming from Beilinson-Bernstein localisation - and shows that their composite, an intertwining operator, agrees up to a rational scalar with the Fontaine operator of the truncated de Rham period sheaf, so that Fontaine's criterion turns de Rhamness into the vanishing of a geometric operator. The kernel of that operator is then decomposed by Hecke eigenvalues, stratum by stratum over the Newton stratification of the flag variety: on the Drinfeld upper half plane the supersingular uniformization and the Lubin-Tate-Drinfeld duality, which exchanges the two differential operators, identify the sections with quaternionic automorphic forms, and on the rational points the rigid cohomology of Igusa curves appears. The eigenvalues that occur are those of classical eigenforms of weight k+1, which is classicality; and the same computation gives a geometric description of the locally analytic vectors of the multiplicity space - the Breuil-Strauch conjecture in the supercuspidal case, the Berger-Breuil-Emerton conjecture in the principal series case, and a uniform statement covering both as the H^1 of a two-term de Rham complex modulo its Hodge filtration - together with a finiteness theorem for the n-invariants of the analytic vectors. What the paper needs from outside is Paper I above all, Scholze and Scholze-Weinstein for the perfectoid towers and their duality, Diao-Lan-Liu-Zhu for the logarithmic de Rham period sheaf, Fontaine for the theory of almost de Rham representations, and Coleman, Katz-Mazur and Rapoport-Zink for the classical geometry of Igusa curves and the supersingular locus.
conventions: C is the completion of an algebraic closure of Q_p; the flag variety Fl of GL_2 is P^1 as an adic space over Spa(C,O_C), and Omega = Fl minus Fl(Q_p) is the Drinfeld upper half plane.

K^p is a fixed neat compact open of GL_2(A_f^p) inside a level-N subgroup with N >= 3 prime to p; X_{K^p} is the perfectoid modular curve at infinite level at p and pi_HT its Hodge-Tate period map. V = Q_p^2 is the standard representation, normalised so that the local system attached to V is the first relative p-adic etale cohomology of the universal elliptic curve, so the universal Tate module is V(1) = V^*.

O_{K^p} is the push-forward of the structure sheaf along pi_HT; superscripts la, sm and lalg denote the subsheaves of GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic, smooth and locally algebraic sections, and a superscript D_p^*-sm the sections smooth for the units of the quaternion algebra. omega^k_{K^p} denotes the corresponding twists by the automorphic bundle.

theta_h is the horizontal Cartan action induced by h -> b_0/n_0; a weight chi = (n_1,n_2) is the character sending diag(a,d) to n_1 a + n_2 d, only integral weights occur, and O^{la,chi}_{K^p} is the chi-isotypic subsheaf. The element t is Fontaine's 2 pi i, and .t denotes the twist by it; -w.(-chi) = (n_2+1, n_1-1) is the dot action of the Weyl element.

d_{k+1} is the operator along the modular curve, d-bar_{k+1} the one along the flag variety, d'_{k+1} and d-bar'_{k+1} their twists, I_k = d-bar'_{k+1} after d_{k+1} = d'_{k+1} after d-bar_{k+1} the intertwining operator, and I^1_k = H^1(I_k). On the Lubin-Tate and Drinfeld sides the same operators are written with subscripts LT and Dr.

M_k(K^p) and M-dagger_k(K^p) are the classical and overconvergent modular forms of weight k and tame level K^p at infinite level at p; A_{D,-chi} is the space of quaternionic forms, A^1 the part factoring through the reduced norm and A^c the complement.

chi~_k is the infinitesimal character of the (k-1)-st symmetric power of the dual standard representation; B^+_dR and its truncations B^+_{dR,k} = B^+_dR/(t^k) are the period rings, and OB^+_dR the structural (log) de Rham period sheaf. A B^+_dR/(t^k)-module is Hodge-Tate of weights 0, l when its reduction modulo t is, in the sense that the Sen operator acts semisimply with eigenvalues 0 and -l on its decompletion.

Locators are the paper's own labels and the page numbers of arXiv v1. References of the form [Pan22] are to Paper I, [Sch15], [SW13], [DLLZ18], [Fon04] and so on as in the paper's bibliography; the paper's numbering shares one counter between named statements and numbered paragraphs, so '5.3.7' may be either.

items.name: Completed cohomology of modular curves at infinite level at p
items.statement: Fix a neat open compact subgroup K^p of GL_2(A_f^p). The completed cohomology is the p-adically completed colimit of the first cohomology of the modular curves Y(K^p K_p) as K_p shrinks, written H~^1(K^p, Z_p). It is p-adically complete and carries a natural continuous action of GL_2(Q_p) x G_Q, where G_Q is the absolute Galois group of Q; the object of study is the finite-dimensional Galois representations occurring inside it.
items.note: Emerton’s completed cohomology, in the form used throughout the paper; the whole paper is about its GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic vectors.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.2: de Rham representations in completed cohomology come from eigenforms
items.statement: Let E be a finite extension of Q_p and rho : G_Q -> GL_2(E) a two-dimensional continuous absolutely irreducible representation. Suppose (1) rho appears in H~^1(K^p, E) := H~^1(K^p, Z_p) tensor E, that is Hom_{E[G_Q]}(rho, H~^1(K^p,E)) is non-zero, and (2) the restriction of rho to a decomposition group at p is de Rham with Hodge-Tate weights 0 and k for some integer k > 0. Then rho arises from a cuspidal eigenform of weight k+1.
items.note: A new geometric proof of a theorem of Emerton; the point is that it does not use the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p) at any stage.

items.name: History of Theorem 1.1.2 and its relation to Emerton’s method
items.statement: The result was first obtained by Emerton, at least in the generic cases, and used by him to attack the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture: he proved a local-global compatibility statement identifying Hom_{E[G_Q]}(rho, H~^1(K^p,E)) with the representation attached to rho restricted to G_{Q_p} under the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, up to multiplicities, and then invoked Colmez's result on the existence of locally algebraic vectors together with the relation between locally algebraic vectors in completed cohomology and the cohomology of local systems on modular curves. The method of this paper is geometric, uses the intertwining operator constructed here as its key input, does not need the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, and is expected to generalise beyond GL_2(Q_p).

items.name: Theorem 1.1.2 is a case of the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture
items.statement: Since rho appears in H~^1(K^p,E), its restriction to G_{Q_l} is unramified for all but finitely many l and its restriction to G_R is odd, so Theorem 1.1.2 is a special case of the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture. In Emerton's approach one first shows that any two-dimensional p-adic geometric absolutely irreducible odd Galois representation of G_Q appears in H~^1(K^p,E), under generic assumptions, and then invokes this result.

items.name: The Banach space representation Pi_rho attached to rho
items.statement: For rho as in Theorem 1.1.2, set Pi_rho := Hom_{E[G_Q]}(rho, H~^1(K^p, E)); it is an E-Banach space representation of GL_2(Q_p), and Pi_rho^{la} denotes its subspace of GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic vectors. The paper gives a geometric description of Pi_rho^{la}; the introduction states it for k = 1, that is when rho corresponds to an eigenform of weight 2, with Subsection 7.3 covering k >= 2. Fixing an embedding tau of E into C, the completion of an algebraic closure of Q_p, Theorem 1.1.2 attaches to rho an irreducible representation pi^infinity = tensor'_l pi_l of GL_2(A_f) over C, the finite part of an automorphic representation of GL_2(A).

items.name: The supercuspidal case: Drinfeld upper half plane and its coverings
items.statement: Suppose pi_p is supercuspidal. By the Jacquet-Langlands correspondence pi^infinity transfers to an irreducible representation pi'^infinity of (D tensor A_f)^*, where D is the quaternion algebra over Q ramified exactly at p and infinity, so that pi'_p is an irreducible representation of D_p^*. Let Omega := P^1 minus P^1(Q_p) be the Drinfeld upper half plane, an adic space over Spa(C, O_C) with its natural GL_2(Q_p)-action, and let M^{(0)}_{Dr,n} be the tower of coverings of Omega constructed by Drinfeld, with pi^{(0)}_{Dr,n} the projection to Omega.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.7: the locally analytic vectors in the supercuspidal case
items.statement: Suppose k = 1 and pi_p is supercuspidal. There is a natural embedding i_pi of pi_p into the O_{D_p}^*-invariants of the colimit over n of H^1(P^1, j_! pi^{(0)}_{Dr,n *} O_{M^{(0)}_{Dr,n}}) tensor pi'_p, coming from the position of the Hodge filtration of rho restricted to G_{Q_p}, and a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism identifying Pi_rho^{la} completed-tensor C with (pi^{infinity,p})^{K^p} tensor the quotient of that same colimit by the image of i_pi; here j_! is extension by zero and the cohomology is computed on the analytic site of P^1.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1.7, p. 4, proved as Theorem 7.3.2, with the GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant upgrade in Remark 7.3.3

items.name: Theorem 1.1.7 verifies the Breuil-Strauch conjecture in dual form
items.statement: The group H^1(P^1, j_! pi^{(0)}_{Dr,n *} O_{M^{(0)}_{Dr,n}}) is isomorphic to the compactly supported cohomology of the structure sheaf on M^{(0)}_{Dr,n}, so Theorem 1.1.7 essentially verifies a conjecture of Breuil-Strauch on Pi_rho^{la} in dual form; that conjecture was completely solved by Dospinescu-Le Bras. Again the method does not rely on any known result from the p-adic local Langlands correspondence.
items.locator: Remark 1.1.8, p. 4, with details in Remark 7.3.6

items.name: Igusa curves and the rigid cohomology H^1_rig(Ig(K^p))
items.statement: Suppose pi_p is a principal series. Let Gamma(p^n) = 1 + p^n Z_p inside GL_2(Z_p) and let X_{K^p Gamma(p^n)} be the compactification of the modular curve of that level. By Katz-Mazur, its base change to C has a natural integral model over O_C whose special fibre has irreducible components indexed by surjections (Z/p^n)^2 -> Z/p^n, meeting at supersingular points. Let X_{K^p Gamma(p^n), F_p-bar, c} be the open subset of non-supersingular points of those components whose index kills (1,0); it is an affine variety over F_p-bar, classically a union of Igusa curves of level n and tame level K^p. Set H^1_rig(Ig(K^p,n)) to be its C-coefficient rigid cohomology and H^1_rig(Ig(K^p)) the colimit over n. The upper-triangular Borel B of GL_2(Q_p) acts on it smoothly, hence locally analytically, and for a finite set S of primes with K_l maximal outside S the spherical Hecke algebra T^S acts; rho and tau determine a homomorphism lambda_tau : T^S -> C.
items.note: The normalisation of lambda_tau is fixed in Subsection 7.3.1 and the spherical Hecke algebra in Subsection 5.5.5.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.10: the locally analytic vectors in the principal series case
items.statement: Suppose k = 1 and pi_p is a principal series. There is a natural embedding i_pi of (pi^infinity)^{K^p} into the locally analytic induction from B to GL_2(Q_p) of the lambda_tau-isotypic part H^1_rig(Ig(K^p))[lambda_tau], coming from the position of the Hodge filtration of rho restricted to G_{Q_p}, and a natural GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism identifying Pi_rho^{la} completed-tensor C with the quotient of that induction by the image of i_pi.

items.name: Identification with D_cris and the Berger-Breuil-Emerton conjecture
items.statement: There is an isomorphism H^1_rig(Ig(K^p))[lambda_tau] = (pi^{infinity,p})^{K^p} tensor D_cris(rho restricted to G_{Q_p}), B-equivariant once the right-hand side is given the correct B-action through the congruence relation. Hence Pi_rho^{la} completed-tensor C is (pi^{infinity,p})^{K^p} tensor the induction of D_cris modulo pi_p, the embedding of pi_p coming from Fil^1 D_dR inside D_dR = D_cris. Such an isomorphism was previously known from Emerton's local-global compatibility together with the description of the locally analytic representation attached to rho under the p-adic local Langlands correspondence; it was conjectured by Berger-Breuil and Emerton and proved by Liu-Xie-Zhang and Colmez.
items.locator: Remark 1.1.11, p. 5, with details in Remark 7.3.9

items.name: The special case
items.statement: When pi_p is special the paper obtains a slightly weaker result.
items.locator: Remark 1.1.12, p. 5, with the statement in Remark 7.3.10

items.name: A uniform formulation: the de Rham complex DR_{k-1} and its Hodge filtration
items.statement: In both Theorems 1.1.7 and 1.1.10 the representation Pi_rho^{la} completed-tensor C appears as a quotient by (pi^infinity)^{K^p}, and this is not a coincidence: there is a natural isomorphism Pi_rho^{la} completed-tensor C = H^1(DR_{k-1})[lambda] modulo Fil^1 H^1(DR_{k-1})[lambda] for a two-term complex DR_{k-1} on P^1, where Fil is the Hodge filtration. For k = 1 the de Rham cohomology of the finite-level modular curve embeds into H^1(DR_0) and gives Fil^1 H^1(DR_0)[lambda] = Fil^1 colim_{K_p} H^1_dR(X_{K^p K_p})[lambda] = (pi^infinity)^{K^p}. So the Breuil-Strauch conjecture in the supercuspidal case and the Berger-Breuil-Emerton conjecture in the principal series case are two instances of one statement. The cohomology H^1(DR_{k-1})[lambda] itself does not see the Hodge filtration; informally DR_0 is a completed tensor product of the de Rham complex of the finite-level curve with the structure sheaf of P^1, in analogy with geometric constructions of representations of real groups as in Kashiwara-Schmid.
items.locator: Remark 1.1.13, p. 5, with Remark 5.5.15, Theorem 7.2.2 and Remark 5.5.16

items.name: Theorem 1.1.14: finite-dimensionality of the n-invariants
items.statement: Let rho be as in Theorem 1.1.2 and let n be the upper-triangular nilpotent subalgebra of Lie GL_2(Q_p). Then the space of n-invariants of the Gamma(p^m)-analytic vectors of Pi_rho is finite-dimensional for every m >= 2. The same result was obtained independently and by a completely different method by Dospinescu-Paskunas-Schraen.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1.14, p. 5, part (2) of Theorem 7.1.2, with Remark 7.1.3

items.name: Fontaine’s criterion and the Fontaine operator
items.statement: Let V be a two-dimensional continuous representation of G_{Q_p} over Q_p which is Hodge-Tate of weights 0 and k, so that V tensor C = W_0 + W_k with both summands non-zero and W_i(i) = (W_i(i))^{G_{Q_p}} tensor C. Fontaine's classification of almost B_dR-representations produces a natural C-linear G_{Q_p}-equivariant operator N : W_0 -> W_k(k) such that V is de Rham exactly when N = 0. The construction: with H_{Q_p} the kernel of the cyclotomic character and Gamma = G_{Q_p}/H_{Q_p} = Z_p^*, set D_pdR(V) to be the H_{Q_p}-invariants of V tensor B_dR on which Gamma acts unipotently; the t-adic filtration of B_dR filters it, and generalising Sen's decompletion Fontaine showed dim D_pdR(V) = dim V and gr^i D_pdR(V) tensor C = W_i(i), with W_i(i) = 0 for i not 0 or k. The action of 1 in Lie Gamma is nilpotent and filtration-preserving, and the induced map gr^0 -> gr^k tensored with C is N.
items.locator: Section 1.2.1, p. 6; quoted from Fontaine, Arithmetique des representations galoisiennes p-adiques
items.note: The Fontaine operator is the organising object of the whole paper: the main theorem is that it has a purely geometric description.

items.name: The Fontaine operator on completed cohomology
items.statement: Since completed cohomology is an admissible Banach space representation of GL_2(Q_p), Pi_rho is admissible and so Pi_rho^{la} is non-zero by Schneider-Teitelbaum. By [Pan22] it has an infinitesimal character chi~_k, that of the (k-1)-st symmetric power of the dual of the standard representation, and the chi~_k-isotypic part H~^1(K^p,Q_p)^{la,chi~_k} is Hodge-Tate of weights 0 and k, with a natural decomposition into W_0 and W_k satisfying W_i(i) = (W_i(i))^{G_{Q_p}} completed-tensor C. Fontaine's construction generalises: there is a natural continuous map N : W_0 -> W_k(k) whose restriction to (V tensor C)_0 agrees with the Fontaine operator of V for every two-dimensional irreducible G_Q-subrepresentation V of H~^1(K^p,Q_p)^{la,chi~_k}. Hence a spectral decomposition of ker N implies Theorem 1.1.2.
items.locator: Section 1.2.2, p. 6; the infinitesimal character is [Pan22, Proposition 6.1.5], see also Dospinescu-Paskunas-Schraen

items.name: Theorem 1.2.3: the spectral decomposition of the kernel of N
items.statement: There is a natural generalized eigenspace decomposition of ker N with respect to the action of the spherical Hecke algebra T^S: ker N is the direct sum over lambda of the generalized eigenspaces (ker N)~[lambda], where lambda : T^S -> C runs over all systems of eigenvalues associated to eigenforms of weight k+1 together with the eigenvalues appearing in the colimit over K_p of H^0(Y(K^p K_p)(C), Q_p).
items.locator: Theorem 1.2.3, p. 7, proved as Theorem 5.5.7 and Corollary 5.5.9

items.name: Eigenspaces versus generalized eigenspaces
items.statement: In fact (ker N)~[lambda] = (ker N)[lambda], the honest eigenspace, when the associated automorphic representation is cuspidal and not special at p; using results from the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p) the same holds in the Steinberg case.

items.name: The infinite-level modular curve, the Hodge-Tate period map and the sheaves O^{la,chi}
items.statement: Let X_{K^p} be the perfectoid modular curve of infinite level at p, the tilde-limit over K_p of the X_{K^p K_p}, introduced by Scholze, with its GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant Hodge-Tate period map pi_HT : X_{K^p} -> Fl = P^1, the flag variety of GL_2 as an adic space over Spa(C, O_C). Let O_{K^p} := pi_{HT*} O_{X_{K^p}} and O^{la}_{K^p} its subsheaf of GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic sections. By the relative Sen theory of [Pan22], O^{la}_{K^p} is annihilated by the horizontal nilpotent subalgebra n_o on Fl, so the horizontal Cartan h = diagonal matrices acts through h -> b_o/n_o; this action is theta_h, and for a weight chi = (n_1,n_2) the sheaf O^{la,chi}_{K^p} is the chi-isotypic part. Moreover [Pan22] gives natural isomorphisms W_0 = H^1(Fl, O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}) for k >= 2 and W_k = H^1(Fl, O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}); for k = 1 there is only a natural map H^1(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p}) -> W_0, whose failure to be an isomorphism comes from H~^0(K^p,Z_p), and W_0[lambda_tau] = H^1(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p})[lambda_tau] still holds.
items.locator: Section 1.2.5, p. 7; the perfectoid modular curve is Scholze’s and the sheaf-theoretic input is [Pan22, 4.2-4.3, 5.1]

items.name: The smooth sheaves and the two derivations
items.statement: Let O^{sm}_{K^p} be the subsheaf of GL_2(Q_p)-smooth sections of O_{K^p}, equivalently the colimit over K_p of pi_{HT*} pi_{K_p}^{-1} O_{X_{K^p K_p}}, and let Omega^{1,sm}_{K^p}(C) be the corresponding colimit of the sheaves of differentials with log poles at the cusps. It is an O^{sm}_{K^p}-module with a natural derivation d, and there are natural inclusions of O^{sm}_{K^p} and of O_{Fl} into O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p}.

items.name: Theorem 1.2.7: the two differential operators d_1 and d-bar_1
items.statement: The natural map O^{sm}_{K^p} tensor_C O_{Fl} -> O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} has dense image. Moreover (1) there is a unique continuous O_{Fl}-linear map d_1 from O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} to O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor_{O^{sm}} Omega^{1,sm}_{K^p}(C) extending d; and (2) there is a unique continuous O^{sm}_{K^p}-linear map d-bar_1 from O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} to O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor_{O_{Fl}} Omega^1_{Fl} extending the derivation of O_{Fl}.
items.note: The existence of these two operators - one along the modular curve, one along the flag variety - is the technical heart of the paper.

items.name: Why d-bar is anti-holomorphic
items.statement: The operator d-bar_1 is essentially the pull-back of derivations on Fl along the Hodge-Tate period map, which as explained by Scholze is a p-adic analogue of the anti-holomorphic Borel embedding; hence the notation.

items.name: The intertwining operators I_{k-1} and the Kodaira-Spencer identification
items.statement: Define I_0 as the composite of d_1 with d-bar_1 tensor 1, landing in Omega^1_{Fl} tensor O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor Omega^{1,sm}_{K^p}(C). The Kodaira-Spencer isomorphisms - Omega^1 of the finite-level curve with log poles at the cusps is the square of the automorphic line bundle, and Omega^1_{Fl} is the inverse square of the tautological bundle - together with the fact that the pull-backs of the two line bundles to X_{K^p} agree up to a Tate twist, identify that target with O^{la,(1,-1)}_{K^p}(1). So I_0 : O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} -> O^{la,(1,-1)}_{K^p}(1), and a standard BGG construction gives I_{k-1} = d-bar'_{k+1} composed with d_{k+1} from O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p} to O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}(k); write I^1_{k-1} for H^1(I_{k-1}).

items.name: Theorem 1.2.10: the intertwining operator is the Fontaine operator
items.statement: For k >= 2 the map I^1_{k-1} agrees with c_k N, and for k = 1 the restriction of I^1_0 to H^1(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p})[lambda_tau] agrees with c_1 N restricted to W_0[lambda_tau], for some non-zero scalar c_k in Q_p.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2.10, p. 8, the main result of Section 6
items.note: This is the innovation the paper advertises: a purely geometric construction of Fontaine’s operator out of two differential operators on the perfectoid modular curve.

items.name: Reduction to the de Rham complex DR_0 and the properties of d-bar_1
items.statement: It remains to give ker I^1_{k-1} a spectral decomposition, and this is done at the sheaf level. For k = 1 the two key properties of d-bar_1 are that it is surjective and that its kernel is exactly O^{sm}_{K^p}: informally, the complex O^{la,(0,0)} -> O^{la,(0,0)} tensor Omega^1_{Fl} is a relative de Rham complex of X_{K^p} over the finite-level curve whose fibres are profinite, hence zero-dimensional, which gives surjectivity, while the kernel is GL_2(Q_p)-invariant and by Beilinson-Bernstein localisation the derivation comes from the action of gl_2, which gives the second. Since H^1(d-bar'_1) is then injective, ker I^1_0 = ker H^1(d_1), and with DR_0 the two-term complex d_1 : O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} -> O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor Omega^{1,sm}_{K^p}(C) one gets ker I^1_0 = H^1(DR_0) modulo Fil^1 H^1(DR_0) - which is what Remark 1.1.13 describes.
items.locator: Sections 1.2.11 and the top of p. 9

items.name: The stratification of the flag variety and where the two cases come from
items.statement: It suffices to give H^*(DR_0) a spectral decomposition, and for y in Fl the stalk H^*(DR_0)_y computes the de Rham cohomology of the fibre pi_HT^{-1}(y); so one stratifies Fl = P^1 into Omega and P^1(Q_p). On Omega, the uniformisation of the supersingular locus by the Lubin-Tate space gives a spectral decomposition with eigenvalues corresponding to automorphic representations of the quaternion group, and since each fibre is a profinite set H^1(DR_0) vanishes there. On P^1(Q_p) the fibre is a perfect Igusa curve and one gets a decomposition with eigenvalues appearing in H^1_rig(Ig(K^p)). For a C-point y of Omega the fibre is the double coset space of D^*, and the key point is that any element of H^0(DR_0)_y = (ker d_1)_y is an automorphic function, that is D_p^*-smooth; this is proved by showing that the duality between the Lubin-Tate and Drinfeld towers at infinite level swaps the roles of d_1 and d-bar_1, so that it becomes the statement that ker d-bar_1 consists of GL_2(Q_p)-smooth elements. For y in P^1(Q_p) the point is that H^*(DR_0)_y computes the rigid cohomology of the classical, non-perfect Igusa curves.

items.name: Organisation of the paper
items.statement: Sections 2 and 3 are preliminary: Section 2 collects facts about locally analytic representations over a Hausdorff LB-space and Section 3 recalls and slightly generalises constructions of [Pan22]. Section 4 proves the existence of d_1 and d-bar_1 and studies the n-invariants of ker H^1(d_k). Section 5 proves the spectral decomposition and studies the local picture of the Lubin-Tate and Drinfeld towers. Section 6 proves that the Fontaine operator is H^1(d-bar'_k composed with d_k) up to a non-zero scalar, the main ingredient being the period sheaf OB^+_dR. Section 7 assembles the main results.

items.name: Four improvements to the previous paper
items.statement: The paper also improves results of [Pan22]: (1) the two notions LA-acyclic and strongly LA-acyclic introduced there are shown to be equivalent, in Proposition 2.3.6; (2) the differential equation satisfied by O^{la}_{K^p}, computed there using a result of Faltings, is explained conceptually in the proof of Theorem 5.2.6 through the relation between the Higgs bundle and the variation of Hodge structure attached to a de Rham local system, the equation being essentially given by the Kodaira-Spencer class, a point of view that works for general Shimura varieties; (3) the inclusion in the relative Hodge-Tate sequence is made Hecke-equivariant in Subsection 4.2.3, the correct sequence being 4.2.1, whereas previously a trivialisation of the H^2 of the relative de Rham cohomology was implicitly fixed; (4) the Cech complexes occurring in the proof of [Pan22, Theorem 5.1.11] are shown to be strict using the Weyl group, in Subsection 3.4.1, so that no largest separated quotient need be taken, and a Cartan-Serre type argument is carried out in this context.

items.name: An alternative construction of the differential operators
items.statement: After the work was finished, Juan Esteban Rodriguez Camargo explained a more direct and conceptual construction of d_1 and d-bar_1 using B^+_dR modulo t^2, which it would be interesting to use to simplify the arguments of Section 6.
items.note: A pointer a design job should follow: if the atlas builds this material, the B^+_dR/t^2 construction may be the better route.

items.name: Global conventions and notation
items.statement: For a topological space X, pi_0(X) is its set of connected components, and for a map f of sheaves of abelian groups H^i(f) denotes the induced map on cohomology. Fix an algebraic closure of Q with G_Q its Galois group; for each rational prime l fix an algebraic closure of Q_l, an embedding of Q-bar into it determining a decomposition group G_{Q_l}, and a lift Frob_l of geometric Frobenius, local class field theory being normalised to send a uniformiser to a lift of geometric Frobenius. The character epsilon from A_f^*/Q_{>0}^* to Z_p^* corresponds to the p-adic cyclotomic character under global class field theory, and is also written for its composite with the determinant on GL_2(A_f); epsilon_p is the p-adic cyclotomic character of G_{Q_p}.

items.name: Analytic functions on a p-adic Lie group and G_n-analytic vectors of a Banach representation
items.statement: Let G be a p-adic Lie group of dimension d and fix a compact open subgroup G_0 with an integer-valued saturated p-valuation; set G_n = G_0^{p^n}. Write C^an(G_n, Q_p) for the Q_p-valued analytic functions on G_n, with its left and right translation actions (the left one is the default). For a Q_p-Banach space representation W of G, C^an(G_n, W) is the space of W-valued analytic functions with the action (g.f)(h) = g(f(g^{-1}h)), and there is a natural G_n-equivariant isomorphism C^an(G_n, W) = C^an(G_n,Q_p) completed-tensor W. The subspace W^{G_n-an} of G_n-analytic vectors is the image of the G_n-invariants under evaluation at the identity; G_n acts continuously on it, identified with the right translation action. If W^{G_n-an} = W the action is called analytic, evaluation at 1 is then an isomorphism, and one gets C^an(G_n,Q_p) completed-tensor W = C^an(G_n,W) with the trivial action on W on the left, the map sending f to g -> g(f(g)). If W is a C-Banach representation then W^{G_n-an} is again a C-Banach space.
items.locator: Section 2.1.1, pp. 11-12; the constructions are recalled from [Pan22, section 2]

items.name: Hausdorff LB-spaces
items.statement: An LB-space is a locally convex topological Q_p-vector space isomorphic to a locally convex inductive limit of a countable inductive system of Q_p-Banach spaces; only Hausdorff LB-spaces are considered, and such a space can be written as the inductive limit of a sequence of Q_p-Banach spaces with injective transition maps.
items.locator: Section 2.1.2, p. 12; the reference is Emerton, Locally analytic vectors in representations of locally p-adic analytic groups

items.name: The locally analytic vectors of a Banach representation form a Hausdorff LB-space
items.statement: For a Q_p-Banach space representation W of G, the space W^{la} = colim_n W^{G_n-an} of G-locally analytic vectors is naturally a Hausdorff LB-space; it is Hausdorff because the inclusion of W^{la} into W is continuous, the inclusion of analytic into continuous functions on G_n being continuous.

items.name: Analytic functions with values in an LB-space, independently of the presentation
items.statement: Let V be the inductive limit of a sequence of Banach spaces V_i. Then C^an(G_n, V) is the colimit of the C^an(G_n, V_i) = C^an(G_n,Q_p) completed-tensor V_i, again a Hausdorff LB-space, and this does not depend on the chosen presentation: writing U_i for the kernel of V_i -> V and W_i = V_i/U_i, the Baire category theorem shows that for each i there is i' >= i with the image of U_i in V_{i'} zero, so that the colimit over the V_j agrees with the colimit over the W_j, and independence of the presentation by the W_i follows from Emerton's Proposition 1.1.10.

items.name: Proposition 2.1.5: a Banach subspace of an LB-space lands in one step
items.statement: Let V be a Hausdorff locally convex topological Q_p-vector space and suppose there are Q_p-Banach spaces V_n with injective continuous linear maps v_n : V_n -> V whose images exhaust V. Then for any Q_p-Banach space W and continuous linear map u : W -> V, the image of u lies in v_n(V_n) for some n. This is essentially Emerton's Proposition 1.1.10, which follows from Bourbaki by observing that the graph of u is closed in the product.
items.note: Used repeatedly, and it is the step that turns an LA-acyclicity statement into an essentially-zero statement in Proposition 2.3.6.

items.name: Locally analytic vectors of a representation on an LB-space
items.statement: Suppose the V_i form an inductive sequence of Banach space representations of G_0. Then G_n acts on C^an(G_n,V) by (g.f)(h) = g(f(g^{-1}h)), and V^{G_n-an} is defined as the image of the G_n-invariants under evaluation at the identity, with the subspace topology; equivalently it is the colimit of the V_i^{G_n-an} inside V. It is a Hausdorff LB-space, the V^{G_n-an} form an inductive sequence, and V^{la} is defined as their colimit, again a Hausdorff LB-space. This does not depend on the choice of G_0 among compact open subgroups carrying an integer-valued saturated p-valuation.

items.name: Compact operators between p-adic Banach spaces
items.statement: A linear operator f : X -> Y between Q_p-Banach spaces is compact if the closure of the image of the unit ball is compact, equivalently if the closure of the image of any bounded set is compact; the notion depends only on the topologies. A compact operator is continuous, and conversely a continuous f, which maps the unit ball into p^k times the unit ball of Y for some k, is compact exactly when the image of the unit ball in p^k Y^o / p^{k+n} Y^o is finite for every n >= 0. Compactness is preserved by composing with continuous operators on either side.
items.note: Stated over Q_p for simplicity; all of section 2.2 holds over a finite extension.

items.name: Standard compact operators in rigid geometry
items.statement: The inclusion of Tate algebras from the closed unit disc to the closed disc of radius |p| is compact. More generally, for a Q_p-Banach algebra B a continuous Q_p-algebra homomorphism from the Tate algebra in n variables to B is compact as soon as the images of the variables are topologically nilpotent; and the same holds for the Banach algebra Z_p<T_1,...,T_n>[[x]] tensor Q_p, with unit open ball Z_p<T_1,...,T_n>[[x]], when the images of the T_i and of x are topologically nilpotent.
items.note: The variant with the formal variable x is what the later application to the Lubin-Tate and Drinfeld towers actually needs.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.3: compact transition maps force Hausdorffness
items.statement: If the V_i form an inductive sequence of Q_p-Banach spaces with injective compact transition maps, then the locally convex inductive limit is Hausdorff.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.3, p. 14; quoted from Schneider, Nonarchimedean functional analysis, Lemma 16.9

items.name: Corollary 2.2.4: Hausdorffness survives a completed tensor product
items.statement: If the V_i form an inductive sequence of Q_p-Banach spaces with injective compact transition maps and W is a Q_p-Banach space, then the locally convex inductive limit of the V_i completed-tensor W is Hausdorff. The proof separates a non-zero vector by applying a functional on W and using Proposition 2.2.3.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.5: a Cartan-Serre criterion for compact transition maps
items.statement: Let V_i and W_i be inductive sequences of Q_p-Banach spaces with continuous transition maps and continuous linear maps f_i : V_i -> W_i such that (1) the f_i commute with the transition maps; (2) for each i there is j >= i with the image of W_i in W_j contained in f_j(V_j); and (3) for each i the composite of f_i with W_i -> W_j is compact for j large. Then for each i the transition map W_i -> W_j is compact for j large. The proof equips f_k(V_k) = V_k/ker f_k with the quotient topology, uses the closed graph theorem to make W_i -> f_k(V_k) continuous, and then factors.
items.note: This is the engine of Subsection 3.4: it is how the Cech complexes there are shown to have compact transition maps, hence Hausdorff colimits.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.2: closed embeddings pass to analytic vectors
items.statement: If V is a closed embedding of Q_p-Banach space representations of G into W, then V^{G_n-an} -> W^{G_n-an} for every n, and V^{la} -> W^{la}, are again closed embeddings; the point is that the completed tensor product with C^an(G_n,Q_p) preserves closed embeddings, and one then takes G_n-invariants.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.3: continuous cohomology vanishing survives a completed tensor product
items.statement: Let H be a profinite group, K a finite extension of Q_p and W a K-Banach space representation of H with vanishing continuous cohomology in all positive degrees. Then the continuous cohomology of W completed-tensor V also vanishes in positive degrees, for any K-Banach space V with trivial H-action. The proof observes that the continuous cochain complex is strict exact by the open mapping theorem and commutes with the completed tensor product.

items.name: Corollary 2.3.4: continuous functions are acyclic after a completed tensor product
items.statement: For H profinite and W a Q_p-Banach space representation of H, the continuous cohomology of C(H,Q_p) completed-tensor W vanishes in all positive degrees. One first replaces the action on W by the trivial one using the H-equivariant isomorphism sending f to g -> g(f(g)), and then applies Proposition 2.3.3 together with the acyclicity of C(H,Q_p) itself.
items.locator: Corollary 2.3.4 with its proof, p. 15; the acyclicity of C(H,Q_p) is from the proof of [Eme06b, Proposition 1.1.3]

items.name: The derived functors R^i LA, LA-acyclicity and strong LA-acyclicity
items.statement: For a Q_p-Banach space representation W of G and i >= 1 set R^i LA(W) := colim_n H^i_cont(G_n, W completed-tensor C^an(G_n,Q_p)) = colim_n H^i_cont(G_n, C^an(G_n,W)), which measures the failure of taking locally analytic vectors. W is LA-acyclic if all R^i LA(W) vanish, and strongly LA-acyclic if for each i the direct system of the H^i_cont(G_n, C^an(G_n,W)) is essentially zero, that is for each n there is m >= n with the transition map to level m zero. Neither notion depends on the choice of G_0, and strong LA-acyclicity implies LA-acyclicity.
items.locator: Section 2.3.5, pp. 15-16; the notions are from [Pan22, section 2.2]

items.name: Proposition 2.3.6: LA-acyclic implies strongly LA-acyclic
items.statement: A LA-acyclic Q_p-Banach space representation of G is strongly LA-acyclic. The proof embeds W as the constants in C(G_0,W), calls the quotient Q, and uses Corollary 2.3.4 to see that C(G_0,W) is acyclic, which gives H^{i+1}_cont(G_n, C^an(G_n,W)) = H^i_cont(G_n, C^an(G_n,Q)) for i >= 1 and a four-term exact sequence in degree one. LA-acyclicity makes colim_n Q_n -> Q^{la} an isomorphism, where Q_n is the Banach quotient of C(G_0,W)^{G_n-an} by W^{G_n-an}; since Q^{la} is a Hausdorff LB-space, Proposition 2.1.5 puts Q^{G_n-an} inside some Q_m, which is exactly the vanishing of the transition map in H^1. The general case follows by induction on i.
items.note: This settles one of the four improvements to [Pan22] listed in 1.3.2: the two notions introduced there coincide.

items.name: What section 2.3 is for
items.statement: The subsection collects simple results used later, and proves the equivalence of LA-acyclicity and strong LA-acyclicity from [Pan22, section 2.2].

items.name: The perfectoid modular curve, the Hodge-Tate period map and the automorphic bundles
items.statement: Let C be the completion of an algebraic closure of Q_p. For a neat open compact K of GL_2(A_f) let X_K be the complete modular curve over Q and X_K the adic space attached to its base change to C. Fix K^p inside the level-N subgroup for some N >= 3 prime to p. There is a unique perfectoid space X_{K^p} over C with X_{K^p} ~ lim_{K_p} X_{K^p K_p}; on non-cusp points it parametrises elliptic curves with level-K^p-structure away from p together with a trivialisation of the p-adic Tate module. With V = Q_p^2 the standard representation of GL_2(Q_p), the convention is that the local system attached to V is the first relative p-adic etale cohomology of the universal family, so the universal Tate module corresponds to V(1) = V^*. Writing omega_1 for the automorphic line bundle at finite level and omega_{K^p} for its pull-back, the relative Hodge-Tate filtration is the exact sequence 0 -> omega_{K^p}^{-1}(1) -> V(1) tensor O_{X_{K^p}} -> omega_{K^p} -> 0, equivalently its untwisted form; the position of omega_{K^p}^{-1} induces the GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant Hodge-Tate period map pi_HT : X_{K^p} -> Fl = P^1, and the pull-back along pi_HT of the tautological ample bundle omega_Fl is omega_{K^p}(-1).
items.locator: Section 3.1.1 with the displayed sequence (3.1.1), p. 17; quoted from [Sch15] and [Pan22, section 4]

items.name: The horizontal Cartan action theta_h
items.statement: Let O_{K^p} = pi_{HT*} O_{X_{K^p}} and let O^{la}_{K^p} be its subsheaf of GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic sections. With g = gl_2(C) the complexified Lie algebra there is a natural action of g_0 = O_Fl tensor g on O^{la}_{K^p}; writing b_0 and n_0 for the horizontal Borel and nilpotent subsheaves, n_0 acts trivially, so b_0/n_0 acts. The Cartan subalgebra h of diagonal matrices acts through h -> O_Fl tensor h = b_0/n_0; this horizontal action is written theta_h and encodes the infinitesimal character.
items.locator: Section 3.1.1, p. 17; quoted from [Pan22, Theorem 4.2.7 and Corollary 4.2.8]

items.name: Twists of O^{la} by the automorphic bundle, and the two ways of seeing them
items.statement: Fix an integer k. For an affinoid open U of Fl the bundle omega_Fl is trivial, and a choice of generator gives an isomorphism of O_{X_{K^p}}(pi_HT^{-1}U) with omega^k_{K^p}(pi_HT^{-1}U), hence a Banach space structure independent of the generator, so that locally analytic vectors are well defined; omega^{k,la}_{K^p} denotes the subsheaf of GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic sections of pi_{HT*}(omega_{K^p})^{tensor k}, with its horizontal Cartan action. There are two ways of viewing it as a twist of O^{la}_{K^p}: twisting on Fl, omega^{k,la}_{K^p}(-k) = O^{la}_{K^p} tensor_{O_Fl} omega_Fl^{tensor k}; and twisting on modular curves, omega^{k,la}_{K^p} = omega^{k,sm}_{K^p} tensor_{O^{sm}_{K^p}} O^{la}_{K^p}, where omega^{k,sm}_{K^p} is the subsheaf of GL_2(Q_p)-smooth sections, that is those annihilated by g, equivalently the push-forward of the colimit of the pull-backs of omega^k from finite level. The horizontal h-action on omega^{k,sm}_{K^p} is trivial and on omega_Fl is through the character sending diag(a,d) to d, and both isomorphisms are h-equivariant. The second isomorphism is proved in Lemma 3.2.8.

items.name: Integral weights, the sheaves O^{la,chi} and the invertible function t
items.statement: A weight chi of h is written chi(diag(a,d)) = n_1 a + n_2 d and identified with the pair (n_1,n_2); only integral weights are considered. O^{la,chi}_{K^p} is the chi-isotypic part of O^{la}_{K^p} for theta_h, and omega^{k,la,chi}_{K^p} is defined likewise. Taking the second exterior power of the Hodge-Tate sequence gives O_{X_{K^p}} = O_{X_{K^p}} tensor det(1); fixing a basis b of Q_p(1), the element 1 tensor b defines an invertible function t on X_{K^p} on which G_{Q_p} acts through the cyclotomic character, and GL_2(A_f) acts through a non-trivial character because the second exterior power of the universal bundle is implicitly trivialised. The notation .t denotes the twist by t. Fixing the standard basis of V, its images e_1, e_2 in H^0(X_{K^p}, omega_{K^p}) are sections of omega_Fl and x := e_2/e_1 is a rational function on Fl.
items.locator: Sections 3.2.1 and the discussion on p. 19; the corresponding object in [Pan22, 4.3.1] was written differently because t is reserved for Fontaine’s 2 pi i here
items.note: The renaming is deliberate: 4.2.3 later removes the implicit trivialisation and makes the Hodge-Tate sequence Hecke-equivariant.

items.name: The basis B of affinoid opens of the flag variety and the approximating sections x_n
items.statement: There is a basis B of open affinoid subsets of Fl, stable under finite intersections, such that for U in B the preimage V_infinity = pi_HT^{-1}(U) is affinoid perfectoid, is the preimage of an affinoid V_{K_p} in X_{K^p K_p} for K_p small, and the colimit of the H^0(V_{K_p}, O) has dense image in H^0(V_infinity, O). Concretely B consists of the finite intersections of rational subsets of U_1 = {|x| <= 1} and U_2 = {|x| >= 1}. Fix U in B inside U_1, so that e_1 generates H^0(V_infinity, omega_{K^p}) and x is regular there. With G_0 = 1 + p^m M_2(Z_p) for m >= 2 chosen so that V_infinity is the preimage of an affinoid V_{G_0}, and G_n = G_0^{p^n}, one can find integers r(n) increasing and sections x_n at level G_{r(n)} with |x - x_n| <= p^{-n}, the line bundle omega_1 being trivial at that level.
items.locator: Section 3.2.1, p. 19; quoted from [Sch15, Theorem III.1.2], [Pan22, Theorem 4.1.7 and 4.3.5]

items.name: Theorem 3.2.2: explicit power-series description of the locally analytic sections
items.statement: Let chi = (n_1,n_2) be an integral weight. (1) For each n >= 0 and each sequence of sections c_i in H^0(V_{G_{r(n)}}, omega^{n_1-n_2}) such that the norms of e_1^{n_2-n_1} c_i p^{(n-1)i} are uniformly bounded, the series f = t^{n_1} e_1^{n_2-n_1} sum_i c_i (x - x_n)^i converges in the G_{r(n)}-analytic vectors of O^{la,chi}_{K^p}(U), every G_n-analytic vector arises this way, and f = 0 if and only if every c_i = 0. (2) Likewise, sections c'_i in H^0(V_{G_{r(n)}}, omega^{n_1-n_2+k}) with the norms of e_1^{n_2-n_1-k} c'_i p^{-(n-1)i} uniformly bounded give all G_n-analytic vectors of omega^{k,la,chi}_{K^p}(U), again with no relations.
items.locator: Theorem 3.2.2 with its proof, pp. 19-20; deduced from [Pan22, Theorem 4.3.9 and Lemma 5.1.2], part (2) from part (1) because multiplication by e_1^k is an isomorphism
items.note: This power-series description is the computational basis of the whole paper: every later local computation, including the differential operators of section 4, is made in these coordinates.

items.name: Corollary 3.2.3: the n-finite vectors and a tensor decomposition
items.statement: For chi = (n_1,n_2) and k integers, let omega^{k,la,chi}_{K^p}(U)^{n-fin} be the subspace of elements t^{n_1} e_1^{n_2-n_1} sum_{i<=l} c_i x^i with c_i in H^0(V_{G_n}, omega^{n_1-n_2+k}) for some l and n. Then it is dense in omega^{k,la,chi}_{K^p}(U), and there is a natural isomorphism omega^{k,la,chi}_{K^p}(U)^{n-fin} = omega^{n_1-n_2+k,sm}_{K^p}(U) tensor_{Q_p} M^v_{(n_2,n_1)}, where M^v_{(n_2,n_1)} consists of those elements with the c_i in Q_p. The notation for M^v comes from the category O.

items.name: Twisting the weight by t
items.statement: O^{la,(n_1+k,n_2+k)}_{K^p} = O^{la,(n_1,n_2)}_{K^p} . t^k for every integer k, which reduces computations to the case n_1 = 0.

items.name: Locally algebraic vectors: the sheaves O^{lalg,chi}
items.statement: For k >= 0 and chi = (0,k), the relative Hodge-Tate filtration gives V(1) -> omega_{K^p}, whose k-th symmetric power Sym^k V(k) -> omega^k_{K^p} is the natural map from H^0(Fl, omega^k_Fl)(k). This defines an injective map Sym^k V(k) tensor omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p} -> O^{la}_{K^p} landing in the weight-(0,k) part, whose image is exactly the subspace of GL_2(Q_p)-locally algebraic vectors of O^{la,(0,k)}_{K^p}; for chi = (n_1, n_1+k) one twists by t^{n_1}. The image is denoted O^{lalg,chi}_{K^p}.

items.name: The Banach spaces A_n and B_n, and a formal power series model
items.statement: For U as above let A_n be the set of f in O^{la,chi}_{K^p}(U) expressible as t^{n_1} e_1^{n_2-n_1} sum_i c_i (x-x_n)^i with the norms of e_1^{n_2-n_1} c_i p^{(n-1)i} uniformly bounded; by [Pan22, Remark 4.3.11] this is independent of the choice of x_n, and it is a Banach space for the sup norm of those quantities. There are continuous inclusions of the G_n-analytic vectors into A_n into the G_{r(n)}-analytic vectors, so O^{la,chi}_{K^p}(U) is the colimit of the A_n as LB-spaces. Fixing a generator s of omega^{n_1-n_2} at level G_{r(n)} identifies A_n with the product of countably many copies of the integral structure sheaf tensored with Q_p, equivalently with O^+(V_{G_{r(n)}})[[(x-x_n)/p^{n-1}]] tensor Q_p. The analogous subspace B_n of omega^{k,la,chi}_{K^p}(U) satisfies H^0(V_{G_{r(n)}}, omega^k) tensor A_n = B_n.
items.locator: Section 3.2.7 with the displayed isomorphisms (3.2.1) and (3.2.2), pp. 20-21
items.note: The model O^+[[ (x-x_n)/p^{n-1} ]] tensor Q_p is exactly the Banach algebra whose compact homomorphisms were isolated in Example 2.2.2.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.8 and Remark 3.2.9: the smooth-to-locally-analytic twisting isomorphism
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism omega^{k,sm}_{K^p} tensor_{O^{sm}_{K^p}} O^{la,chi}_{K^p} = omega^{k,la,chi}_{K^p}, obtained by passing to the colimit in the isomorphisms H^0(V_{G_{r(n)}}, omega^k) tensor A_n = B_n, the same argument applying when e_2 rather than e_1 is a generator. Repeating the argument without fixing the weight, using [Pan22, Theorem 4.3.9], gives omega^{k,la}_{K^p} = omega^{k,sm}_{K^p} tensor_{O^{sm}_{K^p}} O^{la}_{K^p}, which is the isomorphism claimed in 3.1.2.

items.name: Cech complexes of the analytic-vector subsheaves
items.statement: For a finite subset U = {U_1,...,U_l} of B choose G_0 = 1 + p^m M_2(Z_p) with every U_i stable under it. Inside the Cech complex of O^{la,chi}_{K^p} for that cover sits the subcomplex of G_n-analytic vectors, whose cohomology is written Cech-H^*(U, O^{G_n-an,chi}_{K^p}); for m >= n there are natural transition maps.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.11: the Cech cohomology is essentially zero
items.statement: Let U be a finite cover of some U in B by elements of B. Then for every i >= 1 and n >= 0 the natural map from Cech-H^i(U, O^{G_n-an,chi}_{K^p}) to Cech-H^i(U, O^{G_m-an,chi}_{K^p}) is zero for m sufficiently large. The proof replaces the sections over each U_I by the Banach spaces A_{I,n}, identifies the resulting complex with a countable product of Cech complexes of the integral structure sheaf for a finite affinoid cover at level G_{r(n)}, and quotes Tate's acyclicity, whose higher cohomology is killed by a power of p.
items.note: Used only in the proof of Proposition 3.4.11.

items.name: The two covers U and U-prime of the flag variety
items.statement: Let U = {U_1, U_2} with U_1 = {|x| <= 1} and U_2 = {|x| >= 1}, and let U' = {U'_1, U'_2} with U'_1 = {|x| <= |p^{-1}|} and U'_2 = {|x| >= |p|}; both cover Fl, and U'_1, U'_2 are obtained from U_1, U_2 by the action of diag(p,1) and its inverse, so the results proved for elements of B apply to them although they do not lie in B. Choosing G_0 stable on all four, restriction induces natural maps from the Cech cohomology of U' to that of U at each level of analyticity.

items.name: Corollary 3.2.13: sections become extendable to the larger cover
items.statement: For every n >= 0 there is m >= n such that the image of Cech-H^1(U, O^{G_n-an,chi}_{K^p}) in Cech-H^1(U, O^{G_m-an,chi}_{K^p}) lies in the image of Cech-H^1(U', O^{G_m-an,chi}_{K^p}). Equivalently: for every G_n-analytic section s over U_1 cap U_2 there are G_m-analytic sections s_i over U_i such that s + s_1 + s_2 extends to a G_m-analytic section over U'_1 cap U'_2. The proof applies Proposition 3.2.11 twice, to the cover {U_1, U'_1 cap U_2} of U'_1 and then to the cover {U_2, U'_1 cap U'_2} of U_2.

items.name: The Galois action on the sheaves, and fields of definition
items.statement: Since the finite-level modular curves are defined over Q_p, there is a natural continuous action of G_{Q_p} on X_{K^p} commuting with GL_2(Q_p), hence on O^{la,chi}_{K^p} for every integral weight chi; section 3.3 studies this semilinear action relative to the C-structure. For U in B, the affinoids V_{G_n} and their preimages are defined over a finite extension of Q_p: this is clear for U_1 and U_2 because Q_p is dense in C, so x can be approximated by a section defined over a finite extension at finite level, and the general case follows since every U in B is a finite intersection of rational subsets of U_1 and U_2. Fixing a finite extension K over which V_{G_0} is defined, G_K acts continuously on the LB-space O^{la,chi}_{K^p}(U) and on each C-Banach space of G_n-analytic vectors.
items.locator: Section 3.3.1, pp. 23-24; the reference is [Pan22, Theorem 5.1.8] and its proof

items.name: Semilinear C-Banach representations, the field K_infinity and the functor W -> W^K
items.statement: For K a finite extension of Q_p in C let K_infinity be the maximal Z_p-extension of K inside K(mu_{p^infinity}): with the decomposition Z_p^* = (Z/p)^* x (1+2pZ_p) and epsilon~_p the composite of the cyclotomic character with the projection to the second factor, H_K is the kernel of epsilon~_p and K_infinity is its fixed field, so Gal(K_infinity/K) is non-canonically Z_p. For W a C-Banach space with a continuous semilinear G_K-action, W^K is the subspace of G_{K_infinity}-fixed, G_K-analytic vectors, a K-Banach space, and phi_K : C completed-tensor_K W^K -> W is the induced map. The case of interest is when phi_K is an isomorphism; Tate's normalised trace then gives L tensor_K W^K = W^L for every finite extension L, so phi_L is an isomorphism too.
items.locator: Section 3.3.2, p. 24; following Berger-Colmez, whose section 3.1 observes that analytic, not finite, vectors are the right notion in general

items.name: Proposition 3.3.3: the base change of a trivial-action Banach space
items.statement: Let X be a K-Banach space representation of G_K with X^K = X, that is the action of G_{K_infinity} is trivial and the induced action of Gal(K_infinity/K) is analytic. Then (C completed-tensor_K X)^K = X.

items.name: Corollary 3.3.4: kernels and quotients of maps between decompleted representations
items.statement: Let W_1, W_2 be C-Banach spaces with continuous semilinear G_K-actions for which phi_K is an isomorphism, and let phi : W_1 -> W_2 be a continuous C-linear G_{Q_p}-equivariant map. Then (1) ker phi = C completed-tensor_K (ker phi)^K; (2) if phi is a closed embedding then the quotient Z satisfies Z = C completed-tensor_K Z^K; and (3) the same holds for the quotient by the image of any strict phi. The proof reduces to the exactness of C completed-tensor_K (-) on short exact sequences of K-Banach spaces, which follows by choosing an orthonormal basis of C over K.

items.name: The Sen operator
items.statement: By definition the Lie algebra of Gal(K_infinity/K) acts on W^K, and that Lie algebra is identified with Q_p through the cyclotomic character; the action of 1 is the Sen operator, and it is K-linear.

items.name: Hodge-Tate C-Banach representations and their weight decomposition
items.statement: A C-Banach space W with continuous semilinear G_K-action is Hodge-Tate of weight {w_1,...,w_n}, a finite set of integers, if there is a finite extension L of K in C such that phi_L is an isomorphism and the Sen operator acts semisimply on W^L with eigenvalues -w_1,...,-w_n, all the corresponding eigenspaces being non-zero; W is then the direct sum of the W_{-w_i} = C completed-tensor_L W^L_{-w_i}, each Hodge-Tate of the single weight w_i and independent of L. W is Hodge-Tate if it is so for some finite set of integers.

items.name: Remark 3.3.7: comparison with the classical notion
items.statement: W is Hodge-Tate of weight 0 exactly when W = C completed-tensor_K W^{G_K}: if W = C completed-tensor_L W^L_0 then Gal(L_infinity/L) acts trivially on W^L_0, since the action is analytic with trivial infinitesimal action, so W^L_0 = W^{G_L}, and Galois descent gives W^{G_L} = L tensor_K W^{G_K}. More generally W is Hodge-Tate of weight w exactly when its w-th Tate twist is Hodge-Tate of weight 0, and Hodge-Tate of weight {w_1,...,w_n} exactly when W is the direct sum of the C(-w_i) completed-tensor_K W(w_i)^{G_K}. This recovers the classical notion in finite dimensions, and shows that W = C completed-tensor_K W^K whenever W is Hodge-Tate.

items.name: Proposition 3.3.8 and Lemma 3.3.9: the analytic vectors are Hodge-Tate of weight -n_2
items.statement: Let chi = (n_1,n_2) be an integral weight and U in B as in 3.3.1. Then the space of G_n-analytic vectors of O^{la,chi}_{K^p}(U) is Hodge-Tate of weight -n_2 for every n >= 0. The proof first shows that the Banach space A_n of 3.2.7 is Hodge-Tate of weight -n_2: enlarging K so that it contains the p^2-th roots of unity and so that x_n is defined over K, the elements t, e_1, e_2 are acted on by G_K through the cyclotomic character, so x is fixed and A_n is G_K-stable; the subspace A_{n,K} of series with coefficients in the G_K-invariants is a K-Banach space on which G_K acts through the n_2-th power of the cyclotomic character, and Proposition 3.3.3 gives A_n = C completed-tensor_K A_{n,K}. Since the G_n-analytic vectors sit inside A_n, taking G_n-analytic vectors commutes with the base change.
items.locator: Proposition 3.3.8 and Lemma 3.3.9 with their proofs, pp. 26-27

items.name: Proposition 3.3.10: restriction to a smaller open is compact after decompletion
items.statement: Let chi be an integral weight and U, U' in B be G_0 = 1 + p^l M_2(Z_p)-stable opens with l >= 2 whose preimages are the preimages of affinoids V_{G_0}, V'_{G_0} defined over a finite extension K of Q_p, and suppose U is a strict neighbourhood of U', that is the closure of U' lies in U. Then (1) and (2) the G_n-analytic vectors over U and over U' are the base change from K of their K-forms for every n; and (3) the restriction map on K-forms from level n over U to level m over U' is compact for m >= n sufficiently large.
items.note: The proof is where Example 2.2.2 is used: in the coordinates of 3.2.7 the restriction becomes a homomorphism of the Banach algebras O^+[[ (x-x_n)/p^{n-1} ]] tensor Q_p in which the variable is topologically nilpotent, because |x_{n+1} - x_n| <= p^{-n}, while the induced map of integral affinoid algebras is compact since modular curves are of finite type and V_{G_{r(n)}} is a strict neighbourhood of V’_{G_{r(n)}}.

items.name: Remark 3.3.11: what Proposition 3.3.10 says
items.statement: The restriction map from the G_n-analytic vectors over U to the G_m-analytic vectors over U' is essentially the completed tensor product with C of a compact operator.
items.note: This is what feeds Lemma 2.2.5 - the Cartan-Serre criterion - in Subsection 3.4.

items.name: The problem: topologising H^i(Fl, O^{la,chi})
items.statement: For U in B the space H^0(U, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}) = H^0(U, O_{K^p})^{la,chi} is a Hausdorff LB-space; the goal of the subsection is to put such a topology on the cohomology H^i(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}). The starting point is that by Scholze's work H^i(Fl, O^+_{K^p}) is isomorphic as an almost O_C-module to the O_C-coefficient completed cohomology, so it has bounded p-torsion and H^i(Fl, O_{K^p}) is a C-Banach space; and that H^*(Fl, O^+_{K^p}) is computed by the two-term Cech complex of the cover {U_1, U_2}, so that after inverting p the Cech differential is strict.
items.locator: Section 3.4.1, p. 28; the inputs are [Pan22, Corollary 4.4.3] and the proof of [Pan22, Theorem 4.4.6]

items.name: Lemma 3.4.2: restriction to the intersection is a closed embedding
items.statement: The restriction map O_{K^p}(U_1) -> O_{K^p}(U_{12}) is a closed embedding. Injectivity: a section in the kernel extends to a global section vanishing on U_2, and H^0(Fl, O_{K^p}) is the C-coefficient completed cohomology H~^0(K^p,C), on which SL_2(Q_p) acts trivially, so the section is SL_2(Q_p)-invariant; since SL_2(Q_p) . U_2 = Fl it vanishes. Strictness is deduced from the strictness of the Cech complex using the Weyl element.
items.locator: Lemma 3.4.2 with its proof, pp. 28-29; the identification of H^0 is [Pan22, Theorem 4.4.6] and the triviality of the SL_2-action is [Eme06b, 4.2]

items.name: Lemma 3.4.3: strictness is detected by a Weyl involution
items.statement: Let i : A -> B be a continuous map of Q_p-Banach spaces and w a continuous involution of B. Then i is strict if and only if (i, w composed with i) : A + A -> B is strict. One direction is a factorisation; for the other, the map intertwines the swap involution of A + A with w, so it suffices to treat the two eigenspaces, where it agrees with (1+w)i and (1-w)i respectively, and (1+w)/2 is a strict projection.
items.note: Applied with the Weyl element of GL_2(Q_p) as w, this identifies the pair (restriction, its Weyl translate) with the Cech differential; it is the trick that removes the largest-separated-quotient step from [Pan22, Theorem 5.1.11] and it also reproves [Pan22, Remark 5.1.14].

items.name: Strictness after taking analytic vectors, and the Cech computation of the cohomology
items.statement: Let G_0 = 1 + p^2 M_2(Z_p) with G_n = G_0^{p^n}, acting unitarily and continuously on O_{K^p}(U_1) and O_{K^p}(U_{12}). By Lemma 3.4.2 and Lemma 2.3.2 the map on G_n-analytic vectors is again a closed embedding, so by Lemma 3.4.3 the complex of G_n-analytic vectors of the Cech complex is strict; the same holds after passing to a weight chi, giving a strict map from the sum of the G_n-analytic vectors over U_1 and U_2 to those over U_{12}, whose cohomology groups are therefore Banach spaces. Passing to the colimit over n recovers the Cech complex of O^{la,chi}_{K^p} for {U_1,U_2}, and this computes H^i(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}): the Cech cohomology of O^{la}_{K^p} vanishes in positive degrees on each U in B, hence so does that of O^{la,chi}_{K^p}.
items.locator: Section 3.4.4, p. 29; the vanishing is from the proof of [Pan22, Theorem 4.4.6] together with [Pan22, Theorem 5.1.2(1)]

items.name: Definition 3.4.5: the LB-space structure on the cohomology
items.statement: Define Cech-H^*(O^{G_n-an}_{K^p}) as the cohomology of the two-term complex of G_n-analytic vectors for the cover {U_1,U_2}, and Cech-H^*(O^{G_n-an,chi}_{K^p}) likewise in weight chi (the notation of 3.2.10). These are C-Banach spaces with an analytic G_n-action, and H^i(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}) is given the LB-space structure of the colimit over n.

items.name: Remark 3.4.6: the two LB-structures on the cohomology agree
items.statement: The same recipe gives an LB-space structure on H^i(Fl, O^{la}_{K^p}), and by [Pan22, Theorem 4.4.6] there is a second one coming from H^i(Fl, O^{la}_{K^p}) = H^i(Fl, O_{K^p})^{la}; the two are equivalent. For i = 0 the comparison map is an isomorphism. For i = 1 one needs, for each n, a continuous map back from H^1(Fl, O_{K^p})^{G_n-an} to Cech-H^1(O^{G_m-an}_{K^p}) for some m compatible with the inclusions, and this follows from the strong LA-acyclicity of the sections over the U_i and of H^0(Fl,O_{K^p}).
items.locator: Remark 3.4.6, pp. 29-30; the acyclicity input is the beginning of the proof of [Pan22, Theorem 5.1.11]

items.name: Remark 3.4.7: the same topology for the twisted sheaves
items.statement: The construction of Definition 3.4.5 applies to H^i(Fl, omega^{k,la,chi}_{K^p}): choosing an invertible section of omega^k_{K^p} over the preimage of each member of the cover identifies the push-forward with O_{K^p} there, giving a Banach structure independent of the choice, and Lemma 3.4.3 again makes the Cech differential strict. This puts a Banach space structure on H^i(Fl, pi_{HT*} omega^k_{K^p}), although the GL_2(Q_p)-action is then only continuous and not unitary. This is not used in the paper.

items.name: Remark 3.4.8: a further application of the Weyl-involution lemma
items.statement: Lemma 3.4.3 also proves the claim of [Pan22, Remark 5.1.14] without any calculation.

items.name: Proposition 3.4.10: the Cech cohomology is Hodge-Tate of weight -n_2
items.statement: For an integral weight chi = (n_1,n_2), the Galois group G_K acts naturally on the sections over U_1, U_2 and U_{12} for a suitable finite extension K, and by Proposition 3.3.8 the G_n-analytic vectors there are Hodge-Tate of weight -n_2. Hence Cech-H^*(O^{G_n-an,chi}_{K^p}) is Hodge-Tate of weight -n_2, directly by Corollary 3.3.4.

items.name: Proposition 3.4.11: the cohomology is a Hausdorff LB-space
items.statement: H^i(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}) is a Hausdorff LB-space. The continuous map to H^i(Fl, O_{K^p}) is injective except when i = 1 and chi vanishes on the coroot h = diag(1,-1), and in all those cases Hausdorffness follows because the target is a C-Banach space; by Remark 3.2.4 the remaining case reduces to weight (0,0), which is handled by Lemmas 3.4.12 and 3.4.13 together with Corollary 2.2.4.
items.locator: Proposition 3.4.11 with its proof, pp. 30-31; the injectivity criterion is [Pan22, Corollary 5.1.3(2)]

items.name: Lemma 3.4.12: decompletion of the degree-one Cech cohomology
items.statement: For every n >= 0 there is a natural isomorphism Cech-H^1(O^{G_n-an,(0,0)}_{K^p}) = Cech-H^1(O^{G_n-an,(0,0)}_{K^p})^{G_K} completed-tensor_K C, directly from Proposition 3.4.10 and Remark 3.3.7.

items.name: Lemma 3.4.13: the transition maps are compact and their kernels stabilise
items.statement: Write i_{n,m} for the transition map on G_K-invariants of Cech-H^1(O^{G_n-an,(0,0)}_{K^p}). Then (1) i_{n,m} is compact for m sufficiently large; and (2) ker i_{n,m} stabilises for m large, equal to the kernel of the map to H^1(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p}), which is therefore a closed subspace. Part (1) is a Cartan-Serre argument through Lemma 2.2.5, taking the second cover U' of 3.2.12: Corollary 3.2.13 puts the image of level n inside the image from U' at level m, the same holding on G_K-invariants because that image is Hodge-Tate of weight 0 by Corollary 3.3.4; and since U'_1 cap U'_2 is a strict neighbourhood of U_1 cap U_2, Proposition 3.3.10 makes the relevant restriction compact. Part (2) uses the GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant exact sequence (3.4.1) whose kernel term is the colimit of the H^0(X_{K^p K_p}, O), on which the action is smooth while the action on the Cech group is analytic; so G_{n+1} acts trivially on the relevant quotient, which is therefore finite-dimensional because the G_{n+1}-invariants of that colimit are H^0 at level G_{n+1}, and the open mapping theorem finishes it.
items.locator: Lemma 3.4.13 with both proofs, pp. 31-33; the exact sequence (3.4.1) is [Pan22, Corollary 5.1.3(2)]
items.note: This is improvement (4) of 1.3.2 in action: the Weyl-involution strictness plus a Cartan-Serre argument replace the separated-quotient step of the earlier paper.

items.name: The exact sequence relating the locally analytic and Banach cohomology
items.statement: There is a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant exact sequence 0 -> colim_{K_p} H^0(X_{K^p K_p}, O_{X_{K^p K_p}}) -> H^1(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p}) -> H^1(Fl, O_{K^p})^{la,(0,0)} -> 0, the colimit running over the open compact subgroups of GL_2(Q_p).
items.locator: Displayed sequence (3.4.1), p. 32; quoted from [Pan22, Corollary 5.1.3(2)]
items.note: This is the precise form of the discrepancy between W_0 and H^1(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}) that the introduction flags for k = 1.

items.name: Proposition 3.4.14: analytic vectors in the cohomology come from a finite level
items.statement: For every n >= 0 the subspace of G_n-analytic vectors of H^i(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}) is contained in the image of Cech-H^i(O^{G_m-an,chi}_{K^p}) for some m >= n. Only i = 1 needs an argument, since degree 0 is an equality and Fl is one-dimensional. First, H^1(Fl, O_{K^p})^{G_n-an,chi} lies in the image of the composite from Cech-H^1 at some level, because by (3.4.1) the whole locally analytic cohomology is the union of those images and Proposition 2.1.5 applies to a Banach subspace. Then the finite-dimensional space of G_{m'}-invariants of the colimit of the H^0 lies in the image at some level m, and taking G_n-analytic vectors in (3.4.1) writes any v as v' plus an element of that finite-dimensional space.

items.name: The de Rham bundle of the universal elliptic curve, its connection and the classical theta operator
items.statement: Fix K_p and let X = X_{K^p K_p} with C the cusps. The first relative de Rham cohomology of the universal elliptic curve over X - C is a rank two bundle with a Hodge filtration and Gauss-Manin connection; its canonical extension D to X carries a logarithmic connection nabla : D -> D tensor Omega^1_X(C) and the filtration Fil^n D = D for n <= 0, omega for n = 1, and 0 for n >= 2. The Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism is that the composite omega = Fil^1 D -> D -> gr^0 D tensor Omega^1_X(C) = (wedge^2 D) tensor omega^{-1} tensor Omega^1_X(C) is an isomorphism, so Omega^1_X(C) may be identified with (wedge^2 D)^{-1} tensor omega^2; the cup product identifies wedge^2 D with the canonical extension of H^2_dR. For k >= 0 the k-th symmetric power carries nabla_k and a filtration with Fil^k Sym^k D = omega^k, and Kodaira-Spencer makes Fil^1 Sym^k D -> (Sym^k D / Fil^k) tensor Omega^1_X(C) an isomorphism; hence every section s of gr^0 Sym^k D has a unique lift with nabla_k of the lift in Fil^k Sym^k D tensor Omega^1_X(C). This defines theta'_{k+1} from gr^0 Sym^k D to omega^k tensor Omega^1_X(C), a logarithmic differential operator of order k+1 on omega^{-k} tensor (wedge^2 D)^k; applying the same construction to Sym^k D^* gives theta_{k+1} : omega^{-k} -> omega^{k+2} tensor (wedge^2 D)^{-k-1}. For k = 0, theta_1 is the derivation d followed by Kodaira-Spencer. Everything is compatible with varying K_p.
items.note: This is the classical theta operator of the theory of modular forms; the point of the subsection is to extend it O_Fl-linearly to the infinite level.

items.name: The smooth de Rham bundle at infinite level
items.statement: Since D is compatible with varying K_p, the push-forward D^{sm}_{K^p} of the colimit of its pull-backs is a locally free O^{sm}_{K^p}-module on Fl, with Fil^1 = omega^{1,sm}_{K^p} and a connection into D^{sm}_{K^p} tensor Omega^1_{K^p}(C)^{sm}, where the latter is the corresponding colimit of the sheaves of log differentials. The construction of 4.1.2 repeats verbatim; Kodaira-Spencer gives omega^{2,sm}_{K^p} tensor (wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p})^{-1} = Omega^1_{K^p}(C)^{sm}. The line bundle wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p} is isomorphic to O^{la}_{K^p}, but not Hecke-equivariantly.
items.note: The failure of Hecke-equivariance of that last isomorphism is exactly what 4.2.3 fixes.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.4: the operators d_{k+1} exist and are unique
items.statement: Let chi = (n_1,n_2) be integral with k = n_2 - n_1 >= 0. Then there is a unique natural continuous operator d_{k+1} from O^{la,chi}_{K^p} to omega^{2k+2,la,chi}_{K^p} tensor (wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p})^{-k-1} = O^{la,chi}_{K^p} tensor (Omega^1_{K^p}(C)^{sm})^{tensor k+1} such that (1) d_{k+1} is O_Fl-linear, and (2) d_{k+1}(t^{n_1} e_1^i e_2^{k-i} s) = t^{n_1} e_1^i e_2^{k-i} theta_{k+1}(s) for every smooth section s of omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p} and every 0 <= i <= k.
items.note: Uniqueness is immediate from Theorem 3.2.2: the elements t^{n_1} e_1^i e_2^{k-i} s span a dense O_Fl(U)-submodule.

items.name: Remark 4.1.5: the twisted operators d’_{k+1}
items.statement: Being O_Fl-linear, d_{k+1} can be twisted by a line bundle on Fl. Twisting by omega_Fl^{-k}(-k) and using the isomorphisms of 3.1.2 gives, for chi' = chi - (0,k) = (n_1,n_1), a continuous O_Fl-linear operator d'_{k+1} from omega^{-k,la,chi'}_{K^p} to omega^{k+2,la,chi'}_{K^p} tensor (wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p})^{-k-1} with d'_{k+1}(t^{n_1} s) = t^{n_1} theta_{k+1}(s) for smooth s. The existence of d'_{k+1} is equivalent to that of d_{k+1}.

items.name: The local formula for d_1 and the proof of Theorem 4.1.4
items.statement: For k = 0 the operator is built locally. On U in B with e_1 a generator, for f = t^{n_1} sum_i c_i (x-x_n)^i in A_n one sets d_n(f) = t^{n_1}( sum_i (x-x_n)^i dc_i - sum_i (i+1) c_{i+1} (x-x_n)^i dx_n ), the Leibniz rule applied termwise; continuity of d makes the p^{(n-1)i} dc_i uniformly bounded, so d_n lands in the G_{r(n)}-analytic vectors, and on the dense subspace of finite sums d_n(t^{n_1} sum_{i<=l} c_i x^i) = t^{n_1} sum_i x^i dc_i, whence d_{n+1} restricted to A_n is d_n. Passing to the limit gives d_1, independent of the choice of the x_n and compatible with restriction, hence a map of sheaves. O_Fl-linearity is local: on U_1 = Spa(C<x>) the construction commutes with multiplication by polynomials in x and so with O_Fl(U_1) by continuity, and a rational subdomain is handled by density of the image of C<x>[1/g]. For general k one forms D^{chi'} = D^{sm}_{K^p} tensor O^{la,chi'}_{K^p}, extends the filtration O^{la,chi'}-linearly so that Fil^1 = omega^{1,la,chi'} and gr^0 = omega^{-1,la,chi'} tensor wedge^2 D^{sm}, uses d_1 to build a connection nabla_{chi'} on D^{chi'} whose Kodaira-Spencer composite is an isomorphism, and then applies the construction of theta_{k+1} to Sym^k of the dual.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.6: the canonical continuous splitting r_k
items.statement: Normalise the filtration on the dual D^{*,(0,0)} so that gr^i vanishes for i < 0 and gr^0 = omega^{-1,la,(0,0)}_{K^p}. Then the surjection Sym^k D^{*,(0,0)} -> gr^0 Sym^k D^{*,(0,0)} = omega^{-k,la,(0,0)}_{K^p} has a unique continuous left inverse r_k whose composite with nabla_k lands in Fil^k Sym^k D^{*,(0,0)} tensor Omega^1_{K^p}(C)^{sm}. Twisting by wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p} gives the analogous r'_k for Sym^k D^{(0,0)}, with r'_k(f tensor c^k) = r_k(f) tensor c^k for a global invertible horizontal section c of wedge^2 D. Only continuity needs proof: the map sending f to (f mod Fil^1, nabla_k f mod Fil^k) is an isomorphism by Kodaira-Spencer, hence an isometry by the open mapping theorem, and r composed with r_k is (f,0).
items.note: Used in Subsection 6.4.

items.name: What section 4.1 constructs
items.statement: The subsection constructs an operator from O^{la,chi}_{K^p} to a twist of omega^{2k+2,la,chi}_{K^p} for the integer k determined by chi; it comes from differential operators on modular curves and extends the classical theta_{k+1} O_Fl-linearly.

items.name: The operator d-bar_1 from Beilinson-Bernstein localisation
items.statement: There is a GL_2-equivariant isomorphism Omega^1_Fl = omega_Fl^{-2} tensor det. By Beilinson-Bernstein localisation, differential operators on Fl act on O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p}, which gives a natural map d-bar_1 from O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} to O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor_{O_Fl} Omega^1_Fl. Concretely the derivation d/dx on O_Fl is the action of the nilpotent u_+ = the matrix with a single 1 in the upper right, so on any open where e_1 is invertible d-bar_1 sends s to u_+(s) tensor dx; thus d-bar_1 extends the de Rham differential of Fl in an O^{sm}_{K^p}-linear way.
items.locator: Sections 4.2.1 and 4.2.2, pp. 37-38; the localisation input is Beilinson-Bernstein
items.note: This is why the construction along Fl is far simpler than the one along the modular curve: differential operators on the flag variety are just the Lie algebra action.

items.name: The Hecke-equivariant relative Hodge-Tate sequence and the corrected t
items.statement: To make everything Hecke-equivariant the sequence (3.1.1) must be modified: the term omega^{-1} is replaced by gr^1 D = wedge^2 D tensor omega^{-1}, giving 0 -> wedge^2 D tensor omega^{-1}_{K^p}(1) -> V(1) tensor O_{X_{K^p}} -> omega_{K^p} -> 0. Section 3.1 implicitly fixed a trivialisation of wedge^2 D, that is a global non-vanishing section c, and the choice made here is the pull-back of a GL_2(Z-hat)-fixed global section; since wedge^2 D extends the second de Rham cohomology of the universal curve, GL_2(A_f) acts on c through the inverse adelic norm of the determinant. Taking the wedge product gives O_{X_{K^p}} = (wedge^2 D)^{-1} tensor O_{X_{K^p}} tensor det(1), under which t is the image of c^{-1} tensor 1 tensor b. Hence on Fl there is a natural isomorphism O^{la,(1,1)}_{K^p} = O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} . t = O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor (wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p})^{-1} tensor det(1), independent of the choice of t, and combining it with Kodaira-Spencer a natural isomorphism Omega^1_{K^p}(C)^{sm} tensor O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor Omega^1_Fl = O^{la,(1,-1)}_{K^p}(1), normalised by sending s tensor 1 tensor dx to s t / e_1^2 where e_1 is invertible; this is independent of the trivialisations of wedge^2 D and of Q_p(1).
items.locator: Section 4.2.3 with the displayed sequences (4.2.1), (4.2.2) and (4.2.3), p. 38
items.note: This is improvement (3) of 1.3.2: the sequence (4.2.1), not (3.1.1), is the Hecke-equivariant form, and it is the identification (4.2.3) that lets the composite of the two differential operators be read as a map between weight spaces.

items.name: The BGG construction of d-bar_{k+1} for k = 1 and the infinitesimal characters lambda_k
items.statement: For k >= 0 the (k+1)-st derivation gives a GL_2-equivariant map omega^k_Fl -> omega^k_Fl tensor (Omega^1_Fl)^{k+1} = omega_Fl^{-k-2} tensor det^{k+1}, sending s to (u_+)^{k+1}(s) tensor (dx)^{k+1}; the operator to be constructed extends this O^{sm}_{K^p}-linearly up to a constant, following the idea of Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand. The centre of U(g) acts by the same character, called lambda_k, on O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor omega^k_Fl and on its twist by (Omega^1_Fl)^{k+1}. Taking locally analytic vectors in the push-forward of (4.2.1) and twisting gives the exact sequence 0 -> wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p} tensor omega^{-1,la,(1,0)}_{K^p} -> V tensor O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} -> omega^{1,la,(0,1)}_{K^p}(-1) -> 0. By Harish-Chandra and the relation between theta_h and infinitesimal characters, the weight-(n_1,n_2) and weight-(k_1,k_2) parts of O^{la}_{K^p} have the same infinitesimal character exactly when n_1+n_2 = k_1+k_2 and (n_1-n_2-1)^2 = (k_1-k_2-1)^2; hence the lambda_1-isotypic component of the middle term is canonically the quotient, and likewise after twisting by Omega^1_Fl. Taking lambda_1-isotypic components of V tensor d-bar_1 therefore produces d-bar_2, which a direct calculation identifies with s -> (u_+)^2(s) tensor (dx)^2 up to a non-zero rational constant.
items.locator: Sections 4.2.4 with the displayed sequence (4.2.4), pp. 38-39; the infinitesimal-character criterion is [Pan22, Corollary 4.2.8]

items.name: The maps phi_{k,1} and phi_{k,2} for general k
items.statement: For k >= 1 the same construction is run with V replaced by its k-th symmetric power and lambda_1 by lambda_k. The sequence (4.2.4) gives a natural surjection phi_{k,1} : Sym^k V tensor O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} -> omega^{k,la,(0,k)}_{K^p}(-k) and a natural injection phi_{k,2} : omega^{k,la,(0,k)}_{K^p}(-k) tensor (Omega^1_Fl)^{k+1} -> Sym^k V tensor O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor Omega^1_Fl.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.6: both maps are isomorphisms on lambda_k-isotypic parts
items.statement: Both phi_{k,1} and phi_{k,2} induce isomorphisms on lambda_k-isotypic components; in particular phi_{k,1} has a natural U(g)-equivariant left inverse phi'_k from omega^{k,la,(0,k)}_{K^p}(-k) to Sym^k V tensor O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p}. The proof filters Sym^k V tensor O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} by the (wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p})^i tensor omega^{k-2i,la,(i,k-i)}_{K^p}(i-k) for i = 0,...,k and observes that only the i = 0 piece contributes to the lambda_k-isotypic part.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.7: the operators d-bar_{k+1}
items.statement: Let chi = (n_1,n_2) be integral with k = n_2 - n_1 >= 0 and set -w.(-chi) = (n_2+1, n_1-1). There is a natural continuous operator d-bar_{k+1} from O^{la,chi}_{K^p} to (wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p})^{k+1} tensor omega^{-2k-2,la,-w.(-chi)}_{K^p}(k+1) = O^{la,chi}_{K^p} tensor (Omega^1_Fl)^{k+1}, formally the (k+1)-st power of the derivation of Fl, such that (1) it is O^{sm}_{K^p}-linear and (2) there is a non-zero rational constant c with d-bar_{k+1}(s) = c (u_+)^{k+1}(s) tensor (dx)^{k+1} for every section over an open where x is regular. Moreover d-bar_{k+1} commutes with the GL_2(Q_p)-action and with the Hecke action away from p.

items.name: Remark 4.2.8: the two families of operators commute
items.statement: Comparing with the operators d_{k+1} of Theorem 4.1.4, the explicit formulae show that d-bar_{k+1} commutes with d_{k+1}. In fact both can be defined uniformly, which is best explained in the local picture of Subsections 5.2 and 5.3.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.9: d-bar_{k+1} is surjective with locally algebraic kernel
items.statement: For chi = (0,k) with k >= 0 the operator d-bar_{k+1} from O^{la,(0,k)}_{K^p} to its twist by (Omega^1_Fl)^{k+1} is surjective, and its kernel is exactly the locally algebraic subsheaf O^{lalg,(0,k)}_{K^p} = Sym^k V(k) tensor omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p}. For general chi with k = n_2 - n_1 >= 0 the kernel is O^{lalg,chi}_{K^p} = Sym^k V(k) tensor omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p} . t^{n_1}.
