By equivariance it suffices to argue where e_1 generates, where the explicit formula applies: surjectivity because u_+ is surjective there, and for the kernel because it is gl_2-stable and annihilated by (u_+)^{k+1}, so the action is locally finite and an infinitesimal-character computation identifies it with the Sym^k V-isotypic subspace.
items.locator: Proposition 4.2.9 with its proof, pp. 40-41; the surjectivity of u_+ is [Pan22, Proposition 5.2.9]
items.note: These are the two properties of d-bar singled out in 1.2.11 as the key to the spectral decomposition.

items.name: Remark 4.2.10: the d-bar resolution of the smooth sheaf
items.statement: For k = 0 there is a natural exact sequence 0 -> O^{sm}_{K^p} -> O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} -> O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} tensor Omega^1_Fl -> 0, a d-bar-resolution of O^{sm}_{K^p}; in general d-bar_{k+1} gives 0 -> Sym^k V(k) tensor omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p} -> O^{la,(0,k)}_{K^p} -> O^{la,(0,k)}_{K^p} tensor (Omega^1_Fl)^{k+1} -> 0.

items.name: What section 4.2 constructs
items.statement: The subsection constructs an O^{sm}_{K^p}-linear operator from O^{la,chi}_{K^p} to a twist of omega^{-2k-2,la,-w.(-chi)}_{K^p}, coming from differential operators on the flag variety.

items.name: Definition 4.3.1: the intertwining operator I_k
items.statement: Let chi = (n_1,n_2) be integral with k = n_2 - n_1 >= 0. Define I_k : O^{la,chi}_{K^p} -> O^{la,-w.(-chi)}_{K^p}(k+1) as the composite of d_{k+1} with d-bar'_{k+1} := d-bar_{k+1} tensor 1, which makes sense because d-bar_{k+1} is O^{sm}_{K^p}-linear. Formally I_k = d-bar'_{k+1} composed with d_{k+1}, and it commutes with GL_2(Q_p) and with the Hecke action away from p. Since the two operators commute, I_k equally agrees with the composite of d-bar_{k+1} followed by d_{k+1} tensor 1, the identification of the target using (4.2.3); so I_k can be read in either order.

items.name: Remark 4.3.2: what I_k will turn out to be
items.statement: Section 6 gives a p-adic Hodge-theoretic interpretation of I_k: it comes from the action of the additive group, a monodromy operator, in Fontaine's classification of almost de Rham B_dR-representations, and the Tate twist by k+1 in the definition is better understood as gr^k B_dR.

items.name: Definition 4.3.3 and 4.3.4: the induced map on cohomology and its variants
items.statement: Write I^1_k for H^1(I_k), a map from H^1(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}) to H^1(Fl, O^{la,-w.(-chi)}_{K^p}(k+1)). If k > 0 then both sides are the locally analytic vectors of the corresponding Banach cohomology, so I^1_k may be viewed as a map H^1(Fl, O_{K^p})^{la,chi} -> H^1(Fl, O_{K^p})^{la,-w.(-chi)}(k+1). If k = 0 then by the exact sequence (3.4.1) and Remark 4.4.16 the map I^1_0 factors through that quotient, and the induced map is written I'_0.
items.locator: Definition 4.3.3 and Section 4.3.4, pp. 41-42; the identification of the cohomology is [Pan22, Corollary 5.1.3(2)]

items.name: The n-cohomology problem
items.statement: Fix k >= 0 and chi = (n_1,n_2) with n_2 - n_1 = k, and let n be the upper-triangular nilpotent subalgebra C u_+ of g. The aim of the subsection is to determine the n-invariants of ker I^1_k as a representation of the upper-triangular Borel B of GL_2(Q_p), and to deduce the finiteness statement of Theorem 1.1.14. Multiplying by t^{-n_1} reduces to the case n_1 = 0. The results are not used in Sections 5 and 6.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.2: the kernel of I^1_k is the kernel of H^1(d_{k+1})
items.statement: ker I^1_k = ker H^1(d_{k+1}). Since I_k is d-bar'_{k+1} after d_{k+1}, it suffices that H^1(d-bar'_{k+1}) is injective; d-bar_{k+1} tensor 1 is surjective by Proposition 4.2.9, so one needs H^1(Fl, ker d-bar'_{k+1}) = 0, and the second part of that proposition identifies the kernel with Sym^k V(k) tensor omega^{k+2,la,chi}_{K^p} tensor (wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p})^{-k-1}, which reduces the claim to H^1(Fl, omega^{k+2,sm}_{K^p}) = 0 for k >= 0.
items.locator: Lemma 4.4.2 with its proof, p. 42; the vanishing is [Pan22, Corollary 5.3.6]

items.name: Lemma 4.4.4 and Remark 4.4.5: a homological lemma on a space of cohomological dimension one
items.statement: Let X : F -> G be a map of sheaves of abelian groups on Fl, or any space of cohomological dimension one. There are natural maps r : H^0(Fl,G) -> H^0(Fl, coker X) and delta : ker r = H^0(Fl, X(F)) -> H^1(Fl, ker X), and a natural short exact sequence 0 -> coker delta -> ker H^1(X) -> coker r -> 0. In particular (1) if H^1(Fl, ker X) = 0 then ker H^1(X) = coker r, and (2) if H^0(Fl,G) = 0 then H^0(Fl, X(F)) = 0 and there is a short exact sequence 0 -> H^1(Fl, ker X) -> ker H^1(X) -> H^0(Fl, coker X) -> 0. Equivalently, in terms of the hypercohomology H^*(X) of the two-term complex, ker H^1(X) = H^1(X)/Fil^1 H^1(X) with Fil^1 the image of H^0(Fl,G), and 0 -> H^1(Fl, ker X) -> H^1(X) -> H^0(Fl, coker X) -> 0.
items.locator: Lemma 4.4.4 with its proof and Remark 4.4.5, pp. 42-43
items.note: The hypercohomology formulation of Remark 4.4.5 is the form that reappears as the complex DR_{k-1} and its Hodge filtration in Remark 1.1.13.

items.name: Overconvergent and classical modular forms at infinite level
items.statement: Let infinity in Fl be the point where e_1 vanishes, with i_infinity its inclusion. Following [Pan22] set M-dagger_k(K^p) to be the stalk of omega^{k,sm}_{K^p} at infinity and M_k(K^p) = H^0(Fl, omega^{k,sm}_{K^p}) = colim_{K_p} H^0(X_{K^p K_p}, omega^k); these are the overconvergent and the classical modular forms of weight k and tame level K^p, with a natural restriction map between them, and M_k(K^p) = 0 for k < 0. Concretely M-dagger_k(K^p) is the colimit over n of the sections of omega^k on a strict neighbourhood of the canonical locus X_{K^p Gamma(p^n),c}, whose connected components correspond to those of X_{K^p Gamma(p^n)} because Igusa curves are irreducible. For a B x G_{Q_p}-representation W the notation W . e_1^i e_2^j means the twist of W(i+j) by the character sending an upper-triangular matrix to a^i d^j.
items.locator: Section 4.4.6 and the discussion on p. 44, with [Pan22, Definition 5.2.5, 5.3.8, Remark 5.2.7] and [Pan22, 5.2.4]

items.name: Proposition 4.4.7: n-invariants, n-coinvariants and H^0 of O^{la,chi}
items.statement: For chi = (0,k) with k >= 0: (1) the n-invariants of O^{la,chi}_{K^p} are omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p} . e_1^k, via s -> e_1^k s; (2) the n-coinvariants form a skyscraper sheaf at infinity, naturally the direct sum of i_{infinity *} M-dagger_{-k}(K^p) . e_2^k and i_{infinity *} M-dagger_{-k}(K^p) . e_1^{1+k} e_2^{-1}; and (3) H^0(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}) = 0 unless k = 0, in which case it is H^0(Fl, O^{sm}_{K^p}) through the natural inclusion. In particular H^0(Fl, u_+(O^{la,chi}_{K^p})) = 0. All these isomorphisms are O^{sm}_{K^p}-linear.
items.locator: Proposition 4.4.7, p. 44; quoted from [Pan22, Propositions 5.2.6, 5.2.9, 5.2.11 and Corollary 5.1.3]

items.name: Corollary 4.4.8 and Remark 4.4.9: the same for the twisted sheaf, and the restriction map
items.statement: For chi = (0,k) with k >= 0: (1) the n-invariants of omega^{2k+2,la,chi}_{K^p} are omega^{k+2,sm}_{K^p} . e_1^k; (2) its n-coinvariants are the skyscraper i_{infinity *} M-dagger_{k+2}(K^p) . e_2^k plus i_{infinity *} M-dagger_{k+2}(K^p) . e_1^{1+k} e_2^{-1}; and (3) H^0(Fl, omega^{2k+2,la,chi}_{K^p}) = Sym^k V(k) tensor M_{k+2}(K^p), induced by the locally algebraic inclusion, because H^0 of the target of d-bar'_{k+1} vanishes so that the H^0 is the H^0 of ker d-bar'_{k+1}. Under these identifications the natural restriction map from H^0 to H^0 of the n-coinvariants is explicit: the n-coinvariants of Sym^k V are Q_p, generated by the image of the k-th power of (0,1), so the map factors through M_{k+2}(K^p) . e_2^k and is the natural map to M-dagger_{k+2}(K^p) . e_2^k.
items.locator: Corollary 4.4.8 with its proof and Remark 4.4.9, pp. 44-45; the vanishing input is [Pan22, Corollary 5.1.3]

items.name: The n-invariants of the cohomology, and the classical theta operator on them
items.statement: Lemma 4.4.4 with Proposition 4.4.7 gives a natural exact sequence 0 -> H^1(Fl, omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p}) . e_1^k -> H^1(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p})^n -> (M-dagger_{-k}/M_{-k}) . e_1^{-1} e_2^{k+1} + M-dagger_{-k} . e_1^k -> 0, where H^0 of the n-coinvariants is twisted by the dual of n to stay B-equivariant, and H^1(Fl, omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p}) is the colimit of the H^1(X_{K^p K_p}, omega^{-k}). Similarly, since H^1(Fl, omega^{k+2,sm}_{K^p}) vanishes, the n-invariants of H^1(Fl, omega^{2k+2,la,chi}_{K^p}) are (M-dagger_{k+2}/M_{k+2}) . e_1^{-1} e_2^{k+1} + M-dagger_{k+2} . e_1^k. Fixing a trivialisation of wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p}, the operator theta_{k+1} induces a map M-dagger_{-k}(K^p) -> M-dagger_{k+2}(K^p), and by functoriality of Lemma 4.4.4 the map H^1(d_{k+1}) is compatible with theta_{k+1} + theta_{k+1} on these descriptions. There is also a constant action of the Cartan h on H^1(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p})^n, different from the horizontal theta_h, splitting it into weight (k,0) and (-1,k+1) parts.
items.locator: Section 4.4.10, p. 45; the identification of H^1 is [Pan22, Lemma 5.3.5] and the vanishing [Pan22, Corollary 5.3.6]

items.name: Definition 4.4.11: the module D_0
items.statement: D_0 := H^0(Fl, wedge^2 D^{sm}_{K^p}), a free rank-one module over M_0(K^p) with a generator on which GL_2(A_f) acts through the inverse adelic norm of the determinant.

items.name: Proposition 4.4.12: the weight decomposition of the n-invariants of ker I^1_k
items.statement: There is a natural weight decomposition of the n-invariants of ker I^1_k as A_{(k,0)} . e_1^k plus A_{(-1,k+1)} . e_1^{-1} e_2^{k+1}, where A_{(-1,k+1)} is the kernel of theta_{k+1} on M-dagger_{-k}(K^p)/M_{-k}(K^p) with values in (M-dagger_{k+2}(K^p)/M_{k+2}(K^p)) tensor D_0^{-k-1}, and A_{(k,0)} sits in an exact sequence 0 -> colim_{K_p} H^1(X_{K^p K_p}, omega^{-k}) -> A_{(k,0)} -> M-dagger_{-k}(K^p) -> M-dagger_{k+2}(K^p) tensor D_0^{-k-1} with the last map theta_{k+1}. All maps are Hecke- and B-equivariant. The proof is the snake lemma applied to the commutative diagram of 4.4.10.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.13 and Lemma 4.4.14: the kernel of theta_{k+1} on overconvergent forms
items.statement: For k >= 0 the kernel of theta_{k+1} : M-dagger_{-k}(K^p) -> M-dagger_{k+2}(K^p) is M_{-k}(K^p); in particular theta_{k+1} is injective for k > 0. For k = 0 the operator is essentially the derivation, so its kernel on a strict neighbourhood of the canonical locus consists of the locally constant functions, which by the bijection on connected components are the global functions on the modular curve. For k >= 1 one uses the bound dim ker(theta_{k+1} on M-dagger_{-k}(K^p Gamma(p^n))) <= (k+1) times the number of connected components of X_{K^p Gamma(p^n)}, which depends only on the determinant level: away from the cusps, computing the kernel is solving a homogeneous linear ODE of order k+1 by Kodaira-Spencer. Taking the colimit over tame levels, each isotypic part for a smooth character of the ideles is a finite-dimensional smooth representation of GL_2(A_f^p), so the action factors through the determinant; a non-zero kernel would then produce a system of spherical Hecke eigenvalues whose two-dimensional p-adic Galois representation has consecutive Hodge-Tate weights, contradicting Theorem 1.1 of the author's earlier paper since the relevant weight gap k+1 exceeds 1.
items.locator: Lemma 4.4.13 and Lemma 4.4.14 with their proofs, pp. 46-47; the contradiction uses [Pan20, Theorem 1.1]
items.note: The ODE bound is the only place where the order of theta_{k+1} is used quantitatively, and the Galois-theoretic step is what upgrades a bound to a vanishing.

items.name: Theorem 4.4.15: the n-invariants are classical
items.statement: For chi = (0,k) there is a natural weight decomposition of the n-invariants of ker I^1_k into A_{(k,0)} . e_1^k and A_{(-1,k+1)} . e_1^{-1} e_2^{k+1}, where A_{(-1,k+1)} is the kernel of theta_{k+1} on M-dagger_{-k}/M_{-k} and embeds through theta_{k+1} into M_{k+2}(K^p) tensor D_0^{-k-1}, and A_{(k,0)} sits in a short exact sequence 0 -> colim_{K_p} H^1(X_{K^p K_p}, omega^{-k}) -> A_{(k,0)} -> M_{-k}(K^p) -> 0. All maps are Hecke- and B-equivariant. In particular the Hecke action on the n-invariants of ker I^1_k is classical: every system of Hecke eigenvalues appearing there comes from an automorphic form on GL_2(A).
items.note: Obtained from Proposition 4.4.12 by replacing the kernel of theta_{k+1} on overconvergent forms with M_{-k} using Lemma 4.4.13.

items.name: Remark 4.4.16: the shape of A_{(k,0)}
items.statement: For k > 0, A_{(k,0)} is exactly colim_{K_p} H^1(X_{K^p K_p}, omega^{-k}) because M_{-k}(K^p) = 0. For k = 0 the surjection onto M_0(K^p) has a natural GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant right inverse into H^1(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p}), so A_{(0,0)} = colim_{K_p} H^1(X_{K^p K_p}, O) + M_0(K^p).
items.locator: Remark 4.4.16, p. 47; the splitting is [Pan22, Corollary 5.1.3(2)] and the discussion before [Pan22, Theorem 5.3.16]

items.name: Remark 4.4.17: what a sharper description of A_{(-1,k+1)} would need
items.statement: A more precise description of A_{(-1,k+1)} amounts to understanding the cokernel of theta_{k+1} on the canonical locus, which is the H^1 of the de Rham complex of Sym^k D on the dagger space attached to the canonical locus, equivalently a rigid cohomology of the Igusa curve. Coleman determined the primitive part, and his result says roughly that the cokernel of theta_{k+1} is closely related to the finite slope part of classical modular forms.
items.locator: Remark 4.4.17, p. 47; the reference is Coleman
items.note: A concrete open end: the paper does not describe A_{(-1,k+1)} beyond embedding it into classical forms.

items.name: Corollary 4.4.18: finiteness of the analytic n-invariants
items.statement: Let K_p = 1 + p^l M_2(Z_p) with l >= 2. Then (1) the n-invariants of the K_p-analytic vectors of ker I^1_k are finite-dimensional, and (2) the subspace of n-finite vectors, those killed by some power of u_+, is a finitely generated U(g)-module. The idea: K_p-analytic vectors of a smooth representation are the K_p-fixed vectors, so the K_p-analytic vectors of M_{k+2}(K^p) are H^0(X_{K^p K_p}, omega^{k+2}), finite-dimensional since the curve is proper, and similarly for the H^1 term; it remains to see that the maps of Theorem 4.4.15 preserve K_p-analyticity. For A_{(k,0)} this follows from the locally algebraic inclusion, since Sym^k V is algebraic, giving that the intersection of the K_p-analytic vectors with H^1(Fl, omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p}) . e_1^k is H^1(X_{K^p K_p}, omega^{-k}) . e_1^k; for k = 0 the splitting of Remark 4.4.16 is used. For A_{(-1,k+1)} one shows instead that the kernel of H^0(V, omega^{k+2}) -> M-dagger_{k+2}/M_{k+2} is finite-dimensional, using Lemmas 4.4.19 and 4.4.20 to arrange that the preimage of V in every connected component at every deeper level is connected, so that a section in that kernel is fixed by Gamma(p^m) and hence comes from the finite-dimensional M_{k+2}(K^p Gamma(p^m)).
items.note: This is the source of Theorem 1.1.14, the finite-dimensionality of the n-invariants of the Gamma(p^n)-analytic vectors of Pi_rho.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.19: analytic vectors come from a fixed strict neighbourhood
items.statement: There are an integer m > 0 and an affinoid strict open neighbourhood V of the canonical locus X_{K^p Gamma(p^m),c} such that the K_p-analytic vectors inside M-dagger_{-k}(K^p)/M_{-k}(K^p) . e_1^{-1} e_2^{k+1} lie in the image of H^0(V, omega^{-k}). The proof uses Proposition 3.4.14 to put the K_p-analytic vectors of the cohomology inside a Cech group at some level Gamma(p^m), takes n-cohomology of the defining exact sequence of Definition 3.4.5, notes that only the U_2-term contributes in weight (-1,k+1) because the n-coinvariants are supported away from U_1, and then identifies the resulting evaluation map with the construction of the isomorphism between the sections over U_2 modulo the vanishing coordinate and M-dagger_{-k}(K^p): by Theorem 3.2.2 in the coordinate y = 1/x, an H-analytic section restricted to a small disc around infinity is e_2^k times a convergent power series in y, and the map sends it to the constant term.
items.locator: Lemma 4.4.19 with its proof, pp. 48-50; the inputs are [Pan22, Propositions 5.2.6, 5.2.10 and Lemma 5.2.9]

items.name: Lemma 4.4.20: connected components become connected deeper in the tower
items.statement: Let V be an affinoid subset of X_{K^p Gamma(p^m)} meeting each connected component either in the empty set or in a connected strict open neighbourhood of the canonical locus of that component, which is possible because Igusa curves are irreducible. Then there is m' >= m such that for every connected component V' of the preimage of V at level m' and every m'' >= m', the preimage of V' meets each connected component of X_{K^p Gamma(p^{m''})} in a connected set or not at all. The proof compares the profinite sets S_1 = lim_n pi_0 of the preimages of V and S_2 = lim_n pi_0(X_{K^p Gamma(p^n)}) with their Gamma(p^m)-actions; since the stabiliser of a point of S_2 is Gamma(p^m) cap SL_2(Z_p) and Gamma(p^m) acts transitively on S_1, the claim reduces to showing that sl_2(Q_p) acts trivially on the locally analytic functions on S_1, which is proved by evaluating the first-order differential equation (4.4.1) satisfied by locally analytic sections at three points with distinct coordinate values.
items.locator: Lemma 4.4.20 with its proof, pp. 49-51; the differential equation is [Pan22, Theorem 4.2.4]

items.name: Lemma 4.4.21: three classical points in each fibre
items.statement: For every s in S_1 the image under pi_HT of the fibre c^{-1}(s) contains at least three classical points, where c is the natural map from the preimage of V in X_{K^p} to S_1. It suffices to find three classical points of pi_HT(V_infinity) in distinct Gamma(p^m)-orbits: the point at infinity lies there since V contains a canonical locus; a classical point outside the canonical locus gives a non-rational classical point s_2 with positive infimum of the coordinate over its orbit; and applying [Pan22, Lemma 5.2.9] to a small disc produces a third one deeper in the tower.

items.name: Remark 4.4.22: a p-adic proof of the triviality of the SL_2-action on components
items.statement: The same argument gives a purely p-adic proof of the well-known fact that SL_2(Q_p) acts trivially on the colimit over K_p of the sets of connected components of the modular curves X_{K^p K_p}.

items.name: Section 4.4.3: the strategy for the n-invariants
items.statement: The n-invariants of ker I^1_k are computed as a subspace of the n-invariants of H^1(Fl, O^{la,chi}_{K^p}), which were determined in [Pan22, section 5.3]; the ingredient recalled for that purpose is Lemma 4.4.4.

items.name: The strategy of section 5: Newton stratification of the flag variety
items.statement: Section 5 computes ker I^1_k by using the Newton stratification Fl = P^1 = P^1(Q_p) union Omega, where Omega is the Drinfeld upper half plane, and computing the kernel and cokernel of I_k on each stratum. Throughout, for chi = (n_1,n_2) with n_2 - n_1 = k one has d_{k+1} and d'_{k+1} along the modular curve and d-bar_{k+1} and d-bar'_{k+1} along the flag variety, with I_k = d'_{k+1} after d-bar_{k+1} = d-bar'_{k+1} after d_{k+1}.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.2: the stalk at infinity is a completed tensor product with overconvergent forms
items.statement: Let infinity be the vanishing locus of e_1, with local coordinate y = e_1/e_2, so that the stalk of O_Fl at infinity is the colimit of the O_C[[y/p^n]][1/p], each a C-Banach space with the obvious unit ball, and the stalk of omega^{l,sm}_{K^p} is the space M-dagger_l(K^p) of overconvergent forms. Write the completed tensor product of these stalks for the colimit of the corresponding completed tensor products, so that its elements are the series sum_i c_i y^i with coefficients in omega^l(U) for a strict affinoid neighbourhood U of some canonical locus, with the c_i p^{mi} uniformly bounded for some m. Then the natural map is an isomorphism: the stalk of O^{la,(n_1,n_2)}_{K^p} at infinity is the stalk of omega^{n_2-n_1}_Fl completed-tensor M-dagger_{n_1-n_2}(K^p)(n_2-n_1) . t^{n_1}, and likewise the stalk of omega^{l,la,(n_1,n_2)}_{K^p} is the same with M-dagger_{n_1-n_2+l}. The proof writes a section near infinity as t^{n_1} e_2^{n_2-n_1} times a power series in y - y_n by Theorem 3.2.2, after applying the Weyl element, and shrinks the neighbourhood so that y_n = 0.
items.locator: Lemma 5.1.2 with its proof and the discussion of 5.1.1, pp. 52-53; essentially the proof of [Pan22, Proposition 5.2.10]

items.name: Proposition 5.1.4: the kernel of d_{k+1} on the rational points
items.statement: Identifying the stalk of d_{k+1} at infinity with 1 tensor theta_{k+1} through Lemma 5.1.2, Lemma 4.4.13 makes it injective for k >= 1, while for k = 0 the kernel of theta_1 at each finite level is the finite-dimensional space of classical weight-zero forms. Hence, since GL_2(Q_p) acts transitively on P^1(Q_p), the restriction of ker d_{k+1} to P^1(Q_p) vanishes for k >= 1, and ker d_1 restricted to P^1(Q_p) is O_Fl restricted there tensor M_0(K^p) . t^{n_1} (an ordinary tensor product).

items.name: Definition 5.1.6: the rigid cohomology of Igusa curves with Sym^k coefficients
items.statement: Define H^1_rig(Ig(K^p Gamma(p^n)), Sym^k) as the cokernel of theta_{k+1} from M-dagger_{-k}(K^p Gamma(p^n)) to M-dagger_{k+2}(K^p Gamma(p^n)) tensor D_0^{-k-1}, and H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) as the corresponding cokernel at infinite tame-p level; the latter is the colimit of the former and carries a natural smooth action of the Borel B. The twist by D_0^{-k-1} makes everything independent of the trivialisation of D_0. For k = 0 one writes H^1_rig(Ig(K^p)).
items.note: This is the object appearing in the main Theorem 1.1.10 for the principal series case; Coleman studied it and showed it is closely related to the finite slope part of classical modular forms.

items.name: Proposition 5.1.7: finite-dimensionality of that rigid cohomology
items.statement: H^1_rig(Ig(K^p Gamma(p^n)), Sym^k) is a finite-dimensional C-vector space. Coleman determined its dimension: the pair (Sym^k D, nabla_k) defines an overconvergent logarithmic F-isocrystal on the special fibre of the canonical locus, a union of Igusa curves, and the group in question is its log-rigid cohomology after extending coefficients, so the claim follows from the general finiteness theorem for rigid cohomology.
items.locator: Proposition 5.1.7 with its proof, p. 54; quoted from Coleman

items.name: Proposition 5.1.8: the cokernel of d_{k+1} at infinity
items.statement: The stalk of coker d_{k+1} at infinity is the stalk of omega^k_Fl tensor H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)(k) . t^{n_1}, an ordinary tensor product. By Proposition 5.1.7 the image of theta_{k+1} at each finite level is closed, so by the open mapping theorem the completed tensor product with the stalk of O_Fl has closed image with cokernel the completed tensor product with the finite-dimensional rigid cohomology; taking the colimit over n gives the claim.
items.locator: Section 5.1.5, Proposition 5.1.8 with its proof, p. 54

items.name: Section 5.1.9: the ordinary sheaf H^1_ord as a smooth induction
items.statement: Since B acts smoothly on H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k), its smooth induction to GL_2(Q_p) defines a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant sheaf on P^1(Q_p), written H^1_ord(K^p,k): with pi : GL_2(Q_p) -> P^1(Q_p) the orbit map of the point at infinity, its sections over an open U are the smooth functions on the preimage of U with values in the rigid cohomology satisfying f(bg) = b.f(g). Its global sections are the smooth induction of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) from B, and by abuse of notation it is also viewed as a sheaf on Fl through the closed embedding of P^1(Q_p). Roughly, it is the sheaf defined by the rigid cohomology of the ordinary locus of the modular curves.

items.name: Section 5.1.10: the characters e’_1 and e’_2 and locally analytic induction
items.statement: B acts on the fibre of omega^l_Fl at infinity through the l-th power of the character e'_2 sending an upper-triangular matrix to d, and e'_1 is the character sending it to a; these agree with e_2 and e_1 of 4.4.6 as characters of B but carry no Galois action, and W . (e'_2)^l denotes the corresponding twist. There is a Hausdorff LB-space structure on H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) . (e'_2)^l for which the B-action is locally analytic, and its locally analytic induction to GL_2(Q_p) defines a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant sheaf on P^1(Q_p) whose global sections are that induction; for the trivial coefficient the induction of (e'_2)^l is the restriction of omega^l_Fl to P^1(Q_p).

items.name: Corollaries 5.1.11 and 5.1.12: the cokernel sheaves on the rational points
items.statement: The restriction of coker d_{k+1} to P^1(Q_p) is the restriction of omega^k_Fl tensor H^1_ord(K^p,k)(k) . t^{n_1}, and its global sections over P^1(Q_p) are the locally analytic induction from B of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)(k) . (e'_2)^k t^{n_1}. For the twisted operator d'_{k+1} and chi = (-k,0), the restriction of coker d'_{k+1} to P^1(Q_p) is the restriction of omega^{-k-2}_Fl tensor H^1_ord(K^p,k)(k) tensor det^{k+1} . t^{-k}, with global sections the locally analytic induction of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)(k) . (e'_1)^{k+1} (e'_2)^{-1} t^{-k}.
items.note: The second form, with the character (e’_1)^{k+1} (e’_2)^{-1}, is the one that appears in Theorem 1.1.10.

items.name: Why the Lubin-Tate space enters
items.statement: On the Drinfeld upper half plane Omega the preimage under pi_HT is a finite disjoint union of the Lubin-Tate space at infinite level, so the geometry of the Hodge-Tate period map for that space is what is needed. The key point is that the operators d_{k+1} and d-bar_{k+1} are swapped under the isomorphism between the Lubin-Tate and Drinfeld towers, so the results already proved for d-bar_{k+1} in Proposition 4.2.9 apply to d_{k+1}.

items.name: The Lubin-Tate tower, the Gross-Hopkins period map and the Hodge filtration
items.statement: Let H_0 be the unique one-dimensional formal group of height 2 over F_p-bar. The functor sending a W(F_p-bar)-algebra with p nilpotent to the isomorphism classes of deformations (G, rho) of H_0, rho a quasi-isogeny, is represented by a formal scheme M, the disjoint union of the loci M^{(i)} of quasi-isogeny height i, each non-canonically Spf W(F_p-bar)[[T]]; M_LT and M^{(i)}_LT denote the base changes to Spa(C,O_C) of the generic fibres. The covariant Dieudonne crystal of the universal deformation gives a rank two bundle M(G) with integrable connection, trivialised by rho as M(H_0) tensor O, under which the connection is standard; the dual of the Lie algebra of G is the line bundle omega_{LT,0}. Grothendieck-Messing gives a surjection M(H_0) tensor O -> omega_{LT,0}^{-1} with line bundle kernel, hence the Gross-Hopkins period map pi_GM from M_LT to the flag variety Fl_GM of one-dimensional quotients of M(H_0) tensor C; it is etale, locally of finite type, and admits local sections, and the pull-back of the tautological ample bundle is omega_{LT,0}^{-1}. Dualising, D(G) carries the Hodge filtration with Fil^1 = omega_{LT,0}, satisfying Griffiths transversality, and the Kodaira-Spencer map KS is the usual composite.
items.locator: Section 5.2.2, pp. 55-56; the reference is Scholze-Weinstein section 6, with contravariant rather than covariant conventions, and Gross-Hopkins
items.note: The convention change relative to Scholze-Weinstein is flagged by the author: statements may differ from the reference.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.3: the Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism
items.statement: The Kodaira-Spencer map (5.2.1) for the universal deformation over the Lubin-Tate space is an isomorphism, by a standard computation on the Gross-Hopkins flag variety.
items.note: This is the one geometric input that makes the differential equation of Theorem 5.2.6 come out as a generator of the horizontal nilpotent subalgebra.

items.name: The Lubin-Tate tower at infinite level and its Hodge-Tate period map
items.statement: The universal G defines a rank two Z_p-local system on M_LT whose dual is V_LT, normalised as for modular curves; trivialising V_LT modulo p^n gives the GL_2(Z/p^n)-covering M_{LT,n}. By Scholze-Weinstein there is a perfectoid space M_{LT,infinity} with M_{LT,infinity} ~ lim_n M_{LT,n}, strictly the strong completion of the base change of their preperfectoid space, with a natural continuous right GL_2(Z_p)-action extending to GL_2(Q_p) through their p-adic Hodge-theoretic description; the present normalisation differs from the reference by g -> (g^{-1})^t. Writing omega_{LT,infinity} for the pull-back of omega_{LT,0}, trivialising the Tate module gives a surjection Z_p^2 tensor O -> omega_{LT,infinity}(-1) whose kernel is omega_{LT}^{-1} once a principal polarisation is chosen, hence a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant Hodge-Tate period map pi_{LT,HT} from M_{LT,infinity} to Fl whose image is exactly the Drinfeld upper half plane Omega, and the pull-back of omega_Fl along it is omega_{LT,infinity}(-1).
items.locator: Section 5.2.4, pp. 56-57; quoted from Scholze-Weinstein, Theorem 6.3.4 and Propositions 2.3.6, 6.3.9

items.name: The local setting: a Galois perfectoid cover and the horizontal subalgebras
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A,A^+) be an open affinoid of M_LT and X-tilde = Spa(B,B^+) its preimage in M_{LT,infinity}, so X is one-dimensional smooth over Spa(C,O_C) and X-tilde is a GL_2(Z_p)-Galois pro-etale perfectoid cover. By [Pan22, Theorem 3.1.2] the GL_2(Z_p)-locally analytic vectors B^{la} satisfy a first-order differential equation theta_{X-tilde} = 0 with theta_{X-tilde} in B tensor Lie G, the smallness assumption there being removable. The sheaves g_0, b_0, n_0 on Fl are the sections of O_Fl tensor gl_2(C) lying pointwise in the corresponding Borel and nilpotent subalgebras; g_0 acts on B^{la} through pi_{LT,HT}, hence so do b_0 and n_0, and n_0 is an invertible sheaf, locally generated by one differential operator.
items.locator: Section 5.2.5, p. 57; the differential equation is [Pan22, Theorem 3.1.2 and Remark 3.1.5]

items.name: Theorem 5.2.6: the differential equation is a generator of n_0
items.statement: For X-tilde as above, theta_{X-tilde} is a generator of n_0 up to a unit of B; equivalently B^{la} is annihilated by n_0. This follows from the corresponding statement for modular curves by embedding the height-zero Lubin-Tate space into a modular curve. The paper also gives a conceptual proof suggested by Michael Harris: choosing the standard two-dimensional representation, the Higgs field is computed from the variation of p-adic Hodge structure (D(G), nabla_LT); the dual Hodge-Tate sequence filters V tensor O with Fil^0 = omega_LT^{-1}, the Higgs field kills Fil^0 and induces on the quotient the unique B-linear extension of the Kodaira-Spencer map, which is an isomorphism by Proposition 5.2.3, so the Higgs field is a generator of n_0 up to a unit.
items.locator: Theorem 5.2.6 with its proof, pp. 57-58; the Higgs-field input is Liu-Zhu, Theorems 2.1 and 3.8
items.note: This is improvement (2) of 1.3.2: it replaces the computation of [Pan22, Theorem 4.2.7], which used a result of Faltings, by the statement that the differential equation is given by the Kodaira-Spencer class, an argument which works for general Shimura varieties. Footnote 3 of the paper states that the required compatibility between Liu-Zhu’s Higgs bundle and the Higgs field of [Pan22] "can be checked on a toric chart" and that details are deferred to future work, so the conceptual proof is not self-contained; the reduction to [Pan22] is.

items.name: The horizontal Cartan action and the coordinates on the Lubin-Tate side
items.statement: Given Theorem 5.2.6, the b_0-action on B^{la} factors through b_0/n_0 and the Cartan h acts through h -> O_Fl tensor h = b_0/n_0; this action is theta_{LT,h}, and the same construction gives an h-action on the locally analytic vectors of omega_{LT,infinity}. For coordinates, a principal polarisation gives a map from M_{LT,infinity} to the space of isomorphisms from Z_p to Z_p(1), and a choice of generator of Z_p(1) makes 1 a global section t of the structure sheaf; there are t_n at finite level factoring through the components with |t - t_n| <= p^{-n}. The images e_1, e_2 of the standard basis in H^0(omega_{LT,infinity}) make x = e_2/e_1 a coordinate on Fl which is invertible on M_{LT,infinity}, equivalently e_1 is invertible, precisely because the image of pi_{LT,HT} is Omega. With G_n = Gamma(p^n) one finds, for each n, an integer r(n) and elements x_n, e_{1,n}, t_n at level r(n) approximating x, e_1, t to within p^{-n}, so that the logarithms of e_1/e_{1,n} and t/t_n converge.
items.locator: Sections 5.2.7 and the list on pp. 58-59; following [Pan22, sections 4.3.1 and 4.3.5]

items.name: Theorem 5.2.8: power-series description of the locally analytic vectors on the Lubin-Tate side
items.statement: For every n >= 0 and every family of sections c_{i,j,k} at level G_{r(n)} whose norms times p^{(n-1)(i+j+k)} are uniformly bounded, the triple series with terms c_{i,j,k} (x-x_n)^i (log(e_1/e_{1,n}))^j (log(t/t_n))^k converges in the G_{r(n)}-analytic vectors of B, and every G_n-analytic vector of B arises this way. The proof is the same as [Pan22, Theorem 4.3.9].
items.note: The two extra logarithmic variables, absent from Theorem 3.2.2, are what the infinite-level Lubin-Tate space contributes.

items.name: The quaternion algebra acting on the tower
items.statement: Let O_{D_p} = End(H_0) and D_p its rationalisation, a non-split quaternion algebra over Q_p; its unit group is the group of self-quasi-isogenies of H_0 and acts on the right on M_LT and on Fl_GM, and choosing a basis of the Dieudonne module identifies D_p^* with a subgroup of GL_2(C) and Fl_GM with P^1, the action being linear. The action is continuous in the sense of Scholze-Weinstein, pi_GM is equivariant, the left action on the Dieudonne module tensor C is irreducible and on its determinant is the reduced norm. The coverings M_{LT,n} are D_p^*-equivariant and so is M_{LT,infinity}, and omega_{LT,0} and its pull-backs are equivariant line bundles; pi_{LT,GM} denotes the composite of the projection with pi_GM, equivariant for GL_2(Q_p) x D_p^* with GL_2(Q_p) acting trivially on Fl_GM. The centres of GL_2(Q_p) and of D_p^* act in the same way. For X stable under a compact open K of D_p^*, B^{D_p^*-la} denotes the K-locally analytic vectors, independent of K.
items.locator: Section 5.2.9, p. 59; the continuity statements are Scholze-Weinstein Proposition 6.5.5 and Gross-Hopkins Proposition 19.2

items.name: Corollary 5.2.10 and Remark 5.2.11: one inclusion between the two notions of analyticity
items.statement: B^{la} is contained in B^{D_p^*-la}. Indeed, the affinoid at level r(n) is of finite type, so a small subgroup 1 + p^m O_{D_p} acts trivially modulo p on the integral level-r(n) sections and hence analytically; D_p^* acts trivially on x and e_1 and through the reduced norm on t, so after shrinking, the analytic norms agree with the ambient ones, and every element of the shape given by Theorem 5.2.8 is analytic for that subgroup. The converse inclusion is Corollary 5.3.9, proved by swapping the roles of the two groups. All of this holds equally when X is an open affinoid of M_{LT,n} for some n.
items.locator: Corollary 5.2.10 with its proof and Remark 5.2.11, pp. 59-60

items.name: The sheaves on the Drinfeld upper half plane from the height-zero Lubin-Tate space
items.statement: Let M^{(0)}_{LT,infinity} be the preimage of the height-zero locus, stable under GL_2(Q_p)^0 x O_{D_p}^*, where GL_2(Q_p)^0 is the subgroup with determinant in Z_p^*, and let pi^{(0)}_{LT,HT} be the restriction of the period map to Omega. Embedding Lubin-Tate spaces into modular curves and invoking [Sch15, Theorem III.1.2] gives a basis B of open affinoids of Omega whose preimages are affinoid perfectoid and are pulled back from finite level, so the earlier local results apply. Set O_LT to be the push-forward of the structure sheaf, a GL_2(Q_p)^0-equivariant sheaf on Omega with an O_{D_p}^*-action, and O^{la}_LT its subsheaf of GL_2(Q_p)^0-locally analytic sections; by Theorem 5.2.6 it is annihilated by n_0, so h acts through theta_{LT,h} and O^{la,chi}_LT denotes the chi-isotypic part.

items.name: Section 5.2.13: locally algebraic sections on the Lubin-Tate side
items.statement: For chi = (n_1,n_2) with k = n_2 - n_1 >= 0, Theorem 5.2.8 makes t^{n_1} e_1^i e_2^{k-i} s a section of O^{la,chi}_LT for smooth s and 0 <= i <= k; the subsheaf they span is O^{lalg,chi}_LT, consisting exactly of the GL_2(Z_p)-locally algebraic vectors, equivalently the image of H^0(Fl, omega^k_Fl)(k) tensor omega^{-k,sm}_LT . t^{n_1}, and as a GL_2(Z_p)-representation it is Sym^k V(k) tensor omega^{-k,sm}_LT . t^{n_1}.

items.name: The smooth sheaves and the derivation on the Lubin-Tate side
items.statement: Let O^{sm}_LT be the subsheaf of GL_2(Q_p)^0-smooth sections, equivalently the push-forward of the colimit of the pull-backs from finite level, an O_Omega-module; similarly omega^{la}_LT, omega^{sm}_LT and their tensor powers, all modules over O^{sm}_LT tensor O_Omega. Let Omega^1_LT be the corresponding colimit of the sheaves of differentials, non-canonically isomorphic to omega^{2,sm}_LT by Kodaira-Spencer, with derivation d_LT. As in 4.1.2 the (k+1)-st power of d_LT gives a map from omega^{-k,sm}_LT to its twist by (Omega^1_LT)^{k+1}.

items.name: Theorem 5.2.15: the operator d_{k+1} on the supersingular locus
items.statement: For chi = (n_1,n_2) integral with k = n_2 - n_1 >= 0 there is a unique natural continuous operator d^{k+1}_LT from O^{la,chi}_LT to its twist by (Omega^1_LT)^{k+1} such that (1) it is O_Omega-linear and (2) it sends t^{n_1} e_1^i e_2^{k-i} s to t^{n_1} e_1^i e_2^{k-i} (d_LT)^{k+1}(s) for every smooth section s of omega^{-k,sm}_LT and every 0 <= i <= k. This is the restriction of Theorem 4.1.4 to the supersingular locus, proved by repeating section 4.1 with the Lubin-Tate data.

items.name: Theorem 5.2.16: the operator d-bar_{k+1} on the supersingular locus, with kernel and image
items.statement: For the same chi there is a natural continuous operator d-bar^{k+1}_LT from O^{la,chi}_LT to its twist by (Omega^1_Omega)^{k+1}, formally the (k+1)-st power of the derivation of Omega, such that (1) it is O^{sm}_LT-linear and (2) for a non-zero rational constant c it sends s to c (u_+)^{k+1}(s) tensor (dx)^{k+1}. Moreover it is surjective, commutes with GL_2(Z_p), and its kernel is exactly O^{lalg,chi}_LT.

items.name: What the next subsection will do
items.statement: The kernel and cokernel of d^{k+1}_LT admit a description parallel to Theorem 5.2.16, obtained by swapping the roles of GL_2(Q_p) and D_p^*; this is carried out in Subsection 5.3.

items.name: The plan: transport everything through the Lubin-Tate-Drinfeld isomorphism
items.statement: To study the action of D_p^* on M_{LT,infinity} one uses the isomorphism between the Lubin-Tate and Drinfeld spaces at infinite level; all the results of the previous subsection hold for the Drinfeld tower by the same arguments.
items.locator: Section 5.3.1, p. 62; the historical remarks are those following Theorem E of Scholze-Weinstein

items.name: The Drinfeld tower, its Dieudonne crystal and Gross-Hopkins map
items.statement: Let H_1 be a special formal O_{D_p}-module over F_p-bar, unique up to isogeny and isomorphic to H_0 x H_0 as a formal group. The functor of deformations (G',rho') of H_1 by special formal O_{D_p}-modules is pro-represented by a formal scheme M', whose generic fibre base changed to C is M_Dr, the disjoint union of the degree loci M^{(i)}_Dr. The covariant Dieudonne crystal of the universal deformation is a rank four bundle with D_p-action and integrable connection, trivialised by rho'. The Lie algebra of G' gives a rank two bundle, and Grothendieck-Messing a D_p-equivariant surjection from the trivialised crystal onto it, inducing the Gross-Hopkins map pi'_GM from M_Dr to the flag variety Fl'_GM of two-dimensional D_p-equivariant quotients of the four-dimensional space; Drinfeld proved that it is an isomorphism onto its image on the degree-zero part, Fl'_GM is naturally P^1 and the image is exactly Omega. Dualising gives the Hodge filtration on D(G') and again a Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism, easily checked on Omega.
items.locator: Section 5.3.2, p. 62; the references are Drinfeld, Boutot-Carayol and Gross-Hopkins

items.name: The Drinfeld tower at infinite level and its Hodge-Tate period map
items.statement: The universal G' defines a rank four Z_p-local system with D_p-action whose dual is V_Dr; trivialising it as O_{D_p}/p^n gives the coverings M_{Dr,n}, and by Scholze-Weinstein there is a perfectoid M_{Dr,infinity} ~ lim_n M_{Dr,n} with a continuous right O_{D_p}^*-action extending to D_p^*. Fixing an isomorphism of End(H_1) tensor Q with M_2(Q_p) makes GL_2(Q_p) the group of self-quasi-isogenies of H_1, acting continuously on the whole tower and on Fl'_GM; pi_{Dr,GM} is the composite with pi'_GM and is GL_2(Q_p) x D_p^*-equivariant for the trivial D_p^*-action on Fl'_GM. Trivialising the Tate module gives a D_p-equivariant surjection O_{D_p} tensor O -> the dual of the Lie algebra bundle twisted by (-1), with kernel the Lie algebra bundle after choosing a principal polarisation, hence the Hodge-Tate period map pi_{Dr,HT} to the flag variety Fl' of two-dimensional D_p-equivariant quotients of O_{D_p} tensor C.
items.locator: Section 5.3.3, pp. 62-63; quoted from Scholze-Weinstein, Theorem 6.5.4

items.name: Theorem 5.3.4: the Lubin-Tate-Drinfeld duality
items.statement: There are natural GL_2(Q_p) x D_p^*-equivariant isomorphisms M_{LT,infinity} = M_{Dr,infinity}, Fl = Fl'_GM and Fl' = Fl_GM, under which pi_{LT,HT} is identified with pi_{Dr,GM} and pi_{Dr,HT} with pi_{LT,GM}, and the height-zero loci correspond. In particular the image of pi_{LT,HT} is Omega, and there is a natural isomorphism omega_{LT,infinity}(-1) = omega_{Dr,infinity}^{-1}, both being pull-backs of omega_Fl.
items.locator: Theorem 5.3.4, p. 63; quoted from Scholze-Weinstein, Proposition 7.2.2 and Theorem 7.2.3
items.note: This is the duality that swaps the two differential operators, which is the mechanism behind the whole spectral decomposition.

items.name: The local setting on the Drinfeld side and the horizontal subalgebras for D_p^*
items.statement: Let Y be an open affinoid of M_Dr whose preimage Y-tilde = Spa(B,B^+) in M_{Dr,infinity} has pi_{Dr,HT}(Y-tilde) not all of Fl', hence contained in an affinoid; such Y form a basis, because GL_2(Q_p) acts transitively on the fibres of pi_{LT,GM}, so it suffices to take Y missing some point up to translation. Then Y is one-dimensional smooth and Y-tilde is an O_{D_p}^*-Galois pro-etale perfectoid cover, so by [Pan22, Theorem 3.1.2] the D_p^*-locally analytic vectors satisfy a first-order differential equation. A point of Fl' corresponds to a two-dimensional D_p-stable subspace of D_p tensor C, equivalently to a Borel subalgebra of C tensor Lie D_p^*, which defines the sheaves g^0_{D_p}, b^0_{D_p} and n^0_{D_p} on Fl', acting on the locally analytic vectors as before.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.6: the differential equation on the Drinfeld side
items.statement: For Y-tilde as above, the differential operator annihilating the D_p^*-locally analytic vectors is a generator of n^0_{D_p} up to a unit; the proof is that of Theorem 5.2.6, the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism holding for the Drinfeld tower as well.

items.name: The action theta_{Dr,h} and coordinates on the Drinfeld side
items.statement: By Theorem 5.3.6 the quotient b^0_{D_p}/n^0_{D_p} acts; fixing an isomorphism of C tensor Lie D_p^* with gl_2(C) identifies Fl with Fl' and gives an action theta_{Dr,h} of h, independent of the chosen isomorphism, and similarly on the locally analytic vectors of omega_{Dr,infinity}. The global section t may be reused since O_{D_p}^* acts on it through the reduced norm. Taking W_p the unique two-dimensional irreducible representation of D_p inside D_p tensor C, the bundle of D_p-homomorphisms into the Lie algebra bundle has an inverse pull-back omega_{Dr,*}, and omega_{Dr,infinity} is the pull-back of the tautological bundle on Fl' along pi_{Dr,HT}. Choosing a basis f_1, f_2 of its global sections with f_1 invertible on Y-tilde makes y = f_2/f_1 invertible, and with H_n = 1 + p^n O_{D_p} one finds levels r(n) and approximations y_n, f_{1,n}, t'_n to within p^{-n}.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.8: power-series description on the Drinfeld side
items.statement: For every n >= 0 and coefficients at level H_{r(n)} whose norms times p^{(n-1)(i+j+k)} are uniformly bounded, the triple series in (y - y_n), log(f_1/f_{1,n}) and log(t/t'_n) converges in the H_{r(n)}-analytic vectors, and every H_n-analytic vector arises this way; the proof is that of [Pan22, Theorem 4.3.9].

items.name: Corollary 5.3.9: the two notions of local analyticity coincide
items.statement: For B as in 5.3.5, the GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic vectors and the D_p^*-locally analytic vectors of B coincide. One inclusion is Corollary 5.2.10 and the other follows from Theorem 5.3.8 by the same argument with the roles of the groups exchanged; the mismatch in which tower the affinoid comes from is handled by covering Y by affinoids of M_Dr.
items.note: Remark 5.3.10 says the proof rests on explicit calculations and that a more intrinsic proof would be conceptually satisfying; Remark 5.3.11 records that Dospinescu and Rodriguez Camargo obtained the same result independently.

items.name: Remarks 5.3.10 and 5.3.11: the status of Corollary 5.3.9
items.statement: The proof of Corollary 5.3.9 relies on explicit calculations and it would be interesting to have a more intrinsic proof; the author was informed by Gabriel Dospinescu that the result was also obtained by himself and Juan Esteban Rodriguez Camargo.

items.name: The sheaves of D_p^*-smooth sections
items.statement: On the sheaf level, by Corollary 5.3.9 the sheaf O^{la}_LT is also the subsheaf of O_{D_p}^*-locally analytic sections, and one defines the subsheaf of O_{D_p}^*-smooth sections, concretely the colimit over n of the push-forwards along the Gross-Hopkins maps of the structure sheaves of the M^{(0)}_{Dr,n}. Writing omega_LT and omega_Dr for the push-forwards of the two automorphic bundles, one defines their locally analytic, smooth and D_p^*-smooth subsheaves likewise, and the isomorphism omega_{LT,infinity}(-1) = omega_{Dr,infinity}^{-1} induces isomorphisms among them. The action theta_{Dr,h} acts on all of these.

items.name: Corollary 5.3.13 and Lemma 5.3.14: the two Cartan actions agree
items.statement: theta_{LT,h} = theta_{Dr,h} on O^{la}_LT. Since the centres act the same way it suffices to compare the actions of the coroot h, and since both are first-order differential operators it suffices to compare them on the level-r(n) sections, on x, on e_1/e_{1,n} and on t, which Theorem 5.2.8 shows generate. For t both actions factor through the determinant, respectively the reduced norm. The remaining cases are Lemma 5.3.14: (1) both actions vanish on the smooth and on the D_p^*-smooth structure sheaves; (2) theta_{LT,h}(h) vanishes on omega^{sm}_LT and is -1 on the D_p^*-smooth part; (3) symmetrically for theta_{Dr,h}(h). The proofs use that theta_{LT,h} vanishes on O_Fl - seen by writing Fl as a double quotient so that the action comes from the infinitesimal action of the diagonal torus - and that sections of the D_p^*-smooth sheaf are analytic functions on finite etale covers of Omega, together with the computation that the action is -1 on omega_Fl.
items.locator: Corollary 5.3.13 and Lemma 5.3.14 with their proofs, p. 66; the direct calculation is [Pan22, 5.1.1]
items.note: The author notes that the natural proof should use the moduli interpretations of the two towers; the proof given is by explicit calculation.

items.name: Section 5.3.15: D_p^*-locally algebraic sections
items.statement: For a character chi of h, O^{la,chi}_LT is the isotypic subsheaf for theta_{LT,h} = theta_{Dr,h}. For chi = (n_1,n_2) with k = n_2 - n_1 >= 0, Theorem 5.3.8 makes t^{n_1} f_1^i f_2^{k-i} s a section for D_p^*-smooth s, and the subsheaf they span is the sheaf of O_{D_p}^*-locally algebraic vectors, equivalently the image of H^0(Fl', omega^k_{Fl'}) tensor the D_p^*-smooth part of omega^k_LT twisted by t^{n_1}.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.17: the operator d-bar on the Drinfeld side
items.statement: For chi = (n_1,n_2) with k = n_2 - n_1 >= 0 there is a natural continuous operator d-bar^{k+1}_Dr from O^{la,chi}_LT to its twist by (Omega^1_LT)^{k+1}, formally the (k+1)-st power of the derivation of Fl', which is (1) linear over the D_p^*-smooth structure sheaf and (2) given, on an affinoid Y of Omega with a basis f_1, f_2 of the global sections of the tautological bundle such that f_1 generates omega_Dr on Y, by c (u'_+)^{k+1}(s) tensor (dy')^{k+1} for a non-zero rational c, where y' = f_2/f_1 and u'_+ is the unique nilpotent element of Lie D_p^* tensor C carrying f_2 to f_1. Moreover it is surjective, commutes with O_{D_p}^*, and its kernel is exactly the D_p^*-locally algebraic subsheaf, that is H^0(Fl', omega^k_{Fl'}) tensor the D_p^*-smooth part of omega^k_LT twisted by t^{n_1}. In this Drinfeld picture the roles of O_Omega and Omega^1_Omega are played by the smooth structure sheaf and Omega^1_LT, and a choice of basis is needed since the global sections of the tautological bundle on Fl' have no canonical one.

items.name: Remark 5.3.18: the unused operator d on the Drinfeld side
items.statement: Although not needed, one can also redo the construction of Theorem 5.2.15 and obtain a unique natural continuous operator d^{k+1}_Dr on O^{la,chi}_LT, linear over the D_p^*-smooth structure sheaf, extending the (k+1)-st power of the derivation into the colimit Omega^1_Dr of the sheaves of differentials on the M^{(0)}_{Dr,n}.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.20 and Corollary 5.3.21: the two operators agree, and the kernel of d
items.statement: Since u'_+ is the derivation with respect to y' on Fl' and hence on its etale coverings, d-bar^{k+1}_Dr satisfies the characterising properties of d^{k+1}_LT up to a unit, so by the uniqueness in Theorem 5.2.15 one gets d-bar^{k+1}_Dr = c' d^{k+1}_LT for some non-zero rational c'. Consequently d^{k+1}_LT is surjective and its kernel is the D_p^*-locally algebraic subsheaf, H^0(Fl', omega^k_{Fl'})(k) tensor the D_p^*-smooth part of omega^{-k}_Dr twisted by t^{n_1}.
items.note: This is the formal statement of the swap promised in 1.2.12: the kernel of the modular-curve operator on the supersingular locus consists of the functions that are smooth for the quaternion group, that is of automorphic functions.

items.name: The supersingular uniformization setup
items.statement: The supersingular locus of the modular curves is uniformised by Lubin-Tate towers, and the preimage of Omega under pi_HT is a finite disjoint union of the height-zero Lubin-Tate space at infinite level; Deligne used this in his proof of the local Langlands correspondence for GL_2, relating the supercuspidal part of the l-adic cohomology of modular curves to that of Lubin-Tate towers through Jacquet-Langlands, and the same picture appears here with l-adic cohomology replaced by completed cohomology. Concretely, let E_0 be a supersingular elliptic curve over F_p-bar with p-divisible group H_0, fix such an isomorphism, and let D = End(E_0) tensor Q, a quaternion algebra ramified exactly at p and infinity, so that D tensor Q_p = D_p. Fix an isomorphism of the first etale cohomology of E_0 with coefficients in the away-from-p adeles with the standard rank two module, converting the natural right D-action into a left action by the main involution; this identifies D tensor A_f^p with M_2(A_f^p) and makes K^p a compact open of the quaternion group.
items.locator: Section 5.4.1, p. 68; the uniformization is used as in Deligne’s proof

items.name: Theorem 5.4.2: the uniformization theorem at infinite level
items.statement: There is a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism between pi_HT^{-1}(Omega) and the quotient by D^* of the product of M_{LT,infinity} with the coset space of the away-from-p quaternion adeles modulo K^p, functorial in K^p, identifying pi_HT with pi_{LT,HT} on the first factor and omega_{K^p} restricted to Omega with the pull-back of omega_LT; here D^* acts diagonally through the main involution into D_p^* and the natural embedding away from p. The proof: pi_HT^{-1}(Omega) is the preimage of the supersingular locus at level GL_2(Z_p) by [Sch15, Lemma III.3.6]; the supersingular locus at level Gamma(p^n) is uniformised by M_{LT,n} by Rapoport-Zink, and one passes to the limit, using that all supersingular elliptic curves are isogenous to E_0 and Serre-Tate theory. The main involution in the embedding is tracked explicitly, since the normalisation differs from the reference.
items.locator: Theorem 5.4.2 with its proof, pp. 68-69; quoted from [Sch15, Lemma III.3.6] and Rapoport-Zink, Theorem III and 6.13

items.name: Lemma 5.4.4: the preimage of Omega is a finite disjoint union of Lubin-Tate spaces
items.statement: The double coset space of the quaternion adeles modulo K^p carries a free action of the units of O_{D_p}, because K^p lies in a level-N subgroup with N >= 3 prime to p, so that the relevant intersections are finite hence trivial; by finiteness of the class group one may write the adeles as a finite union of cosets. The resulting map from the disjoint union over that finite index set of copies of M^{(0)}_{LT,infinity} to the uniformised space is an isomorphism, GL_2(Q_p)^0-equivariantly: pi_HT^{-1}(Omega) is the disjoint union of finitely many copies of M^{(0)}_{LT,infinity}. The proof rewrites M_{LT,infinity} as a quotient of a product by D_p^* and then as a quotient of the height-zero part by the units.
items.locator: Section 5.4.3 and Lemma 5.4.4 with its proof, p. 69

items.name: Corollaries 5.4.6 and 5.4.7: d_{k+1} is surjective on Omega and the cokernel is supported on the rational points
items.statement: The uniformization identifies O_{K^p} restricted to Omega with the direct sum of copies of O_LT, hence after taking locally analytic vectors identifies theta_h with theta_{LT,h} and the restriction of d_{k+1} with d^{k+1}_LT; so the surjectivity of the latter, Corollary 5.3.21, gives that d_{k+1} is surjective on Omega. Therefore coker d_{k+1} is supported on P^1(Q_p) and, by Corollaries 5.1.11 and 5.1.12, for chi = (-k,0) one has coker d_{k+1} = omega^k_Fl tensor the pushforward of H^1_ord(K^p,k)(k) . t^{-k}, coker d'_{k+1} the corresponding twist, and the global sections are the locally analytic inductions of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)(k) with characters (e'_2)^k t^{-k} and (e'_1)^{k+1}(e'_2)^{-1} t^{-k} respectively.

items.name: Corollary 5.4.8 and Remark 5.4.9: I^1_k is surjective
items.statement: The cokernel of I_k is supported on P^1(Q_p), and I^1_k is surjective: the first cohomology of a sheaf supported on the profinite set P^1(Q_p) vanishes, and since Fl is one-dimensional taking H^1 is right exact. It is worth observing that the two-term complex I_k has H^1 supported on the zero-dimensional P^1(Q_p) and H^0 supported on at most a one-dimensional set, a perversity condition.
items.locator: Corollary 5.4.8 with its proof and Remark 5.4.9, p. 70

items.name: Section 5.4.10: the kernel of d_{k+1} as equivariant maps
items.statement: Writing X_{K^p} for the double coset space of the quaternion adeles modulo K^p, isomorphic to a finite disjoint union of copies of the units of O_{D_p}, the proof of Lemma 5.4.4 exhibits pi_HT^{-1}(Omega) as the quotient of the product of M^{(0)}_{LT,infinity} with X_{K^p} by those units acting through the inverse main involution. Hence O_{K^p} restricted to Omega is the sheaf of equivariant maps from X_{K^p} to O_LT, and likewise ker d_{k+1} restricted to Omega is the equivariant maps into ker d^{k+1}_LT.

items.name: Definition 5.4.11: quaternionic automorphic forms
items.statement: For chi = (n_1,n_2) with n_2 - n_1 >= 0, let W_{(-n_1,-n_2)} be the dual of the irreducible algebraic representation of D_p^* of highest weight (n_2,n_1), which is H^0(Fl', omega^k_{Fl'}) . t^{n_1}. Then (1) A_{D,-chi} is the space of maps from the double coset space of the quaternion adeles to W_{(-n_1,-n_2)} that are equivariant for some compact open away from p and at p, the space of quaternionic forms on the quaternion group over the adeles, with smooth actions of the away-from-p group by right translation and of D_p^*; (2) A^1_{D,-chi} is the subspace of maps factoring through the reduced norm, non-zero only when n_1 = n_2; and (3) A^c_{D,-chi} is the quotient, the Hecke action giving a natural splitting of A_{D,-chi} as the sum of the two.

items.name: Proposition 5.4.12 and Remark 5.4.13: the kernel on Omega is quaternionic forms
items.statement: There is a Hecke- and GL_2(Q_p)^0-equivariant isomorphism identifying ker d_{k+1} restricted to Omega with the units-of-O_{D_p} invariants of the K^p-invariant quaternionic forms A_{D,(-n_1,-n_2)} tensor the D_p^*-smooth part of omega^{-k}_Dr, twisted by (n_2) and by the n_1-st power of the character sending x to |det x| det x; the invariants are for the diagonal action, through Definition 5.4.11 on the forms and through the inverse main involution on the bundle. The proof identifies equivariant maps with the invariants of smooth maps, uses that the action on the bundle is smooth hence locally finite to split off the coefficient, and tracks the Tate twists coming from the Galois and Hecke actions on t. The isomorphism extends to a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant one after replacing the bundle by the direct sum over the integers of its copies, on which O_{D_p}^* x GL_2(Q_p)^0 extends to D_p^* x GL_2(Q_p).
items.locator: Proposition 5.4.12 with its proof and Remark 5.4.13, pp. 71-72
items.note: This is the supercuspidal half of the main theorem in embryo: the sections of the kernel over the supersingular stratum are exactly quaternionic automorphic forms, which is what Jacquet-Langlands then converts into automorphic forms on GL_2.

items.name: Propositions 5.4.15 and Corollary 5.4.16: the global kernel of d_{k+1} and of d’_{k+1}
items.statement: Let j be the open embedding of Omega and j_! extension by zero. Combining Proposition 5.1.4 with Proposition 5.4.12: for k >= 1, ker d_{k+1} is j_! of the quaternionic-forms sheaf of Proposition 5.4.12; and ker d_1 is the direct sum of j_! of the same sheaf with A^c in place of A - the cuspidal part - and of O_Fl tensor M_0(K^p), suitably twisted. Twisting by (Omega_Fl)^{k+1} gives the analogous descriptions of ker d'_{k+1} and ker d'_1. For k = 0 the extra argument is that the image of O_Omega tensor M_0(K^p) inside the invariants is exactly the part built from A^1, using the identification of A^1 with M_0(K^p) as smooth functions on the same double coset space of ideles and the fact that each isotypic part of O_LT for a smooth character of the units is O_Omega.
items.locator: Section 5.4.14, Proposition 5.4.15 with its proof and Corollary 5.4.16, pp. 72-73

items.name: Remark 5.4.17: the uniform reading of all these kernels and cokernels
items.statement: For k = 0 the complex d_1 computes the de Rham cohomology of the fibres of the Hodge-Tate period map: over Omega each fibre is a profinite set by the uniformization theorem, so only degree zero contributes; over P^1(Q_p) the fibre is related to the Igusa curve and one is computing its de Rham cohomology, which is Propositions 5.1.4 and 5.1.8. For d-bar the analogous statement is that one computes the de Rham cohomology of the fibres of the projection from the infinite-level curve to level GL_2(Z_p), again profinite, so that the cokernel vanishes.

items.name: Two factorisations, two decompositions
items.statement: ker I^1_k is decomposed twice, once through I_k = d'_{k+1} after d-bar_{k+1} and once through I_k = d-bar'_{k+1} after d_{k+1}; the two give different views and comparing them is informative.

items.name: Lemma 5.5.2: the filtration coming from the first factorisation
items.statement: There are natural short exact sequences 0 -> ker H^1(d-bar_{k+1}) -> ker I^1_k -> ker H^1(d'_{k+1}) -> 0 and 0 -> H^1(Fl, ker d'_{k+1}) -> ker H^1(d'_{k+1}) -> H^0(coker d'_{k+1}) -> 0, and an isomorphism of ker H^1(d'_{k+1}) with the first hypercohomology of the two-term complex d'_{k+1}. The first uses the surjectivity of d-bar_{k+1}; the second uses that H^0 of the target of d'_{k+1} vanishes and applies Lemma 4.4.4 with Remark 4.4.5.
items.locator: Lemma 5.5.2 with its proof, pp. 73-74; the vanishing is [Pan22, Corollary 5.1.3]

items.name: The abbreviation epsilon for the twist by t
items.statement: Since G_{Q_p} acts on t through the cyclotomic character and GL_2(A_f) through epsilon composed with the determinant, t(-1) is that character as a representation of GL_2(A_f) x G_{Q_p}; epsilon is written for the twist by t(-1).

items.name: Theorem 5.5.4: the three-step filtration of ker I^1_k
items.statement: For chi = (-k,0) there is a natural increasing filtration on ker I^1_k, trivial in degrees <= 0 and everything from degree 3 on, with graded pieces: in degree 1, ker H^1(d-bar_{k+1}) = Sym^k V tensor H^1(omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p}) . epsilon^{-k}; in degree 2, H^1(ker d'_{k+1}), which is the units-of-O_{D_p} invariants of H^1(j_! of the D_p^*-smooth part of omega^{k+2}_Dr) tensor the quaternionic forms A_{D,(k,0)}, twisted by det^{k+1} and by epsilon_p^{-k}; and in degree 3, H^0(coker d'_{k+1}), the locally analytic induction from B of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) twisted by epsilon^{-k}(e'_1)^{k+1}(e'_2)^{-1}. For k = 0 the same holds with the first piece H^1(O^{sm}_{K^p}), the second built from the cuspidal part A^c plus a copy of M_0(K^p), and the third the induction of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p)) twisted by e'_1 (e'_2)^{-1}. All isomorphisms are Hecke- and GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant.
items.note: The proof needs the vanishing of H^0 of the target of d-bar_{k+1}, which follows because H^0(j_! omega^{k+2,sm}_Dr) = 0 - every connected component of M_{Dr,n} surjects onto Omega - and H^0(Fl, Omega_Fl) = 0.

items.name: The spherical Hecke algebra and the spectra of classical forms
items.statement: Let S be a finite set of primes containing p with K_l maximal outside S, T_l and S_l the usual double coset operators, and T^S the Z_p-algebra they generate; it acts on O^{la}_{K^p} and commutes with theta_h, I_k, d_{k+1} and d-bar_{k+1}, all of which are defined at p. The action of T^S on the classical forms M_k(K^p) is semisimple, giving an eigenspace decomposition, and its spectrum is written sigma^{K^p}_k, with sigma^{K^p}_{k,n} for the spectrum on M_k(K^p) . t^n. For k >= 2 there is also a decomposition of H^1(Fl, omega^{2-k,sm}_{K^p}) = colim_{K_p} H^1(X_{K^p K_p}, omega^{2-k}) indexed by systems of eigenvalues attached to cuspidal automorphic representations whose infinitesimal character at infinity matches the algebraic representation of highest weight (k-2,0), a subset of sigma^{K^p}_{k,k-1}, seen from the Hodge-Tate decomposition of the etale cohomology with Sym^{k-2} coefficients. On the quaternionic forms the Hecke action is semisimple by Jacquet-Langlands, and for k >= 1 the decomposition of A_{D,(k,0)} is indexed by cuspidal representations with the matching infinitesimal character and with pi_p special or supercuspidal, a subset of sigma^{K^p}_{k+2,1}; for k = 0 an eigenform either factors through the reduced norm, hence transfers to a weight-zero form, or transfers to a cuspidal eigenform of weight 2.

items.name: Theorem 5.5.7: the generalized eigenspace decomposition of ker I^1_k
items.statement: For chi = (-k,0) there are natural generalized eigenspace decompositions of ker I^1_k indexed by sigma^{K^p}_{k+2,1} for k >= 1, and by the union of sigma^{K^p}_{2,1} and sigma^{K^p}_0 for k = 0. By Theorem 5.5.4 it suffices to decompose each graded piece; the first two are handled by 5.5.5, and for the third one uses that H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) is a colimit of finite-dimensional Hecke-stable spaces, so a generalized eigenspace decomposition exists, and then bounds its spectrum. The bound is the interesting step: if a system lambda were outside the expected set then Fil^2 would vanish on it and the whole generalized eigenspace would be the H^0 of the cokernel, whose n-invariants are non-zero by Lemma 5.5.8; but Theorem 4.4.15 says the n-invariants of ker I^1_k are classical, forcing lambda to appear in classical forms of weight k+2 or in weight -k, a contradiction.
items.locator: Theorem 5.5.7 with its proof, pp. 76-77; alternatively the third piece can be handled by Coleman or by work on the l-adic cohomology of Igusa curves with independence of l
items.note: This is Theorem 1.2.3 of the introduction, the statement that implies the main classicality theorem once the intertwining operator is identified with the Fontaine operator.

items.name: Lemma 5.5.8: the cokernel has non-zero n-invariants
items.statement: The n-invariants of H^0(Fl, the generalized lambda-eigenspace of coker d'_{k+1}) are non-zero. Since the sheaf is supported on the profinite set P^1(Q_p) it suffices to look at the stalk at the zero of e_2, where it is the stalk of omega^{-k-2}_Fl tensor H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)(k) . t^{-k}, and the n-invariants of that stalk of the line bundle are a line.

items.name: Corollary 5.5.9: the decomposition for the variant I’_0
items.statement: The kernel of I'_0, the map induced by I^1_0 on the Banach cohomology, decomposes into generalized eigenspaces indexed by the union of sigma^{K^p}_{2,1} and sigma^{K^p}_0, because it is a quotient of ker I^1_0.

items.name: Section 5.5.10: the de Rham complex DR_k and its Hodge filtration
items.statement: Since ker I^1_k = ker H^1(d_{k+1}), consider the two-term de Rham complex DR_k given by d_{k+1} on O^{la,(-k,0)}_{K^p}. The decreasing filtration with Fil^1 the target alone filters the hypercohomology, and ker H^1(d_{k+1}) = H^1(DR_k) modulo Fil^1 H^1(DR_k), with Fil^1 H^1(DR_k) = coker H^0(d_{k+1}) by Remark 4.4.5.

items.name: Lemma 5.5.11 and Definition 5.5.12: the Hodge filtration is classical forms
items.statement: (1) H^0(d_{k+1}) = 0, since H^0 of the source vanishes for k non-zero and equals M_0(K^p) . t^{n_1}, killed by d_1, otherwise; hence Fil^1 H^1(DR_k) is H^0 of the target. (2) That H^0 is naturally Sym^k V tensor M_{k+2}(K^p)(k) tensor D_0^{-k-1} . t^{-k}, induced by the locally algebraic inclusion. The resulting map i_H from that space into H^1(DR_k) is what describes the Hodge filtration on the de Rham cohomology of the modular curves; since D_0^{-1}(1) . t^{-1} = M_0(K^p) tensor det^{-1}, it can also be written with the dual of V as a map from Sym^k V^* tensor M_{k+2}(K^p) tensor D_0^{-1}.
items.locator: Lemma 5.5.11 with its proof and Definition 5.5.12, p. 78, with Remark 5.6.12

items.name: Proposition 5.5.13: the two-step description of H^1(DR_k)
items.statement: There is a natural exact sequence exhibiting H^1(DR_k) as an extension: the sub is the units-of-O_{D_p} invariants of H^1(j_! of the D_p^*-smooth part of omega^{-k}_Dr) tensor the cuspidal quaternionic forms A^c_{D,(k,0)}, twisted by epsilon_p^{-k}; the quotient is H^0 of the ordinary sheaf tensor omega^k_Fl twisted by epsilon^{-k}, which is the locally analytic induction from B of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) twisted by epsilon^{-k}(e'_2)^k.

items.name: Corollary 5.5.14: the eigenspaces in the supercuspidal and principal series cases
items.statement: Let lambda in sigma^{K^p}_{k+2,1} correspond to a cuspidal automorphic representation pi. (1) If pi_p is supercuspidal then H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) . t^{-k}[lambda] = 0 by Corollary 5.6.11, and the generalized eigenspace of ker I^1_k is the quaternionic term of Proposition 5.5.13 at lambda modulo the image of i_H; in particular the generalized eigenspace is the honest eigenspace, and Theorem 5.5.4 gives a short exact sequence expressing it as an extension of the invariants term by Sym^k V tensor H^1(omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p}) . epsilon^{-k}[lambda]. (2) If the cuspidal quaternionic part vanishes at lambda, that is pi_p is a principal series, then the generalized eigenspace is the locally analytic induction of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) twisted by epsilon^{-k}(e'_2)^k at lambda modulo the image of i_H, again an honest eigenspace, with the corresponding short exact sequence.
items.note: These two cases are exactly Theorems 1.1.7 and 1.1.10 of the introduction, before the p-adic Hodge theory of section 6 is used to replace I^1_k by the Fontaine operator.

items.name: Remark 5.5.15: the special case is expected but not proved directly
items.statement: The equality of generalized eigenspace and eigenspace is expected to hold when pi_p is special as well; it can be proved using Emerton's local-global compatibility together with work on the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p), and a direct proof would be very interesting. In both cases treated, what is actually proved is that H^1(DR_k)[lambda] is its own generalized eigenspace and that ker I^1_k[lambda] is H^1(DR_k)[lambda] modulo Fil^1.
items.note: An explicit open end of the paper, and the reason Remark 1.1.12 says the special case gives a slightly weaker result.

items.name: Remark 5.5.16: a uniform sheaf-theoretic reading and the analogy with Kashiwara-Schmid
items.statement: The two terms of Proposition 5.5.13 can be written uniformly: viewing the cuspidal quaternionic forms as a C-local system L_ss on the etale site of Omega and the restriction of omega^k_Fl as a sheaf there, with nu the projection from the etale to the analytic site, the sub is H^1(Fl, j_! nu_*(L_ss tensor the restriction of omega^k_Fl)); and with L_ord the ordinary local system on P^1(Q_p), the quotient is H^0(Fl, i_!(L_ord tensor the restriction of omega^k_Fl)), where i_* = i_!. This is very close to Kashiwara-Schmid's geometric constructions of representations of real groups on the flag variety. These representations should be regarded as objects of the classical local Langlands correspondence, in that they do not see the Hodge filtration, which suggests that a p-adic local Langlands correspondence may need a filtered equivariant derived category on the flag variety.
items.note: The paper’s own suggestion about what the right home for a p-adic local Langlands correspondence might be; worth carrying into any roadmap brief.

items.name: Section 5.5.6: the module D_0 in explicit terms
items.statement: By 4.2.3, D_0 = M_0(K^p) . c where GL_2(A_f) acts on the generator c through the inverse adelic norm of the determinant.

items.name: The complex D_k and the semisimplicity of its Hecke action
items.statement: For k >= 0 let D_k be the two-term complex given by theta_{k+1} on omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p}. The inclusion into the k-th symmetric power of the dual smooth de Rham bundle induces a quasi-isomorphism of D_k with the de Rham complex of that bundle. The vanishing of H^0(theta_{k+1}) and of H^1(omega^{k+2,sm}_{K^p}) gives a natural exact sequence 0 -> H^0 of the target -> H^1(D_k) -> H^1(omega^{-k,sm}_{K^p}) -> 0 and H^2(D_k) = 0, and H^1(D_k) is the colimit of the de Rham cohomologies of Sym^k D^* at finite level. Since that bundle is defined over Q, the Shimura isomorphism for its complex fibre shows the Hecke action of T^S on H^1(D_k) is semisimple.

items.name: Section 5.6.3: the exact triangle and the snake lemma sequence
items.statement: With DR_k the de Rham complex of d_{k+1} and DR'_k that of d'_{k+1}, Remark 4.2.8 makes d-bar_{k+1} into an exact triangle from D_k tensor Sym^k V . epsilon^{-k} to DR_k to DR'_k. Since H^0(DR'_k) = 0, one gets 0 -> H^1(D_k) tensor Sym^k V . epsilon^{-k} -> H^1(DR_k) -> H^1(DR'_k) -> 0; combining with the kernel-cokernel sequences for both complexes and applying the snake lemma to the map induced by d-bar_{k+1} gives the four-term exact sequence (5.6.1) relating ker SS_k, H^1(D_k) tensor Sym^k, ker ORD_k and coker SS_k, where SS_k and ORD_k are the maps induced by d-bar_{k+1} on the kernel and cokernel terms.
items.locator: Section 5.6.3, p. 80 with the displayed sequence (5.6.1)

items.name: Lemma 5.6.4: the kernel of the ordinary map
items.statement: ker ORD_k = Sym^k V tensor the locally analytic induction from B of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) . epsilon^{-k}. Indeed, by Corollary 5.4.7 the two cokernels are omega^k_Fl and omega^{-k-2}_Fl tensor det^{k+1} tensored with the ordinary sheaf, and ORD_k is induced by d-bar_{k+1} between those line bundles, whose kernel is H^0(Fl, omega^k_Fl) = Sym^k V tensor C.

items.name: Definition 5.6.5: compactly supported de Rham cohomology of the Drinfeld tower
items.statement: Let DR_dR be the complex given by the derivation from the D_p^*-smooth structure sheaf to Omega^1_Dr, the latter being omega^{2}_Dr twisted by det via Kodaira-Spencer. Define H^i_{dR,c} of the height-zero Drinfeld tower at infinite level as the hypercohomology of j_! applied to that complex; since only H^1 of each term is non-zero, it is the (i-1)-st cohomology of the induced map H^1(j_! of the structure sheaf) -> H^1(j_! Omega^1_Dr).

items.name: Lemma 5.6.6: identification of the supersingular map, its kernel and cokernel
items.statement: There is a natural morphism of complexes from the two-term complex given by d-bar_{k+1} on the D_p^*-smooth part of omega^{-k}_Dr to Sym^k V tensor DR_dR which is a quasi-isomorphism admitting a left inverse; the reason is that the centre of U(g) acts on the target and only the isotypic part for the infinitesimal character of omega^k_Fl is non-zero, where it is exactly the source. Applying j_! and Proposition 5.4.15 with Corollary 5.4.16 identifies SS_k with the map induced by H^1(d-bar_{k+1}) on the quaternionic-forms description, and gives ker SS_k = the units-invariants of H^1_{dR,c} tensor the cuspidal quaternionic forms, tensored with Sym^k V and twisted, while coker SS_k is the corresponding expression with H^2_{dR,c} and the full quaternionic forms for k >= 1, with an extra summand M_0(K^p) when k = 0.

items.name: Theorem 5.6.7: the p-adic vanishing-cycle exact sequence
items.statement: For k >= 1 there is a natural exact sequence 0 -> the units-invariants of H^1_{dR,c} tensor A_{D,(k,0)} -> H^1(D_k) -> the locally analytic induction from B of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) -> the units-invariants of H^2_{dR,c} tensor A_{D,(k,0)} -> 0; for k = 0 the same with the cuspidal quaternionic forms and an extra summand M_0(K^p) in the last term. The proof feeds Lemmas 5.6.4 and 5.6.6 into the sequence (5.6.1) and removes the factor Sym^k V by taking GL_2(Q_p)-smooth parts after tensoring with its dual.
items.note: This is the paper’s second, independent proof that the spectrum of the Igusa rigid cohomology is classical, and it is what Corollary 5.6.11 is deduced from.

items.name: Remark 5.6.8: the analogy with the l-adic vanishing cycle sequence
items.statement: Theorem 5.6.7 is a p-adic analogue of the usual vanishing cycle exact sequence in the l-adic case. It can also be obtained as the hypercohomology of the exact triangle relating j_! of the restriction of D_k to Omega, D_k itself, and i_* i^* D_k: the last computes the induction of the rigid cohomology of the Igusa curves, and the first computes the compactly supported de Rham cohomology of the supersingular locus, essentially that of the Lubin-Tate towers, the comparison with the Drinfeld side using the theorem of Colmez-Dospinescu-Niziol that the two towers have the same compactly supported de Rham cohomology.
items.locator: Remark 5.6.8, p. 82; the references are Carayol and [CDN20, Theoreme 4.4]
items.note: The appeal to Colmez-Dospinescu-Niziol is what licenses reading the supersingular term as Drinfeld rather than Lubin-Tate cohomology.

items.name: Section 5.6.9: why the notation is compactly supported de Rham cohomology
items.statement: Defining H^i_{dR,c} at finite level by the same recipe, the infinite-level group is the colimit. Since the finite-level Drinfeld spaces are partially proper, the higher cohomology of the structure sheaf and of the differentials vanishes, so the de Rham cohomology is the naive one, and Serre duality gives H^i_dR dual to H^{2-i}_{dR,c}; the finiteness of the morphism to Omega identifies the H^1 of j_! of the pushforward with the compactly supported H^1 of Colmez-Dospinescu-Niziol. Since H^0_dR is the continuous functions on the set of connected components, H^2_{dR,c} is finite-dimensional.

items.name: Lemma 5.6.10: the top compactly supported cohomology is abelian
items.statement: The action of GL_2(Q_p)^0 on H^2_{dR,c} of the height-zero Drinfeld tower at infinite level factors through the determinant, and the action of the units of O_{D_p} factors through the reduced norm.

items.name: Corollary 5.6.11: the Igusa eigenspaces are honest and the local component is not supercuspidal
items.statement: Let lambda correspond to a cuspidal automorphic representation pi of GL_2 over the adeles and suppose the generalized lambda-eigenspace of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) is non-zero. Then (1) it is the honest eigenspace, and (2) pi_p is either a principal series or special. The proof uses the exact sequence of Theorem 5.6.7 at lambda: the outer terms carry semisimple Hecke actions, so failure of semisimplicity in the middle would force the last term to contain a full induction from B, contradicting Lemma 5.6.10; and the same lemma shows the induction receives a non-zero map from pi_p, so pi_p is a principal series or special, the character case being excluded either by genericity or because it would put a special representation into the top compactly supported cohomology.
items.note: This is exactly what Corollary 5.5.14 needed: in the supercuspidal case the Igusa contribution vanishes, so the eigenspace is entirely quaternionic.

items.name: Remark 5.6.12: the Hodge filtration is the classical one
items.statement: By Lemma 5.5.11 the natural map from H^1(D_k) to H^1(DR_k) identifies the two Fil^1 terms, so the inclusion of Fil^1 H^1(DR_k) into H^1(DR_k) describes exactly the position of the Hodge filtration on H^1(D_k), the de Rham cohomology of the modular curves.
items.note: This is what makes the uniform formulation of Remark 1.1.13 - a quotient by Fil^1 of a de Rham cohomology - literally the classical Hodge filtration.

items.name: The period ring B^+_dR and Fontaine’s t
items.statement: Let O_{C-flat} be the tilt of O_C and A_inf its Witt vectors, with the surjection theta to O_C sending a Teichmuller lift to its first coordinate, and its rational version to C. B^+_dR is the completion of A_inf[1/p] along the kernel of theta: a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field C, filtered by the powers of that kernel, and by Hensel every finite extension K of Q_p in C lifts canonically into it, compatibly with the Galois action. Fixing a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, equivalently a generator of Z_p(1), the element [epsilon] - 1 generates the kernel and t = log[epsilon] is Fontaine's 2 pi i, on which G_{Q_p} acts through the cyclotomic character; the graded pieces are canonically C(k).

items.name: Banach B^+_dR/(t^k)-modules and their graded pieces
items.statement: B^+_dR/(t^k) is a Q_p-Banach algebra with unit ball the image of A_inf. A Q_p-Banach space W is a Banach B^+_dR/(t^k)-module if it carries a module structure whose multiplication is jointly continuous; it is filtered by the t^i W, with graded pieces W_i. If W is flat over B^+_dR/(t^k) then each t^i W is closed, being the kernel of multiplication by t^{k-i}, so each W_i is a C-Banach space and W_i = W_0(i).

items.name: The standing assumptions and the decompleted pieces
items.statement: Fix a finite extension K of Q_p in C.
