For W a Banach B^+_dR/(t^k)-module with continuous semilinear G_K-action, W^K_i denotes the G_{K_infinity}-fixed G_K-analytic vectors of W_i, a K-Banach space, with comparison map phi^K_i into W_i. The standing assumptions are that W is flat over B^+_dR/(t^k) and that phi^K_0 is an isomorphism; Tate's normalised trace then gives L tensor_K W^K_0 = W^L_0 for every finite extension L, so phi^L_0 is an isomorphism too. Finally W^K denotes the G_{K_infinity}-fixed G_K-analytic vectors of W itself, a filtered K-Banach space, with natural injections g^K_i from gr^i W^K into W^K_i.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.5: Fontaine’s generalisation of Sen theory
items.statement: Let W be a flat Banach B^+_dR/(t^k)-module with continuous semilinear G_K-action such that phi^K_0 is an isomorphism. Then there is a finite extension K' of K inside K_infinity such that (1) g^{K'}_i is an isomorphism for all i >= 0 and (2) the same holds for every finite extension L of K', so that L tensor_{K'} W^{K'} = W^L. The proof is an induction on k using Lemma 6.1.6.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.6 and Lemma 6.1.7: surjectivity of decompletion and an essentially-zero statement
items.statement: For W as in Proposition 6.1.5 and j >= 0: (1) the map from the G_{K_infinity}-invariants of W to those of W/t^j W is surjective, because t^j W is filtered by the W_i and H^1_cont(G_{K_infinity}, W_i) = H^1_cont(G_{K_infinity}, C) completed-tensor W^K_i = 0 by Tate's classical vanishing and Proposition 2.3.3; and (2) the image of W^{K_n} in (W/t^j W)^{K_n} contains (W/t^j W)^K for some n. The second reduces to Lemma 6.1.7, that the transition map in H^1_cont of the completed tensor product with analytic functions is eventually zero, which is proved by writing the completion of K_infinity as the sum of the kernel of Tate's normalised trace and K_n, using that the inverse of gamma - 1 has norm tending to 1 on that kernel, and the classical vanishing of the transition map on the K_n-part.
items.locator: Lemma 6.1.6 and Lemma 6.1.7 with their proofs, pp. 85-86; the Ax-Sen-Tate theorem and [BC08, 4.1] are used, and the norm estimate follows [Pan22, Lemma 3.6.6]

items.name: Proposition 6.1.8: kernels and cokernels of strict maps
items.statement: Let f : X -> Y be a continuous B^+_dR/(t^k)-linear G_K-equivariant map of flat Banach modules with phi^K_0 an isomorphism on both, and suppose f is strict topologically and strict for the t-adic filtrations, that is f(t^i X) = f(X) cap t^i Y. Then ker f and coker f are flat, their phi^K_0 are isomorphisms, and there is a finite extension L of K in K_infinity for which 0 -> (ker f)^L -> X^L -> Y^L -> (coker f)^L -> 0 is exact. The proof uses the filtration-strictness to get exactness on graded pieces and then Corollary 3.3.4.

items.name: Definition 6.1.9 and 6.1.10: Hodge-Tate B^+_dR/(t^k)-representations of weights 0 and l
items.statement: W is Hodge-Tate of weights 0, l, for l >= 1, if W_0 is Hodge-Tate of weights 0, l in the sense of Definition 3.3.6, that is if over some finite extension the Sen operator acts semisimply on the decompletion with eigenvalues 0 and -l. One then decomposes W^L_0 and hence W_0 into the two eigenspaces, independently of L, and likewise each W_i = W_{i,0} + W_{i,-l} = W_{0,0}(i) + W_{0,-l}(i); the Sen operator acts on W^L_{i,j} by i+j, so the Lie algebra acts trivially exactly on W^L_{0,0} and on W^L_{l,-l}(l).

items.name: Lemma 6.1.11: no extension of K is needed in the Hodge-Tate case
items.statement: If W is a flat Banach B^+_dR/(t^k)-module with continuous semilinear G_K-action which is Hodge-Tate of weights 0, l, then W_0 = C completed-tensor_K W^K_0 and every g^K_i is an isomorphism. One reduces by induction to the exactness of 0 -> (tW)^{K_n} -> W^{K_n} -> W^{K_n}_0 -> 0 after passing to Gal(K_infinity/K)-analytic vectors, which follows by decomposing W^{K_n} into generalized eigenspaces for a topological generator, the eigenvalues being cyclotomic characters raised to the powers i+j.

items.name: Sections 6.1.12 and Definition 6.1.13: the Fontaine operator
items.statement: Let k >= 1 and let W be a flat Banach B^+_dR/(t^{k+1})-module with continuous semilinear G_K-action, Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k. By Lemma 6.1.11, W^K is filtered with graded pieces the W^K_{i,0} and W^K_{i,-k}. Let nabla be the bounded operator on W^K given by the action of 1 in the Lie algebra of Gal(K_infinity/K), and E_0(W^K) the generalized eigenspace for the eigenvalue 0; there is a natural exact sequence 0 -> W^K_{k,-k} -> E_0(W^K) -> W^K_{0,0} -> 0 on whose outer terms nabla acts trivially, so nabla induces a K-linear map from W^K_{0,0} to W^K_{k,-k}. Its C-linear extension N_W : W_{0,0} -> W_{0,-k}(k) is the Fontaine operator; it is independent of K and commutes with the G_K-action.

items.name: Remark 6.1.14: functoriality of the Fontaine operator
items.statement: The Fontaine operator is functorial: a continuous C-linear G_K-equivariant map between two such modules intertwines their Fontaine operators.

items.name: Section 6.1.15: the case of a two-dimensional Galois representation
items.statement: Let V be a two-dimensional representation of G_{Q_p} over a finite extension E, Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k, which here means that the G_{Q_p}-invariants of V tensor C and of V tensor C(k) are both non-zero. Set W = V tensor B^+_dR/(t^{k+1}), a finite free module, with the Banach structure given by a lattice, independent of the choice. Then W_0 = V tensor C splits into the two one-dimensional pieces on which G_{Q_p} acts through the corresponding powers of the twisted cyclotomic character, so E_0(W^{Q_p}) has E-dimension 2. Comparing with Fontaine's paper, E_0(W^{Q_p}) is his D_pdR(V) and the restriction of nabla is his -nu.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.16: N_W vanishes exactly for de Rham representations
items.statement: Let V be a two-dimensional continuous representation of G_{Q_p} over a finite extension with Hodge-Tate weights 0 and k > 0, and W = V tensor B^+_dR/(t^{k+1}). Then N_W = 0 if and only if V is de Rham. Proof sketch: V is de Rham iff D_dR(V) has dimension 2; since the invariants of V tensor C(l) vanish for l > k, D_dR(V) injects into E_0(W^{Q_p}), and equality of dimensions forces G_{Q_p} to act trivially, so N_W = 0. Conversely if N_W = 0 then W^{G_{Q_p}} = E_0(W^{Q_p}), and since the kernel of B^+_dR/(t^l) tensor V -> W is filtered by positive Tate twists of C, which have vanishing H^1_cont, the invariants agree for all l > k, so passing to the limit gives dimension 2.
items.locator: Theorem 6.1.16 with its proof, p. 90; quoted from Fontaine
items.note: This is the criterion that converts the geometric computation of the paper into the classicality Theorem 1.1.2.

items.name: Section 6.1.17: the LB-space version
items.statement: The construction extends to Hausdorff LB-modules: let W be the colimit of an increasing sequence of Banach B^+_dR/(t^{k+1})-modules with continuous semilinear G_K-actions and continuous equivariant linear transition maps, assumed Hausdorff and flat over B^+_dR/(t^{k+1}), the individual terms not required to be flat. Then W_0 = W/tW is again Hausdorff, W^K and W^K_0 are defined as before, and W is called Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k if the comparison map for W_0 is an isomorphism and the Sen operator acts semisimply with eigenvalues 0 and -k, the completed tensor product being interpreted through a presentation of W^K_0 as an increasing union of K-Banach subspaces. The eigenspace decompositions of W_0 and of each W_i follow as before.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.18: decompletion in the LB setting
items.statement: For W as in 6.1.17 and Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k, the maps gr^i W^K -> W^K_i are isomorphisms for all i >= 0, and W^L = W^K tensor_K L for every finite extension L of K in C. The key point is to write W_0 as an increasing union of C-Banach Hodge-Tate representations, use Proposition 2.1.5 to interleave those with the graded pieces of the W^j, and then repeat the arguments of Proposition 6.1.5 and Lemma 6.1.11.

items.name: Section 6.1.19: the Fontaine operator in the LB setting
items.statement: With W as in 6.1.17 and Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k, the same construction applies: nabla acts on W^K, the generalized eigenspace E_0(W^K) sits in an exact sequence with W^K_{k,-k} and W^K_{0,0}, and nabla induces the Fontaine operator N_W from W_{0,0} to W_{0,-k}(k), functorially in W.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.20 and Corollary 6.1.21: exactness and compatibility with the Fontaine operators
items.statement: Let f : X -> Y be a continuous B^+_dR/(t^k)-linear G_K-equivariant map of Hausdorff flat LB-modules with the comparison maps isomorphisms, and assume X and Y are increasing unions of G_K-stable Banach submodules that are Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k, that f maps the n-th term to the n-th term strictly, that coker f is Hausdorff, and that f is strict for the t-adic filtrations. Then ker f and coker f are again Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k and flat, their comparison maps are isomorphisms, and 0 -> (ker f)^K -> X^K -> Y^K -> (coker f)^K -> 0 is exact. Consequently the four Fontaine operators of ker f, X, Y and coker f form a commutative diagram of two exact rows.
items.locator: Proposition 6.1.20 and Corollary 6.1.21 with their proofs, pp. 91-92
items.note: This is the tool that transports the Fontaine operator along the exact sequences produced in section 5.

items.name: The relative period sheaves B^+_dR on the infinite-level modular curve
items.statement: The sheaf A_inf on X_{K^p} assigns to an affinoid perfectoid open the Witt vectors of the tilt of its ring of integral elements, with the surjection theta onto the integral structure sheaf and its rational version; B^+_dR on X_{K^p} is the completion of A_inf[1/p] along the kernel of theta, and the inclusion of C gives a map from the absolute B^+_dR, whose element t also generates the relative kernel, so that the t-adic filtration has graded pieces the Tate twists of the structure sheaf. Pushing forward along pi_HT gives B^+_dR on Fl with gr^i = O_{K^p}(i), and one works with the truncations B^+_{dR,k} = B^+_dR/(t^k). For U in B, the sections over U form a flat Banach B^+_dR/(t^k)-module whose unit ball is the image of A_inf, GL_2(Q_p) acts, and B^{+,la}_{dR,k} denotes the subsheaf of locally analytic sections with its induced filtration; as in 3.3.1, G_K acts on the sections for a suitable finite extension K. The Lie algebra acts on the locally analytic subsheaf, and for an infinitesimal character chi~ of the centre Z of the enveloping algebra, B^{+,la,chi~}_{dR,k} is the isotypic part, with natural maps from its graded pieces to the twists of O^{la,chi~}_{K^p}.
items.locator: Section 6.2.1, pp. 92-93; the reference is [Sch13, section 6 and Lemma 6.3]

items.name: Lemma 6.2.2: the graded pieces are what they should be, and flatness
items.statement: For i = 0,...,k-1 the natural maps gr^i B^{+,la}_{dR,k} -> O^{la}_{K^p}(i) and gr^i B^{+,la,chi~}_{dR,k} -> O^{la,chi~}_{K^p}(i) are isomorphisms; in particular both sheaves are flat over B^+_dR/(t^k). Locally, the first reduces to the LA-acyclicity of the sections of O_{K^p}; the second reduces to the vanishing of the higher Ext groups over Z against the character, which is computed by a Koszul complex after Harish-Chandra identifies the action of Z with a subalgebra of a polynomial ring in two variables, the needed vanishing over the symmetric algebra being [Pan22, Lemma 5.1.2(1)].
items.locator: Lemma 6.2.2 with its proof, pp. 93-94; the acyclicity is [Pan22, Proposition 4.3.15] and the Cartan action is [Pan22, Corollary 4.2.8]

items.name: Section 6.2.3: the infinitesimal character chi~_k and the two weight spaces
items.statement: Harish-Chandra's isomorphism identifies the centre of the enveloping algebra with the Weyl invariants of the symmetric algebra of h for the dot action, so an infinitesimal character is a Weyl orbit in the dual of h. For k >= 1, chi~_k is the orbit {(0,1-k),(-k,1)}, the infinitesimal character of the (k-1)-st symmetric power of the dual of the standard representation. On the chi~_k-isotypic part the horizontal Cartan action satisfies an explicit quadratic relation, giving a natural decomposition of O^{la,chi~_k}_{K^p} as the sum of O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p} and O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}; by Proposition 3.3.8 these are Hodge-Tate of weights 0 and k respectively, so the isotypic part is Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k.

items.name: Sections 6.2.4 and Definition 6.2.5: the Fontaine operator N_k on the sheaves
items.statement: For U in B the module B^{+,la,chi~_k}_{dR,k+1}(U) satisfies all the assumptions of 6.1.17, so the construction of 6.1.19 gives a Fontaine operator from O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}(U) to O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}(U)(k); by functoriality these glue to a map of sheaves N_k : O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p} -> O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}(k).

items.name: Theorem 6.2.6: the intertwining operator is the Fontaine operator
items.statement: For every positive integer k, N_k = c_k I_{k-1} for some non-zero scalar c_k in Q_p. Remark 6.2.7 notes that one could show c_k is rational but this is not needed.
items.locator: Theorem 6.2.6 and Remark 6.2.7, p. 94, proved in Subsections 6.3 to 6.5, with Remark 6.5.13
items.note: This is the main theorem of Section 6 and Theorem 1.2.10 of the introduction: the geometric operator built from two differential operators on the perfectoid modular curve is Fontaine’s monodromy operator up to a scalar.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.9 and Corollary 6.2.10: strictness of the Cech complex for the period sheaves
items.statement: The restriction B^+_{dR,k}(U_1) -> B^+_{dR,k}(U_{12}) is a closed embedding and is strict for the t-adic filtrations, both claims following from Lemma 3.4.2 because the graded pieces are the Tate twists of O_{K^p}. Hence by Lemma 3.4.3 the Cech complex of the cover {U_1,U_2} is strict both topologically and for the t-adic filtrations.
items.locator: Section 6.2.8, Lemma 6.2.9 and Corollary 6.2.10 with their proofs, pp. 94-95

items.name: Corollary 6.2.11: the same after taking analytic vectors and isotypic parts
items.statement: The maps on G_n-analytic chi~-isotypic vectors and on locally analytic isotypic sections are closed embeddings, the latter also strict for the t-adic filtrations by Lemma 6.2.2, so the corresponding Cech complexes are strict, the locally analytic one also filtration-strict.

items.name: Definition 6.2.12 and Proposition 6.2.13: the cohomology of the period sheaves
items.statement: For F any of B^+_{dR,k}, its G_n-analytic isotypic subsheaf or its locally analytic isotypic subsheaf, define the Cech cohomology of the cover {U_1,U_2}; these are Banach B^+_dR/(t^k)-modules in the first two cases and the locally analytic one is the colimit, an LB-module. For F = B^+_{dR,k} and its locally analytic isotypic part these Cech groups compute H^*(Fl, F), the groups are flat over B^+_dR/(t^k), the t-adic filtration has gr^i H^*(Fl,F) = H^*(Fl, gr^i F), and H^*(Fl, B^{+,la,chi~}_{dR,k}) is Hausdorff - the last because its graded pieces are filtered by the H^* of the weight sheaves, which are Hausdorff by Proposition 3.4.11.
items.locator: Definition 6.2.12 and Proposition 6.2.13 with its proof, pp. 95-96

items.name: Corollary 6.2.15: on cohomology, the Fontaine operator is I^1_{k-1}
items.statement: Taking chi~ = chi~_k and applying Proposition 6.1.20 to the Cech complex, H^1(Fl, B^{+,la,chi~_k}_{dR,k+1}) is Hodge-Tate of weights 0, k and satisfies the assumptions of 6.1.17, and its Fontaine operator agrees up to a non-zero scalar in Q_p with I^1_{k-1} : H^1(Fl, O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}) -> H^1(Fl, O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}(k)). This is a direct consequence of Theorem 6.2.6 and Corollary 6.1.21.
items.locator: Section 6.2.14 and Corollary 6.2.15 with its proof, p. 96

items.name: Section 6.2.16 and Proposition 6.2.17: comparison with the Banach cohomology
items.statement: Since B^+_{dR,k+1} is filtered by the LA-acyclic sheaves O_{K^p}(i), the locally analytic vectors of its cohomology agree with the cohomology of its locally analytic subsheaf. More precisely, for k >= 2 one has H^1(Fl, B^{+,la,chi~_k}_{dR,k+1}) = H^1(Fl, B^+_{dR,k+1})^{la,chi~_k}; for k = 1 there is an exact sequence with the first and last terms the Ext^1 and Ext^2 over Z of chi~_1 against H^0(Fl, B^+_{dR,2})^{la}. The Ext terms vanish for k >= 2 because H^0(Fl, B^{+,la}_{dR,k+1}) is filtered by the twists of H^0(Fl, O^{la}_{K^p}), on which sl_2(Q_p) acts trivially by its relation with the completed cohomology.
items.locator: Section 6.2.16 and Proposition 6.2.17 with its proof, p. 96; following the proofs of [Pan22, Theorem 4.4.6 and Corollary 5.1.3], and using Theorem 7.2.3 below
items.note: The k = 1 discrepancy is the same phenomenon as the exact sequence (3.4.1): it is why the introduction has to treat k = 1 separately and why only the lambda_tau-isotypic statement is claimed there.

items.name: Section 6.3.1: the strategy, and the case k = 1
items.statement: Since I_{k-1} is the composite of d-bar'_k after d_k, the proof factorises N_k as a composite of two maps and identifies each with one of the two differential operators. The mechanism is to replace B^+_{dR,k+1} by a resolution given by the Poincare lemma sequence 0 -> B^+_dR -> OB^+_dR -> OB^+_dR tensor Omega^1_X(C) -> 0 on the infinite-level curve, viewed as a log pro-etale covering of a finite level; the case k = 1 is sketched first.

items.name: Section 6.3.2: the abstract linear-algebra mechanism
items.statement: The formal setup: let M be an abelian group with an endomorphism N with N^2 = 0, let M' be a subgroup of ker N containing N(M), so that N induces a map from M'' = M/M' to M'. This recovers the construction of the Fontaine operator with M = E_0(W^K), M' = W^K_{k,-k}, M'' = W^K_{0,0} and N = nabla. Now suppose given an extension of the triple: a group M_1 containing M with an endomorphism N_1 squaring to zero and restricting to N, a map theta from M_1 to M'' extending the projection, and correspondingly M'_1 with M'_2 = M'_1/M', together with a section s of the induced map.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.3 and Remark 6.3.4: the operator as a composite through the section
items.statement: In the setup of 6.3.2, N_{M'} = -N_{1,M'} composed with (pi after s) as maps from M'' to M'. The proof lifts a class through s, corrects the lift by an element of M'_1 so that it lands in M, and computes. In the application, M is the generalized eigenspace E_0 of the locally analytic isotypic period module at U, M' and M'' are the two weight spaces, N is nabla, and the two short exact sequences are built from the Poincare lemma sequence and its k-th graded piece; what remains is to construct M_1, M'_1, N_1 and the section s.
items.locator: Lemma 6.3.3 with its proof and Remark 6.3.4, pp. 99-100

items.name: Section 6.3.5: the structural de Rham period sheaf and its properties
items.statement: For U in B with preimage V_infinity, pulled back from an affinoid at finite level defined over a finite extension K, the cusps give a log structure on V_0 and V_infinity is an open covering in the pro-Kummer-etale site, so the geometric de Rham period sheaf of Diao-Lan-Liu-Zhu can be evaluated there, giving OB^+_dR(V_infinity). It has: a surjection theta_log onto the structure sheaf of the perfectoid curve, whose kernel powers give an exhaustive complete filtration with gr^i the i-th symmetric power of gr^1 over gr^0; a filtration-strict injection of B^+_dR(V_infinity) compatible with theta; an injection of the colimit of the finite-level structure rings; and compatible actions of G_K and of the group. It does not depend on the choices of K and of the open subgroup.
items.locator: Section 6.3.5, pp. 99-100; the constructions are [DLLZ18, section 2.2, Definition 2.2.10, Proposition 2.3.15] and [Sch16a, (3)]

items.name: Section 6.3.6: the Poincare lemma sequence and log Faltings extension
items.statement: The logarithmic connection of V_0 extends B^+_dR(V_infinity)-linearly to nabla_log on OB^+_dR(V_infinity), independently of the finite level, and induces a short strict exact Poincare lemma sequence 0 -> B^+_dR(V_infinity) -> OB^+_dR(V_infinity) -> OB^+_dR(V_infinity) tensor Omega^1_{V_0}(C) -> 0. Its first graded piece is the log Faltings extension 0 -> O(1) -> gr^1 OB^+_dR -> O tensor Omega^1_{V_0}(C) -> 0; since Omega^1_{V_0}(C) is the square of the automorphic bundle by Kodaira-Spencer it is trivial, and the symmetric-power description gives gr^k OB^+_dR a filtration with graded pieces the Tate twists O(i) for i = 0,...,k. Choosing X in Fil^1 whose image generates the quotient gives an isomorphism of filtered groups B^+_dR(V_infinity)[[X]] = OB^+_dR(V_infinity) with X of degree one.
items.locator: Section 6.3.6 with the displayed sequences (6.3.2) and (6.3.3), pp. 99-100; the connection is [DLLZ18, 2.2.15]

items.name: Sections 6.3.7 and 6.3.8: the truncated sheaves and their locally analytic isotypic parts
items.statement: Assigning to U the module OB^+_dR(V_infinity) defines a filtered sheaf on Fl, and OB^+_{dR,k} is its truncation; there is a natural map from B^+_{dR,k}. Each OB^+_{dR,k}(U) is a finite module over B^+_{dR,k}(U) and carries a Banach algebra structure with unit ball the image of A_inf(V_infinity)[[X]], independent of X. The sheaf is GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant; OB^{+,la}_{dR,k} is the locally analytic subsheaf, the Lie algebra acts, and OB^{+,la,chi~}_{dR,k} is the isotypic part, both with induced filtrations. Since Faltings's extension filters OB^+_{dR,k} by copies of O_{K^p} up to Tate twists, the argument of Lemma 6.2.2 shows taking graded pieces commutes with taking locally analytic vectors and isotypic parts, and the argument of Proposition 6.1.18 shows it also commutes with taking G_{K_infinity}-fixed G_K-analytic vectors.

items.name: Proposition 6.3.9: graded pieces, locally analytic vectors and the induced filtration
items.statement: For U in B with G_K acting, and for i >= 0 and l > 0, the natural maps from gr^i of the locally analytic sheaf to the locally analytic vectors of gr^i, from gr^i of the isotypic part to the isotypic part of gr^i, and the same after taking G_{K_infinity}-fixed G_K-analytic vectors, are all isomorphisms. Moreover the i-th symmetric power of Faltings's extension induces a natural filtration on gr^i of the isotypic decompleted sheaf whose graded pieces are the twists O^{la,chi~_l}_{K^p}(U)(j)^K tensor the (i-j)-th power of Omega^1_{V_0}(C) for j = 0,...,i. Since gr^i does not depend on k > i one writes gr^i OB^{+,la}_dR.

items.name: Sections 6.3.10 and 6.3.11: the eigenspace decomposition and the main diagram
items.statement: The action of 1 in the Lie algebra of Gal(K_infinity/K) on the decompleted isotypic sections decomposes them into generalized eigenspaces, since they are filtered by the twists of O^{la,chi~_l}_{K^p}(U)^K; the eigenvalue 0 part is the one of interest. Then one writes down the truncated Poincare lemma sequence for chi~_k together with its Fil^k-part, evaluates at U, takes G_{K_infinity}-fixed G_K-analytic vectors and the generalized eigenspace of 0, obtaining a diagram of two exact rows in which the constituents are O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}(U)^{G_K}, E_0 of the period modules, and the graded pieces of the structural sheaf.

items.name: Section 6.3.12: the reduction of Theorem 6.2.6 to two comparisons
items.statement: The diagram of 6.3.11 realises the setup of 6.3.2 with N and N_1 given by the action of 1 in the Lie algebra, except that a section s_{k+1} of E_0(theta_log) must be constructed, from O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}(U)^{G_K} to the G_K-invariants of the structural period module, whose composite with E_0(nabla_log) lands in the expected filtration step; this is done in Definition 6.4.10. Granting it, Lemma 6.3.3 gives N_k(U) = -N'_k composed with (E_0(nabla_log) after s_{k+1}), where N'_k is obtained by applying the same Lie algebra element to the middle term of the exact sequence attached to gr^k. So Theorem 6.2.6 reduces to comparing E_0(nabla_log) after s_{k+1} with d_k, and N'_k with d-bar'_k.

items.name: Proposition 6.3.13: the first comparison
items.statement: For the section s_{k+1} of Definition 6.4.10, E_0(nabla_log) composed with s_{k+1} equals d_k, both viewed as maps from O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}(U)^{G_K} to its tensor product with the k-th power of Omega^1_{V_0}(C).

items.name: Proposition 6.3.14: the second comparison
items.statement: There is a non-zero scalar c_k in Q_p with N'_k = c_k d-bar'_k, both viewed as maps from O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}(U)^{G_K} tensor the k-th power of Omega^1_{V_0}(C) to O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}(U)(k)^{G_K}.

items.name: Section 6.4.1: periods from the relative de Rham comparison
items.statement: The goal is to construct the section s_{k+1} of E_0(theta_log) and to compute its composite with E_0(nabla_log); this needs explicit elements of OB^+_dR, produced from the relative de Rham comparison theorem on modular curves, which provides OV_0-linear period maps l_n from the n-th symmetric power of the de Rham bundle tensored with the n-th symmetric power of the dual standard representation into OB^+_dR(U).
items.locator: Section 6.4.1, pp. 103-104, with the displayed maps (6.4.1) to (6.4.3); following [Pan22, 4.1.3]

items.name: Lemmas 6.4.2 and 6.4.3: invertibility and convergence in the period ring
items.statement: (6.4.2) An element of OB^+_dR(U) is invertible if and only if its image under theta_log is invertible, since the ring is complete for the kernel-adic topology. (6.4.3) If the a_n are sections of O_{V_0} tending to zero and y has theta_log(y) of norm at most one, then the series with terms a_n y^n converges in OB^+_{dR,k}(U); equivalently convergence of the series in y is equivalent to convergence of its image. The proof splits y as a Teichmuller-type lift plus an element of the kernel, following Berger-Colmez.
items.locator: Lemmas 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 with their proofs, p. 104; essentially [BC16, Lemme 4.9]

items.name: Section 6.4.4: the period x-tilde lifting the coordinate
items.statement: For k = 1 and e_1 invertible on the preimage, fix a section f_1 of the de Rham bundle whose image generates gr^0. Then l_1 applied to f_1 tensor the second dual basis vector has invertible image under theta_log, hence is invertible by Lemma 6.4.2, and x-tilde is defined as minus the ratio of the two periods l_1(f_1 tensor e_1^*) and l_1(f_1 tensor e_2^*). It satisfies theta_log(x-tilde) = x and is fixed by G_K.

items.name: Lemma 6.4.6: the p-adic Legendre relation
items.statement: (1) For sections g_1, g_2 of the de Rham bundle and vectors v_1, v_2 in the dual standard representation, the determinant expression l_1(g_1 tensor v_1) l_1(g_2 tensor v_2) - l_1(g_1 tensor v_2) l_1(g_2 tensor v_1) lies in t OB^+_dR(U). (2) Consequently nabla_log applied to phi_1(x) lies in t OB^+_dR(U) tensor Omega^1_{V_0}(C). The first part reduces to the inclusion of the determinant of the de Rham bundle into t times the determinant of the standard representation, which follows from the description of the horizontal sections in the proof of [Sch13, Theorem 7.6].
items.locator: Section 6.4.5 and Lemma 6.4.6 with its proof, pp. 105-106
items.note: The name records the analogy with Legendre’s relation between periods of an elliptic curve: the Wronskian-type determinant of two periods is a multiple of 2 pi i, here of t.

items.name: Section 6.4.7: x-tilde is well defined modulo t
items.statement: Although x-tilde and phi_1 depend on the choice of f_1, Lemma 6.4.6 shows x-tilde modulo t OB^+_dR(U) is independent of that choice: the Poincare lemma sequence modulo t is exact because all its terms are free over B^+_dR(U), and the lemma places x-tilde modulo t in B^+_dR(U)/(t) = O_{K^p}(U).

items.name: Proposition 6.4.8: the section phi_1 in weight zero
items.statement: Given f_1 as above there is a G_K x G_0-equivariant map phi_1 from the union over finite extensions of the decompleted weight-(0,0) sections into OB^+_dR(U) such that (1) theta_log after phi_1 is the identity, (2) phi_1 is linear over the finite-level structure rings, (3) its composite into each truncation is continuous, and (4) phi_1(x) is congruent to x-tilde modulo t.

items.name: Section 6.4.9 and Definition 6.4.10: the section s_{k+1} for general k
items.statement: For k >= 2 one follows the strategy of Subsection 4.1: the period maps l_n are extended, using phi_1, to maps l'_n linear over the decompleted weight-(0,0) sections, defined on the n-th symmetric power of the de Rham bundle tensored with those sections and with the n-th symmetric power of the dual representation. The Hodge filtration on Sym^n D and the Hodge-Tate filtration give natural surjections onto gr^0, and the canonical splitting of Lemma 4.1.6 provides a map psi_{k-1} in the other direction; s_{k+1} is defined as l'_{k-1} modulo Fil^{k+1} composed with psi_{k-1}. It takes values in the locally analytic isotypic part and satisfies theta_log after s_{k+1} equal to the identity.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.11: the first comparison, proved
items.statement: The image of nabla_log after s_{k+1} lies in Fil^{k-1} of the truncated structural sheaf tensored with Omega^1_{V_0}(C), and under the identification of that space with the weight-(1-k,0) sections tensored with the k-th power of Omega^1_{V_0}(C) one has nabla_log after s_{k+1} = d_k. This is Proposition 6.3.13. It suffices to prove it modulo t, by Lemma 6.4.12, and modulo t it is the commutativity of an explicit diagram, Lemma 6.4.13.

items.name: Lemma 6.4.12: reduction modulo t loses nothing on invariants
items.statement: The natural map from the G_K-invariants of the truncated locally analytic isotypic structural sheaf at U to the G_K-invariants of its reduction modulo t is an isomorphism. The proof uses the exactness of the sequence relating the decompleted spaces, their generalized eigenspace decompositions for the Lie algebra action, and the fact that 0 does not occur in the spectrum on the t-multiples.

items.name: Lemma 6.4.13: the comparison diagram commutes
items.statement: The diagram whose commutativity gives nabla_log after s_{k+1} = d_k modulo t commutes: the left triangle by the definition of s_{k+1}, and the right square because l'_{k-1} modulo t is a K-linear map of C-LB spaces, hence extends C-linearly, after which the identification of the symmetric powers of the de Rham bundle over the weight-(0,0) sections makes the comparison explicit.

items.name: Section 6.5.1: the definition of N’_k recalled
items.statement: With e_1 invertible on the preimage, take the locally analytic vectors in the k-th graded piece of the Poincare lemma sequence, 0 -> gr^k B^{+,la}_dR(U) -> gr^k OB^{+,la}_dR(U) -> gr^{k-1} OB^{+,la}_dR(U) tensor Omega^1_{V_0}(C) -> 0, then pass to the chi~_k-isotypic part and to the G_{K_infinity}-fixed G_K-analytic vectors; N'_k is obtained from the action of the Lie algebra element on the middle term.
items.locator: Section 6.5.1 with the displayed sequence (6.5.1), p. 110

items.name: Proposition 6.5.2 and Lemma 6.5.3: exactness survives, by splitting Faltings’s extension
items.statement: The sequence (6.5.1) stays exact after taking G_K-invariants and z_k-isotypic parts. For k = 1 this follows from Lemma 6.5.3: the surjection from gr^1 OB^{+,la}_dR(U) onto O^{la}_{K^p}(U) tensor Omega^1_{V_0}(C) admits a G_K x U(z)-equivariant section, so the locally analytic Faltings extension splits equivariantly; Faltings's own splitting result is what provides it. The general case follows because gr^k is the k-th symmetric power of gr^1.
items.locator: Proposition 6.5.2 and Lemma 6.5.3 with their proofs, pp. 110-111; the splitting is due to Faltings

items.name: Proposition 6.5.4 and Corollary 6.5.5: the quadratic relation and what Z does
items.statement: Let theta_Sen be the action of 1 in the Lie algebra of Gal(K_infinity/K) on the decompleted sections. Then it satisfies an explicit quadratic relation involving the Casimir, because theta_Sen is the horizontal Cartan action on the lower-right idempotent by [Pan22, Theorem 5.1.8] and the relation between that action and the centre is known. Consequently (1) Z acts on gr^k B^{+,la}_dR(U)^{G_K, z_k} through chi~_k, so that space is O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}(U)(k)^{G_K}; and (2) the action of Z on gr^{k-1} OB^{+,la}_dR(U)^{G_K,z_k} has a generalized eigenspace decomposition in which the chi~_k-generalized eigenspace is the honest eigenspace, equal to O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}(U)^{G_K} tensor Omega^1_{V_0}(C).
items.locator: Proposition 6.5.4 and Corollary 6.5.5 with their proofs, pp. 111-112; the inputs are [Pan22, Theorem 5.1.8 and Corollary 4.2.8] and 6.2.3

items.name: Section 6.5.6 and Lemma 6.5.7: the operator N-tilde_k and its comparison with N’_k
items.statement: Taking the chi~_k-generalized eigenspace of gr^k OB^{+,la}_dR(U)^{G_K,z_k}, equivalently the kernel of the square of the shifted Casimir, one gets an exact sequence with outer terms O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}(U)(k)^{G_K} and O^{la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}(U)^{G_K} tensor the k-th power of Omega^1_{V_0}(C); the action of the shifted Casimir induces a map N-tilde_k between those outer terms. Comparing the two recipes - one lifts along gr^k nabla_log and applies the Lie algebra element, the other applies the shifted Casimir - gives N'_k = N-tilde_k divided by 2k.
items.locator: Section 6.5.6 and Lemma 6.5.7 with its proof, pp. 112-113

items.name: Section 6.5.8 and Lemma 6.5.9: both operators preserve the n-finite vectors
items.statement: Both N-tilde_k and d-bar'_k are continuous O^{sm}_{K^p}(U)-linear maps from omega^{2k,la,(1-k,0)}_{K^p}(U) to O^{la,(1,-k)}_{K^p}(U)(k), using Kodaira-Spencer and the fixed trivialisation of the determinant of the de Rham bundle. Both send the n-finite subspace of Corollary 3.2.3 into the n-finite subspace of the target, and in the tensor decomposition of that corollary both are induced by O^{sm}_{K^p}(U)-linear maps between the finite-dimensional category-O modules M^v_{(0,1-k)} and M^v_{(-k,1)}(k). For d-bar'_k this is read off the explicit formula of Theorem 4.2.7.
items.locator: Section 6.5.8 and Lemma 6.5.9 with its proof, pp. 113-114

items.name: Lemma 6.5.10: the n-finite part of the Hodge-Tate sequence
items.statement: The Hodge-Tate sequence induces an exact sequence of n-finite parts, 0 -> O^{la,(1,-1)}_{K^p}(U)^{n-fin}(1) -> V(1) tensor omega^{1,la,(0,-1)}_{K^p}(U)^{n-fin} -> omega^{2,la,(0,0)}_{K^p}(U)^{n-fin} -> 0, and under the tensor decompositions of Corollary 3.2.3 it is the tensor product of omega^{2,sm}_{K^p}(U) with an exact sequence of category-O modules 0 -> M^v_{(-1,1)}(1) -> V(1) tensor M^v_{(0,-1)} -> M^v_{(0,0)} -> 0.

items.name: Section 6.5.11 and Lemma 6.5.12: the two operators differ by a non-zero scalar
items.statement: Proposition 6.3.14 follows: the n-finite subspace is dense and both maps are continuous, so by Lemma 6.5.9 it suffices to compare the two induced maps between the category-O modules M^v_{(0,1-k)} and M^v_{(-k,1)}(k). Both are gl_2(Q_p)-equivariant, and the space of such maps is one-dimensional, so they are proportional; Lemma 6.5.12 shows neither is zero - for d-bar'_k from its explicit formula, and for N-tilde_k because M^v_{(-k,1-k)} is the Verma module of highest weight -rho, so that in the language of translation functors the relevant generalized eigenspace is its translation, and the induced operator is non-zero.
items.locator: Section 6.5.11 and Lemma 6.5.12 with its proof, pp. 114-115

items.name: Remark 6.5.13: the constant is rational
items.statement: Since the category-O modules have natural Q-structures preserved by sl_2(Q), the proof shows that N-tilde_k and d-bar_k differ by a constant in Q, so the constant c_k of Proposition 6.3.14, and hence of Theorem 6.2.6, may be taken in Q^*.

items.name: Section 7.1.1: completed cohomology, recalled precisely
items.statement: For K^p a compact open of GL_2(A_f^p), set H~^i(K^p, Z/p^n) to be the colimit over K_p of the cohomology of the complete modular curves X_{K^p K_p}(C) with Z/p^n-coefficients, and H~^i(K^p, Z_p) the inverse limit over n. In general the torsion is killed by a fixed power of p by Calegari-Emerton, and for modular curves it is well known to be torsion free. For a Q_p-Banach space W, H~^i(K^p, W) is the completed tensor product, a Q_p-Banach space with continuous GL_2(Q_p)-action; for W = Q_p it is admissible, and since the curves are defined over Q, etale cohomology gives a commuting G_Q-action.
items.locator: Section 7.1.1, pp. 115-116; the torsion bound is [CE12, Theorem 1.1], the definition Emerton’s

items.name: Theorem 7.1.2: the main theorem, in its body form
items.statement: Let rho : G_Q -> GL_2(E) be two-dimensional continuous absolutely irreducible such that (1) rho appears in H~^1(K^p,E), with H~^1(K^p,E)[rho] the image of the evaluation map, and (2) rho restricted to G_{Q_p} is de Rham with Hodge-Tate weights 0 and k for some k > 0. Then (1) classicality: rho arises from a cuspidal eigenform of weight k+1; and (2) finiteness: for K_p = 1 + p^n M_2(Z_p) with n >= 2, the n-invariants of the K_p-analytic vectors of H~^1(K^p,E)[rho] form a finite-dimensional E-vector space. A description of the locally analytic vectors as a GL_2(Q_p)-representation is given in Subsection 7.3.

items.name: Remark 7.1.3: the independent representation-theoretic proof of finiteness
items.statement: The main result of Dospinescu-Paskunas-Schraen, that the locally analytic vectors of H~^1(K^p,E)[rho] have an infinitesimal character, is by their later work enough to deduce the finiteness statement, and they even prove finiteness for the K_p-analytic vectors themselves, by a purely representation-theoretic method.
items.locator: Remark 7.1.3, p. 116; also [Pan22, Proposition 6.1.5] and [DPS22, Corollary 6.7]

items.name: Section 7.1.4: the big Hecke algebra and its Galois determinant
items.statement: With S a finite set containing p outside which K_l is maximal, T(K^p K_p) is the Z_p-subalgebra of endomorphisms of the finite-level cohomology generated by the T_l and S_l^{+-1}, independent of S, and the big Hecke algebra T(K^p) is the projective limit: a complete semilocal noetherian Z_p-algebra with finite residue fields, acting faithfully on H~^1(K^p,Z_p) and commuting with GL_2(Q_p) x G_Q. There is a continuous two-dimensional determinant of G_{Q,S} valued in it in Chenevier's sense, whose Frobenius characteristic polynomial is X^2 - l^{-1}T_l + l^{-1}S_l, whose cyclotomic twist is the Eichler-Shimura congruence relation on completed cohomology. A homomorphism lambda to E gives a semisimple rho_lambda, and the Eichler-Shimura relation makes the Hom from rho_lambda(-1) into completed cohomology equal to that into its lambda-isotypic part; when rho_lambda is absolutely irreducible, by Boston-Lenstra-Ribet the isotypic part is itself rho_lambda(-1)-isotypic.

items.name: Theorem 7.2.2 and the deduction of Theorem 7.1.2
items.statement: Let rho be as in Theorem 7.1.2 and lambda the cyclotomic twist of a Hecke character with rho_lambda(-1) = rho, so that the lambda-isotypic part of completed cohomology is H~^1(K^p,E)[rho]; its base change to C splits into Hodge-Tate weight 0 and weight k parts. Then there is a natural GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism between the locally analytic vectors of the weight-zero part and ker I^1_{k-1} tensor E at lambda. Theorem 7.1.2 follows: the right-hand side is non-zero, so Theorem 5.5.7 forces the classical forms of weight k+1 to have a non-zero lambda-part, which is classicality, and the finiteness is Corollary 4.4.18.
items.locator: Section 7.2.1, Theorem 7.2.2 and the proof of Theorem 7.1.2, pp. 117-118
items.note: This is the bridge: everything proved about the geometric operator on the flag variety is transported to completed cohomology here.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.3: completed cohomology with period-sheaf coefficients
items.statement: There is a natural G_{Q_p}-equivariant isomorphism of B^+_{dR,k}-modules between H~^i(K^p, B^+_{dR,k}) and H^i(Fl, B^+_{dR,k}). For k = 1 this is the comparison H~^i(K^p,C) = H^i(Fl, O_{K^p}); for k >= 2 one constructs a map reducing to it modulo t and concludes by induction using flatness.
items.locator: Proposition 7.2.3 with its proof, p. 118; the k = 1 case is [Pan22, Corollary 4.4.3], essentially due to Scholze [Sch15, section IV.2]

items.name: Lemma 7.2.4: constructing the comparison map on the etale site
items.statement: There is a natural G_{Q_p}-equivariant homomorphism of B^+_{dR,k}-modules from H~^i(K^p, B^+_{dR,k}) to H^i(Fl, B^+_{dR,k}) reducing modulo t to the known isomorphism. The natural proof uses the primitive comparison theorem and Scholze's argument; the proof given instead uses only the etale site, through the sheaves of truncated Witt vectors of the integral structure sheaf modulo p, an almost isomorphism between their etale and analytic cohomology, and the observation that the quotient maps from A_inf onto A_inf modulo the k-th power of the kernel of theta and p^m factor through truncated Witt vectors.
items.locator: Lemma 7.2.4 with its proof, pp. 118-119; the primitive comparison is [Sch13, proof of Theorem 8.4], the model argument [Sch15, proof of Theorem IV.2.1], the acyclicity [Sch12, Propositions 6.14 and 7.13]

items.name: Lemmas 7.2.5 and 7.2.6: the limit arguments behind the comparison
items.statement: (7.2.5) For k >= 1 the torsion of H^i(X_{K^p}, A_inf modulo the k-th power of the kernel of theta), taken almost, is killed by a power of p, and that cohomology is the inverse limit of its reductions modulo p^m; proved by induction on k using that the kernel is principal and the k = 1 case from [Pan22, Corollary 4.4.3]. (7.2.6) There are natural isomorphisms H~^i(K^p, A_inf modulo that power) = inverse limit over m of H~^i(K^p,Z/p^m) tensor the corresponding quotient, the stronger statement being that H~^i(K^p,M) is the inverse limit of H~^i(K^p,Z/p^m) tensor M for any p-adically complete torsion-free M, which follows from a complex of p-adically complete torsion-free modules computing completed cohomology; and the cohomology on X_{K^p} agrees with the cohomology on Fl of the push-forward.
items.locator: Lemmas 7.2.5 and 7.2.6 with their proofs, pp. 119-120; the complex is from [Eme06b, pp. 27-28]

items.name: Lemma 7.2.7 and the proof of Theorem 7.2.2
items.statement: There is a natural G_{Q_p}-equivariant isomorphism of B^+_{dR,k+1}-modules between the locally analytic lambda-isotypic part of H~^1(K^p, B^+_{dR,k+1} tensor E) and H^1(Fl, B^{+,la,chi~_k}_{dR,k+1}) tensor E at lambda. The point is that rho_lambda has Hodge-Tate weights -1 and k-1, so the locally analytic vectors of the isotypic part have infinitesimal character chi~_k by [Pan22, Proposition 6.1.5], and then Propositions 7.2.3 and 6.2.17 apply. Theorem 7.2.2 follows: since rho is de Rham, Theorem 6.1.16 makes the Fontaine operator of the corresponding module vanish, and by functoriality together with Corollary 6.2.15 that operator is I^1_{k-1} on the weight-zero locally analytic part, so that part is exactly the kernel.
items.locator: Lemma 7.2.7 with its proof and the conclusion on p. 120

items.name: Section 7.3.1: the setup for the local description
items.statement: Combining Theorem 7.2.2 with Subsection 5.5 gives a geometric description of the locally analytic representation H~^1(K^p,E)[lambda]^{la}. When the automorphic representation attached to rho is supercuspidal at p this is a special case of the Breuil-Strauch conjecture, solved by Dospinescu-Le Bras; when it is a principal series at p it is a special case of a conjecture of Berger-Breuil and Emerton, solved by Liu-Xie-Zhang and Colmez; and the work here shows both can be formulated uniformly. Fixing an embedding tau of E into C and writing lambda_tau for the composite, and M_{k+2} for the colimit of the classical forms with its smooth GL_2(A_f)-action, the non-vanishing of M_{k+2}(K^p) tensor D_0^{-1} at lambda_tau makes lambda_tau correspond to an irreducible representation pi^infinity = tensor' pi_l of GL_2(A_f) inside M_{k+2} tensor D_0^{-1} with (pi^infinity)^{K^p} the lambda_tau-part.

items.name: Theorem 7.3.2 and Remarks 7.3.3-7.3.5: the supercuspidal description
items.statement: Suppose pi_p is supercuspidal. Then there is a GL_2(Q_p)^0-equivariant isomorphism between the locally analytic weight-zero part of H~^1(K^p,C)[lambda_tau] and (pi^{infinity,p})^{K^p} tensor the quotient of the units-of-O_{D_p} invariants of H^1(Fl, j_! of the D_p^*-smooth part of omega^{-k+1}_Dr) tensor pi'_p, twisted, by Sym^{k-1} V^* tensor pi_p. It follows from Theorem 7.2.2 and Corollary 5.5.14, moving the tensor factor outside the quotient using new vectors at the places away from p; by Remark 5.4.13 it upgrades to a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism. Corollary 5.5.14 also gives the corresponding short exact sequence with sub (pi^infinity)^{K^p} tensor Sym^{k-1} V^*. Since rho is two-dimensional, the weight-zero part determines the whole locally analytic Hom space up to a non-canonical isomorphism, so the theorem also describes H~^1(K^p,C)[lambda_tau]^{la}; and because H~^1(K^p,E)^{la} is admissible in the sense of Schneider-Teitelbaum, the theorem implies a form of admissibility for the quaternionic cohomology as a locally analytic representation over C, although C is not spherically complete as their theory assumes.
items.locator: Theorem 7.3.2 with its proof and Remarks 7.3.3, 7.3.4 and 7.3.5, pp. 122-123
items.note: This is Theorem 1.1.7 of the introduction.

items.name: Remark 7.3.6: the comparison with the Breuil-Strauch conjecture
items.statement: For k = 1, since pi'_p is fixed by a small subgroup, the quaternionic term is the units-invariants of H^1(Fl, j_! of the push-forward of the structure sheaf of a finite-level Drinfeld space) tensor pi'_p, and by 5.6.9 there is an exact sequence relating the compactly supported de Rham cohomology to that H^1. Taking lambda-isotypic parts in Theorem 5.6.7 gives that the units-invariants of H^1_{dR,c} tensor pi'_p is D_dR(rho restricted to G_{Q_p}) tensor pi_p, which is the form of the statement proved by Dospinescu-Le Bras.

items.name: Theorem 7.3.7 and Remark 7.3.8: the principal series description
items.statement: Suppose pi_p is a principal series. Then there is a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism between the locally analytic weight-zero part of H~^1(K^p,C)[lambda_tau] and the locally analytic induction from B of H^1_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^{k-1}) twisted by epsilon^{-k+1}(e'_2)^{k-1} at lambda, modulo (pi^infinity)^{K^p} tensor Sym^{k-1} V^*. Corollary 5.5.14 also gives the short exact sequence with that sub and with quotient the induction twisted by epsilon^{-k+1}(e'_1)^k (e'_2)^{-1} at lambda.
items.note: This is Theorem 1.1.10 of the introduction.

items.name: Remark 7.3.9: the rigid cohomology of Igusa curves is D_cris
items.statement: For k = 1, and in general by the same discussion, H^1_rig(Ig(K^p)) is the log rigid cohomology of the tower of Igusa curves, and the comparison between log rigid and log crystalline cohomology gives H^1_rig(Ig(K^p))[lambda] = (pi^{infinity,p})^{K^p} tensor D_cris(rho restricted to G_{Q_p}), where D_cris is taken over a sufficiently ramified cyclotomic extension and carries a Weil group action by Fontaine's recipe; the congruence relation on the Igusa curves turns that into a B-action making the isomorphism B-equivariant. Hence the principal series description becomes the statement of the Berger-Breuil-Emerton conjecture.
items.locator: Remark 7.3.9, pp. 123-124; the congruence relation is [Car86, section 1.6.4]

items.name: Remark 7.3.10: the uniform formulation
items.statement: As in Remark 5.5.15, the locally analytic weight-zero part is H^1(DR_k)[lambda_tau] modulo Fil^1, which gives the descriptions of Theorems 7.3.2 and 7.3.7 in the supercuspidal and principal series cases; this suggests that the Breuil-Strauch conjecture and the Berger-Breuil-Emerton conjecture can be formulated in one way, and the same is expected when pi_p is special.

items.name: Remark 7.3.11: the special case
items.statement: For pi_p special and k = 1, Theorem 5.5.4 gives ker I^1_0 at lambda_tau a three-step filtration whose graded pieces are (pi^{p,infinity})^{K^p} tensor pi_p, the quaternionic term, and the induction of the Igusa cohomology. If rho restricted to G_{Q_p} is absolutely irreducible, Emerton's local-global compatibility identifies the locally analytic weight-zero part with the completed tensor product of (pi^{p,infinity})^{K^p} with the locally analytic vectors of the representation attached to rho by the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, whose structure was conjectured by Emerton and proved by Liu-Xie-Zhang and Colmez. Theorem 7.2.2 gives an inclusion into ker I^1_0 at lambda_tau, and it is in fact an equality: a careful analysis using Serre duality shows Fil^2 is essentially the completed tensor product with Breuil's Sigma(2,L), and gr^3 essentially agrees with the locally analytic induction in Emerton's conjectural sequence. Hence ker I^1_0 at lambda_tau is the honest eigenspace in the special case too.
items.locator: Remark 7.3.11, pp. 124-125; the references are [Eme06a, Conjecture 6.7.7], [LXZ12], [Col14] and [Bre04, sections 2-3, Remarque 3.5.7]
items.note: This is what Remarks 1.1.12, 1.2.4 and 5.5.15 point forward to: the special case is settled, but only by importing the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, which the rest of the paper deliberately avoids.

prerequisites.work: Lue Pan, On locally analytic vectors of the completed cohomology of modular curves, Forum of Mathematics Pi 10 (2022), e7 (cited as [Pan22])
prerequisites.why: Paper I of this series and an unavoidable prerequisite: the relative Sen theory showing that the locally analytic sections are annihilated by the horizontal nilpotent subalgebra, the horizontal Cartan action and the weight sheaves, the power-series description of sections over the standard affinoids, the identification of the cohomology of those sheaves with completed cohomology, and the existence of an infinitesimal character. Almost every item of this extraction quotes it.

prerequisites.work: P. Scholze, On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties, Annals of Mathematics 182 (2015) (cited as [Sch15]), together with his p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum of Mathematics Pi 1 (2013) (cited as [Sch13])
prerequisites.why: The perfectoid modular curve at infinite level, the Hodge-Tate period map and the basis of affinoids whose preimages are affinoid perfectoid; the period sheaves and the primitive comparison theorem behind the comparison of completed cohomology with period-sheaf cohomology.

prerequisites.work: P. Scholze and J. Weinstein, Moduli of p-divisible groups, Cambridge Journal of Mathematics 1 (2013) (cited as [SW13])
prerequisites.why: The Lubin-Tate and Drinfeld towers at infinite level as perfectoid spaces, their group actions and continuity, and the duality isomorphism between them that exchanges the two period maps. Subsections 5.2 and 5.3 are written on top of this.

prerequisites.work: H. Diao, K.-W. Lan, R. Liu and X. Zhu, Logarithmic adic spaces: some foundational results (cited as [DLLZ18])
prerequisites.why: The pro-Kummer-etale site of a log adic space and the geometric de Rham period sheaf with its logarithmic connection, Poincare lemma sequence and Faltings extension, which is the resolution the whole of Section 6 runs on.

prerequisites.work: J.-M. Fontaine, Arithmetique des representations galoisiennes p-adiques, Asterisque 295 (2004) (cited as [Fon04])
prerequisites.why: The classification of almost de Rham B_dR-representations: the space D_pdR, the nilpotent operator nu whose negative is the Sen-type operator used here, and the criterion that a Hodge-Tate representation is de Rham exactly when the induced operator vanishes. The paper's main theorem is the identification of its geometric operator with this one.

prerequisites.work: L. Berger and P. Colmez, Theorie de Sen et vecteurs localement analytiques, Annales scientifiques de l'ENS 49 (2016) (cited as [BC16]), with their earlier [BC08]
prerequisites.why: That the right notion in Sen theory in this generality is locally analytic rather than finite vectors, Tate's normalised traces in the form used, and the convergence lemma for series in the period ring.

prerequisites.work: M. Emerton, On the interpolation of systems of eigenvalues attached to automorphic Hecke eigenforms, Inventiones 164 (2006); Locally analytic vectors in representations of locally p-adic analytic groups, Memoirs of the AMS (cited as [Eme17]); and Local-global compatibility in the p-adic Langlands programme for GL_2/Q (cited as [Eme11])
prerequisites.why: Completed cohomology and its admissibility; the theory of locally analytic vectors over LB-spaces that Section 2 extends; and the local-global compatibility that the paper deliberately avoids for its main theorem but invokes for the special case in Remark 7.3.11.

prerequisites.work: R. Liu and X. Zhu, Rigidity and a Riemann-Hilbert correspondence for p-adic local systems, Inventiones 207 (2017) (cited as [LZ17])
prerequisites.why: The relation between a de Rham local system, its associated Higgs bundle and the graded pieces of its connection, which gives the conceptual identification of the differential equation with the Kodaira-Spencer class in Theorem 5.2.6. The compatibility with the earlier paper's Higgs field is deferred to future work, so a blueprint must supply it (recorded as a source issue).

prerequisites.work: P. Colmez, G. Dospinescu and W. Niziol, Cohomologie p-adique de la tour de Drinfeld, Journal of the AMS 33 (2020) (cited as [CDN20])
prerequisites.why: That the Lubin-Tate and Drinfeld towers have the same compactly supported de Rham cohomology, and the Serre duality and compactly supported cohomology conventions for the finite-level Drinfeld spaces, which is what licenses reading the supersingular term of the vanishing-cycle sequence on the Drinfeld side.

prerequisites.work: G. Dospinescu and A.-C. Le Bras, Revetements du demi-plan de Drinfeld et correspondance de Langlands p-adique, Annals of Mathematics 186 (2017) (cited as [DLB17])
prerequisites.why: The Breuil-Strauch conjecture, of which the supercuspidal main theorem here is a special case in dual form, and the identification of the relevant compactly supported cohomology with D_dR tensored with the local component.

prerequisites.work: R. Coleman, Classical and overconvergent modular forms, Inventiones 124 (1996), and Classical and overconvergent modular forms of higher level, Journal de theorie des nombres de Bordeaux 9 (1997) (cited as [Col96, Col97])
prerequisites.why: The theta operator on overconvergent forms, the finite-dimensionality of the rigid cohomology of Igusa curves with symmetric-power coefficients and the description of its primitive part in terms of the finite slope part of classical forms - the one place where a sharper description of the paper's answer would come from.

prerequisites.work: N. Katz and B. Mazur, Arithmetic moduli of elliptic curves, Annals of Mathematics Studies 108 (1985) (cited as [KM85])
prerequisites.why: The integral model of the modular curve of level Gamma(p^n) whose special fibre has components indexed by surjections from (Z/p^n)^2, meeting at supersingular points, and the irreducibility of the Igusa curves. Every statement about the canonical locus and its connected components rests on this.

prerequisites.work: M. Rapoport and T. Zink, Period spaces for p-divisible groups, Annals of Mathematics Studies 141 (1996) (cited as [RZ96]), with M. Gross and M. Hopkins, Equivariant vector bundles on the Lubin-Tate moduli space (cited as [GH94])
prerequisites.why: The uniformization of the supersingular locus of the modular curve by the Lubin-Tate tower at finite level, and the Gross-Hopkins period map with the continuity of the quaternionic action.

prerequisites.work: G. Dospinescu, V. Paskunas and B. Schraen, Infinitesimal characters in arithmetic families (cited as [DPS20, DPS22])
prerequisites.why: That the locally analytic vectors of the multiplicity space have an infinitesimal character, used throughout, and an independent purely representation-theoretic proof of the finiteness statement, in a form stronger than the one obtained here.

prerequisites.work: R. Liu, B. Xie and Y. Zhang, Locally analytic vectors of unitary principal series of GL_2(Q_p) (cited as [LXZ12]), P. Colmez, La serie principale unitaire de GL_2(Q_p): vecteurs localement analytiques (cited as [Col14]), and C. Breuil, Invariant L et serie speciale p-adique (cited as [Bre04])
prerequisites.why: The p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p) in the principal series and special cases, and Breuil's Sigma(2,L); these are what the paper's principal series theorem recovers geometrically, and what Remark 7.3.11 imports to settle the special case.

prerequisites.work: A. Beilinson and J. Bernstein, A generalization of Casselman's submodule theorem (cited as [BB83]), with Harish-Chandra's isomorphism and the Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand resolution
prerequisites.why: Localisation on the flag variety, which is what makes the operator along the flag variety simply a power of the nilpotent Lie algebra element; the identification of the centre of the enveloping algebra and its infinitesimal characters; and the BGG pattern by which the operators for general k are built from the case k = 1.

prerequisites.work: P. Schneider and J. Teitelbaum, Banach space representations and Iwasawa theory (cited as [ST02]), and P. Schneider, Nonarchimedean functional analysis (cited as [Sch02])
prerequisites.why: Admissible Banach and locally analytic representations, and the functional analysis of compact operators and inductive limits used in Section 2. Note the paper's own remark that the coefficient field C is not spherically complete, so the Schneider-Teitelbaum theory does not literally apply to the statements over C.

prerequisites.work: M. Kashiwara and W. Schmid, Quasi-equivariant D-modules, equivariant derived category, and representations of reductive Lie groups (cited as [KS94]), and H. Carayol, Sur la mauvaise reduction des courbes de Shimura (cited as [Car86])
prerequisites.why: The geometric constructions of representations of real groups on the flag variety, which Remark 5.5.16 proposes as the model for what a p-adic local Langlands correspondence should look like; and the l-adic vanishing cycle sequence and the congruence relation on Igusa curves, of which the paper's Theorem 5.6.7 is the p-adic analogue.

routes.title: Completed cohomology and p-adic local-global compatibility over Q, Part II: locally analytic vectors and the Hodge-Tate period map
routes.reason: This is the route the maintainer has already chosen for this paper: papers.json records that PAPER-PAN-26 is 'Already routed by the maintainer: a Part II, LocallyAnalyticCompletedCohomology (DESIGN-PAN), of the completed-cohomology roadmap. Do not re-route it: read the paper in full and route its items into that roadmap's layers and to existing roadmaps as sources.' That roadmap is not yet registered - it has no file in research/blueprint/roadmaps/ and does not appear in data/atlas.json, because DESIGN-PAN is still pending in queue.json - so its layers cannot be named and the items are carried here, to the same roadmap id and with the same parent, rather than to a new target. The parent carries completed cohomology, its Hecke and deformation actions and p-adic local-global compatibility over Q; what this paper adds is a different object, the sheaf of GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic sections of the structure sheaf of the perfectoid modular curve pushed forward along the Hodge-Tate period map, and everything built from it: the weight decomposition under the horizontal Cartan action, the two differential operators and the intertwining operator, its identification with Fontaine's monodromy operator, the spectral decomposition of its kernel over the Newton stratification, and the resulting classicality and local-global statements. That is a layer sequence of its own, and PROTOCOL section 15 makes it a Part II rather than a re-planning of the parent. When DESIGN-PAN has run, a reviewer should re-express this route as a source route naming that roadmap's layers.
routes.brief: Final theorems to reach: (i) that a two-dimensional absolutely irreducible representation of the Galois group of Q which appears in the completed cohomology of modular curves and is de Rham at p with Hodge-Tate weights 0 and k > 0 comes from a cuspidal eigenform of weight k+1; (ii) that the n-invariants of the Gamma(p^n)-analytic vectors of the corresponding multiplicity space are finite-dimensional for n >= 2; (iii) the geometric description of the locally analytic vectors of that space, as a quotient of the compactly supported cohomology of the Drinfeld tower tensored with quaternionic forms when the local component is supercuspidal, and as a quotient of a locally analytic induction of the rigid cohomology of Igusa curves when it is a principal series; and (iv) the uniform statement behind both, that the locally analytic vectors are H^1 of a two-term de Rham complex on the flag variety modulo its Hodge filtration. What to cover: the pushforward sheaves O_{K^p}, their locally analytic and smooth subsheaves and the twists by the automorphic bundle; the horizontal Cartan action and the weight sheaves O^{la,chi}, with the explicit power-series description of their sections over the standard affinoids; the Hodge-Tate structure of those sections and the compactness of restriction maps, with the Hausdorff LB-space structure on the cohomology of the flag variety; the differential operator along the modular curve extending the classical theta operator O_Fl-linearly, the operator along the flag variety coming from Beilinson-Bernstein localisation, and the intertwining operator built from them, with its n-cohomology; the Newton stratification of the flag variety and the computation of the kernel and cokernel of the operator on each stratum, which needs the supersingular uniformization and the exchange of the two operators under Lubin-Tate-Drinfeld duality; the spectral decomposition of the kernel and the vanishing-cycle sequence that makes its generalized eigenspaces honest; and the comparison of the intertwining operator with the Fontaine operator of the truncated de Rham period sheaf. What to import: the parent roadmap for completed cohomology, its big Hecke algebra and the Galois determinant; PerfectoidShimuraVarieties and HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups for the perfectoid tower, the Hodge-Tate period map and the Hodge-Tate exact sequence; PadicHodgeTheory and CohomologyComparisons for the period rings, the structural de Rham sheaf and Fontaine's almost de Rham theory; LocallyAnalyticDistributions for the functional analysis of locally analytic vectors; GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer for Jacquet-Langlands and the local classification; and from the literature Paper I of this series, which is indispensable, together with Scholze-Weinstein, Diao-Lan-Liu-Zhu, Fontaine and Coleman.

routes.reason: L0 constructs the Banach spaces of functions analytic on every residue ball with their Gauss norms, and L1 and L2 the transform and the growth conditions on them; Section 2 of this paper is exactly the next step in that direction, and the paper is its source. It extends the theory of locally analytic vectors from Banach representations to Hausdorff LB-spaces, isolates the criterion by which a Banach subspace of an LB-space lands in one step of a presentation, gives the compact-operator criteria that make such colimits Hausdorff, including a Cartan-Serre lemma, and proves that the two notions of acyclicity for the functor of locally analytic vectors introduced in the author's earlier paper coincide. None of that is specific to modular curves, and every later section of the paper uses it.

S3 constructs the Hodge-Tate period map on the open perfectoid tower with its equivariance and torsor identifications, and S5 compares the abstract tower with the modular one; this paper supplies three things those layers need in the form in which they are used here. First, the basis of affinoid opens of the flag variety whose preimages are affinoid perfectoid and pulled back from a finite level, with the approximating sections that make the power-series descriptions possible. Second, the correction that makes the relative Hodge-Tate sequence Hecke-equivariant: the subobject is not the inverse of the automorphic bundle but its tensor with the determinant of the de Rham bundle, and the paper records exactly how the implicit trivialisation of that determinant affects the Hecke action. Third, the uniformization of the preimage of the Drinfeld upper half plane as a finite disjoint union of height-zero Lubin-Tate spaces at infinite level, in the equivariant form at infinite level.

ET.6a is 'Two-tower cohomological realization (mixed characteristic)', built from formal-module and p-divisible-group deformation spaces, which is precisely the material this paper needs and reworks: the Lubin-Tate tower with its Gross-Hopkins period map and Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism, the Drinfeld tower with its special formal modules, both at infinite level, and the Scholze-Weinstein duality between them together with the quaternionic group action. The paper is a source for that layer in the p-adic rather than l-adic setting, and it contributes the fact that layer does not contain: under the duality the two differential operators are exchanged, so that local analyticity for GL_2(Q_p) and for the units of the quaternion algebra coincide.

R06.1 constructs B_dR^+ with its filtration from the shared A_inf and theta interfaces. What this paper adds, and what no layer of the atlas currently plans, is Fontaine's classification of almost de Rham B_dR-representations in the generality the applications need: Banach and then Hausdorff LB modules over B_dR^+/(t^k) with a continuous semilinear Galois action, Fontaine's generalisation of Sen theory to them, the behaviour of kernels and cokernels of strict maps, the definition of the Fontaine operator on a module that is Hodge-Tate of weights 0 and k, and the criterion that it vanishes exactly for de Rham representations. That criterion is the engine of the paper's classicality theorem, and it belongs beside the period rings.

CP.0 fixes the common objects and coefficient normalisations and CP.3 the canonical B_dR^+-valued deformation of de Rham cohomology. This paper is a source for both in the relative, logarithmic and infinite-level setting: the structural de Rham period sheaf with its log connection, the Poincare lemma sequence and the log Faltings extension with the explicit power-series presentation of the period ring, the commutation of graded pieces with locally analytic vectors and with decompletion, and the comparison identifying the completed cohomology of a modular curve with coefficients in the truncated period sheaf with the cohomology of the flag variety, proved here using only the etale site.

RD.4 constructs rigid cohomology with compact support and its finiteness. The paper uses that layer's output twice and sharpens it into the shape its consumers need: the rigid cohomology of the tower of Igusa curves with symmetric-power coefficients, defined as the cokernel of the theta operator on overconvergent forms and identified with the log-rigid cohomology of an overconvergent logarithmic F-isocrystal, and the compactly supported de Rham cohomology of the height-zero Drinfeld tower at infinite level, with the Serre duality and partial properness that make its top degree finite-dimensional. Both are sources for that layer.

R17.1 and R17.3 carry quaternionic local transfer and global Jacquet-Langlands, and R16.3 the local classification for GL_2; the paper needs all three in a specific form and supplies it. The space of quaternionic forms on the multiplicative group of the quaternion algebra ramified at p and infinity, with its coefficients in an algebraic representation, its splitting into the part factoring through the reduced norm and its complement, and the semisimplicity of the spherical Hecke action on it with the spectrum described through Jacquet-Langlands as those cuspidal representations whose local component at p is special or supercuspidal, is exactly what those layers plan, stated for the group and coefficients this application uses.

SR.2 constructs smooth and compact induction from closed subgroups with Frobenius reciprocity and induction in stages. The paper needs the sheaf-theoretic form of induction from the Borel to GL_2(Q_p) on the rational points of the flag variety, in both the smooth and the locally analytic variety, together with the fact that the induction of the character by which the Borel acts on the fibre of the automorphic line bundle at infinity recovers that bundle restricted to the rational points. That is a source for SR.2, and the locally analytic version, which the layer does not plan, is where the main theorem in the principal series case lives.

R15.2 carries integral Hecke theory and q-expansions and R15.5 eigenforms and lifting. The paper needs the de Rham bundle of the universal elliptic curve with its Gauss-Manin connection, Hodge filtration and Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism, and the differential operator theta_{k+1} of order k+1 built from them, together with the spaces of classical and of overconvergent modular forms at infinite tame level presented as sections over strict neighbourhoods of the canonical locus. Those are classical objects which those layers plan, and the paper is a source for the form in which a p-adic geometric argument needs them.

sourceIssues.reason: The theorem constructs d-bar^{k+1}_Dr, and every other occurrence in it - part (2) of the first list, and both parts of the 'Moreover' list on the same page - prints Dr; only this one prints LT. It is more than cosmetic because d-bar^{k+1}_LT is a different operator, constructed in Theorem 5.2.16 on p. 61, and the property asserted here is false of it: that theorem states d-bar^{k+1}_LT is O^{sm}_LT-linear, linear over the GL_2(Q_p)^0-smooth sections, and the two subsheaves O^{sm}_LT and O^{D_p^*-sm}_LT of O^{la}_LT are different, neither containing the other. Indeed if d-bar^{k+1}_LT were linear over the D_p^*-smooth sections its kernel would contain them, whereas Theorem 5.2.16(2) computes that kernel as the GL_2(Z_p)-locally algebraic subsheaf Sym^k V(k) tensor omega^{-k,sm}_LT . t^{n_1}, built from the GL_2-smooth sections. gaps.gap: The special case is settled only by importing the p-adic local Langlands correspondence
gaps.detail: Remark 1.1.12 says the result is slightly weaker when the local component pi_p is special, and Remarks 1.2.4, 5.5.15 and 7.3.11 say why: that the generalized eigenspace is an honest eigenspace, and the resulting description of the locally analytic vectors, are obtained there from Emerton's local-global compatibility and the known p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p), the very inputs the paper otherwise avoids. Remark 5.5.15 asks for a direct proof. A blueprint following this paper will have the supercuspidal and principal series cases self-contained and the special case only conditionally.

gaps.gap: The conceptual proof of Theorem 5.2.6 rests on a compatibility deferred to future work
gaps.detail: Footnote 3 on p. 58 states that the compatibility between Liu-Zhu's Higgs bundle and the Higgs field of the author's earlier paper 'can be checked on a toric chart' and that details will appear in future work. The theorem itself also has a complete proof by reduction to [Pan22, Theorem 4.2.7], so nothing in the paper depends on the gap, but the advertised improvement - a Kodaira-Spencer explanation of the differential equation that works for general Shimura varieties - does. Recorded as source issue E3.

gaps.gap: Two key coincidences are proved only by explicit calculation
gaps.detail: Remark 5.3.10 says of Corollary 5.3.9 - that GL_2(Q_p)-local analyticity and D_p^*-local analyticity agree on the infinite-level tower - that 'our proof relies on explicit calculations' and that an intrinsic proof would be conceptually satisfying; Dospinescu and Rodriguez Camargo obtained the same result independently. Similarly the proof of Corollary 5.3.13, that the two Cartan actions coincide, says the natural proof should use the moduli interpretations of the two towers. Both are places where a blueprint would want a better argument than the one available.

gaps.gap: The cokernel of the theta operator, and hence one graded piece of the answer, is not described
gaps.detail: Remark 4.4.17 asks for a more precise description of the summand A_{(-1,k+1)} of the n-invariants, which amounts to understanding the cokernel of theta_{k+1} on the canonical locus, that is the H^1 of a de Rham complex on a dagger space, equivalently a rigid cohomology of the Igusa curve. Coleman determined the primitive part; the general description is open.

gaps.gap: An alternative and simpler construction of the two differential operators is not carried out
gaps.detail: Remark 1.3.3 records that after the work was finished, Juan Esteban Rodriguez Camargo explained a more direct and conceptual construction of d_1 and d-bar_1 using B^+_dR modulo t^2, and that it would be very interesting to simplify the arguments of Section 6 with it. Since Section 6 is the longest and most technical part of the paper, a design job should consider whether to follow the published route or that one.

gaps.gap: What the method suggests beyond GL_2(Q_p) is programmatic
gaps.detail: Remark 1.1.3 says the method is expected to generalise and hopefully to shed light on the conjectural p-adic local Langlands correspondence for groups beyond GL_2(Q_p), and Remark 5.5.16 suggests more precisely that a p-adic correspondence may need a filtered equivariant derived category on the flag variety, since the representations constructed here do not see the Hodge filtration. These are directions, not theorems, and should not be planned as if they were.

The paper shares one counter between its named environments and its plain numbered paragraphs - 'Theorem 5.3.8' and '5.3.7 (Compare 5.2.7)' are consecutive labels - so the inventory had to catch both, and it also had to exclude citations into Papers I and II, which are printed in the same shape ('[Pan22, Theorem 3.1.2]' begins a line as convincingly as a real statement). Each of those 322 labels was then required to appear in the locator of some item, and all 322 do.

Two findings came out of that check rather than from reading. Theorem 5.3.8 introduces its coefficients as d_{i,j,k} and then writes the series with c_{i,j,k}; Theorem 5.3.17 constructs d-bar^{k+1}_Dr and then states property (1) for d-bar^{k+1}_LT. Both were confirmed on clips rendered at 300 and 320 dpi, so neither is an extraction artifact, and the second was checked to be more than cosmetic: Theorem 5.2.16 states that d-bar^{k+1}_LT is linear over the GL_2(Q_p)^0-smooth sections, and its kernel is the GL_2(Z_p)-locally algebraic subsheaf, so it is not linear over the D_p^*-smooth sections as the printed property (1) would have it.

Internal consistency of the main computations. Proposition 5.5.13 states the supersingular term with the cuspidal quaternionic forms A^c for every k, while Proposition 5.4.15 computes the kernel of d_{k+1} with the full A for k >= 1 and with A^c only for k = 0. These agree: A^1_{D,-chi} is non-zero only when n_1 = n_2, and for chi = (-k,0) with k >= 1 one has n_1 = -k and n_2 = 0, so A = A^c there; while for k = 0 the extra summand of ker d_1 contributes nothing to H^1 because H^1(P^1, O) = 0. The k = 0 degree-two graded piece of Theorem 5.5.4 keeps an extra M_0(K^p), which matches the extra summand of Corollary 5.4.16 together with H^1(Fl, Omega_Fl) = C, as the proof states.

The k = 1 exceptions line up. The introduction's 1.2.5 flags that for k = 1 there is only a map from H^1(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}) to W_0, with the discrepancy coming from H~^0; the precise statement is the exact sequence (3.4.1) whose kernel term is the colimit of the H^0 of the finite-level curves; the same discrepancy reappears as the Ext terms in Proposition 6.2.17, which vanish for k >= 2 because sl_2(Q_p) acts trivially on that colimit; and it is why 4.3.4 has to introduce the separate map I'_0 and why Theorem 1.2.10 states the k = 1 case only after restricting to a lambda_tau-isotypic part. Those four places were checked against each other.
